A number of steps are required to prepare documents to be converted, as Quicktagit uses specific word document structures to identify how to create the xml document. Additional steps can be taken while formatting Word documents to reduce work further along the production process.

item.title: Moodle Quiz Setup & Settings
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Updated Quiz Notification Considerations section with more info regarding quiz notification settings based on modality.

Quiz Settings Overview

OL Production requires the following quiz setting information to correctly set up quizzes in the Moodle environment.

Production will often use the settings from the previous version of the course if revised/new quiz setting information has not been provided.

Quiz Review Options

We can control what students see Immediately after the attempt (means within 2 minutes of the student clicking "submit all and finish") and Later, while the quiz is still open (means after 2 minutes).

We do have an additional After the quiz is closed option that can be used for online-paced courses. Since the After the quiz is closed option is data/time-specific it needs to be set by the Open Learning Faculty Member.

The attempt - Will show how the student responded to each question.

Whether correct - Displays whether the student's response to each question is correct or incorrect.

Marks - Reveals the marks awarded to the student and the grade for the quiz.

Specific feedback - Will show the feedback for the response. Each response to a question can have feedback for both correct and incorrect answers. This setting is needed for students to see any feedback comments manually added after the attempt by the Open Learning Faculty Member.

General feedback - Displays general feedback for the whole question as set when adding the question to the quiz. This is the most common type of feedback used in OL Moodle Quizzes.

Right answer - Reveals the correct answer to each question, whether the student answered correctly or not.

Overall feedback - Displays feedback for the entire quiz as set in the quiz settings.

Example Standard Assessed Quiz Settings

Standard Assessed Quiz

Name: Quiz 1 (20%)

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of Modules A, B, and C, complete Quiz 1. It is worth 20% of your grade. You will have 50 minutes and one attempt to complete this quiz. Be sure to be prepared and give yourself enough uninterrupted time to answer the questions all at one time.

Time limit: 50 minutes

Number of attempts: 1

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (If the OLFM wants to provide additional feedback or if included in quiz material)
  • General feedback (if included in quiz material)

Health-Science Assessed Quiz

There are stricter settings for Health-Science sector quizzes. This would include MDLB, RESP, NURS, HLTH courses. The students are NOT allowed to see the correct answer, however, for these courses it is typical that feedback is provided.

Name: Quiz 1 (20%)

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of Modules A, B, and C, complete Quiz 1. It is worth 20% of your grade. You will have 50 minutes and one attempt to complete this quiz. Be sure to be prepared and give yourself enough uninterrupted time to answer the questions all at one time.

Note: The mark you received for each question and general feedback for incorrect answers will be available immediately after you have submitted the quiz for 2 minutes only (feedback will have tan/yellow highlight). We recommend you review and look up the correct answers after the quiz and in preparation for the final exam. After 2 minutes, only the grade will be available.

Time limit: 50 minutes

Number of attempts: 1

Review options:

Immediately after the attempt (available for 2 minutes):

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (If the OLFM wants to provide additional feedback or if included in quiz material). Note: For Health-Science assessed quizzes, students are not able to see OLFM provided feedback after the attempt as students are only able to see the quiz Marks.
  • General feedback (if included in quiz material)

Later, while the quiz is still open (after 2 minutes)

  • Marks

Self-Test Quiz

Name: Module A Self-Test

Description/Instructions: Complete this self-test to check your understanding of key concepts. The self-tests are not graded, and they do not count towards your final grade.

Time limit: unlimited

Number of attempts: unlimited

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if provided)
  • General feedback (if provided)
  • Right answer
  • Overall feedback (if provided)

Practice Exam

Name: Practice Exam

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of all course materials, complete the practice exam under exam conditions; i.e., give yourself three hours and do not refer to your textbook or notes for help. Once complete, check your practice exam with the answers provided and consult your Open Learning Faculty Member if you need assistance or have any questions. Note: The Description/Instructions should also include any other exam-specific resources that may or may not be used.

Time limit: Should match Final Exam time limit

Number of attempts: unlimited

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if provided)
  • General feedback (if provided)
  • Right answer
  • Overall feedback (if provided)

Final Exam

Final Exam instructions are on the Final Exams Overview page.

Quiz Notifications

By default, Moodle does not send out email notifications to OLFMs for student quiz attempt submissions. Use the following steps to enable quiz notifications.

Note: Quiz notifications are enabled/disable on a per-quiz basis.

  1. Click on the quiz you would like to update.
  2. Select Permissions from the More dropdown.
  3. In the Filter search, enter "notification" which will bring up:
    Activity: Quiz
    Get a notification message when an attempt is submitted
  4. In the Roles with permissions column, click the + option, and select OLFM Online.
  5. Changes are save automatically.

To disable notification, complete the first four steps and click the Trash icon beside the OLFM Online option.

Quiz Notification Considerations

  • Online Paced Containers: We only need to have the Final Exam notifications turned on and not other individual quizzes.
  • Standard Web Containers: Notifications are required for any quizzes that need to be graded by the OLFM including the Final Exam. If the quizzes are auto-marked (e.g. only have basic multiple choice, T/F, etc.) then notifications are not required.
  • Assignments/Quiz Activities: Assignments that use the quiz activity should have notifications turned on.

item.title: Remote Work Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Remote Access Instructions:

VPN

Access for Windows 10 Remote

VPN is required for all Production websites and services such as JIRA, D4P, ProdWiki, MoodleProducer, O Drive, SVN, SFTP for CIS, etc.

O: Drive

  1. See https://www.tru.ca/its/employees/remoteaccess/batchfile.html
  2. You will need O drive for XML scripting and Oxygen CSS styles (if you didn’t download local copies)
  3. If you have issues, make sure you don’t already have an O:Drive taken up by something like a USB stick. You will need to run the BAT file every time you restart your computer/VPN, it asks for your password twice.

Office Suite

Microsoft Office is pre-installed on TRU computers, the following instructions are only needed if you are using a personal computer.

  1. Go to https://www.office.com/ and sign in as your TRU email and password.
  2. At the top right click on “Install Office > Office 365 apps”
  3. Follow installation instructions. When done you may need to sign in again.
  4. To turn off Microsoft Teams, ctrl+alt+del, more details, startup, disable.

Outlook Email Setup

Note:
The Outlook desktop app has not been working well remotely, and many people prefer to use the web app: https://exwebmail.tru.ca/owa/

  1. On Outlook’s first start it will ask for email accounts.
  2. Enter your TRU email, then select "Exchange 2013 or earlier", then enter your password.
  3. For other accounts, when entering your password click “more choices, Use a different account” then login using your TRU email and password.
  • Olproduction@tru.ca
  • fixmycourse@tru.ca
  • OLCISUPDATES@tru.ca
  • Olmedia@tru.ca

Communication Tools

Mattermost

Main area/method of on online communication for OL Production.

https://matter.tru.ca

Microsoft Teams

Web app (sign in with TRU Network ID)

Desktop app download

Skype

Not used. See Mattermost and Microsoft Teams

  1. Download Skype https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=724368
  2. Go to O:\Public Temporary Share\ITServices\SkypeCerts
  3. For both certificates, right click and install.
  4. Store Location > Local Machine
  5. Place all certificates in the following store > Trusted Root Certification Authorities Now open Skype and login with TRU email and password. You need the VPN connected to use skype.

SVN/Subversion

Subversion software should already be installed on TRU Production computers, if not use the link included in step 1.

  1. Download Tortoise SVN https://tortoisesvn.net/downloads.html
  2. Install as normal
  3. Checkout course files from http://phoenix.tru.ca:9880/production/trunk/Courses/
  4. On first connection, login with your SVN username and password (Not email).
  5. If you don’t have your login details, ask Sean for a password reset email.
  6. Or try http://phoenix.tru.ca:9890/ubersvn and “Forgotten Password”

Oxygen XML

TRU Production Computer:

Follow the Oxygen XML setup steps in the OL Production Wiki: https://olhub.tru.ca/prodwiki/index.php/XML

Personal Computer:

  1. Download Oxygen https://www.oxygenxml.com/xml_editor/download_oxygenxml_editor.html
  2. Request Academic 30-day trial from download page (when you click download button)
  3. TRU email took 20min to send key, if you’re impatient use a personal email Enter key when installing Options > Import Global Options >

O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\DEVELOPMENT_OXYGEN_XML\truolcourse_oxygen_global_settings.xml If you want to use Oxygen without being connected to VPN+O:Drive then copy the _OXYGEN_XML folder to your machine

  1. Then in Options > Preferences > Document Type Association > Locations, add your local folder location to the Additional frameworks directories. If you get a CSS error when opening a course xml, then you probably don’t have VPN+O:Drive or a local template setup correctly.

Production Links (VPN Required):

JIRA: https://olhub.tru.ca:8443/
D4P: https://olhub.tru.ca/d4p2/
Wiki: https://olhub.tru.ca/prodwiki/
Moodle Producer: https://olhub.tru.ca/moodle-producer/ U:moodle P:producer
XML Print: https://olhub.tru.ca/xmltoprint/ U:xml P:print
Mattermost: https://matter.tru.ca/
TRU Webhelpdesk: https://whd2.tru.ca/helpdesk/WebObjects/Helpdesk.woa/
Moodle: https://moodle.tru.ca/
Blackboard: https://blearn.tru.ca/
WordPress: http://trubox.ca/wp-login.php
SVN Checkout: http://phoenix.tru.ca:9880/production/trunk/Courses/
SVN Webapp: http://phoenix.tru.ca:9890/ubersvn

External Workflow Process

  1. Follow VPN instructions and connect your personal computer to TRU network
  2. Setup access to O: drive folders
  3. For Subversion course file access download and install Tortoise SVN (lastest version)
  4. Install Office 365 (free) if you don’t currently have it on your machine
  5. JIRA/D4P for updates
  6. Files committed to and from Subversion
  7. Word and Production scripting tools (Online and Desktop)
  8. Mattermost for team communication

Reminder:
Please remember to keep all your OL related user login details (Subversion, JIRA, etc.) saved in a secure area that you can access outside of work if needed.

item.title: Formatting Quiz in Word for Respondus
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Standard Formatting Overview

Respondus will import the following question types into Moodle:

  • Multiple choice
  • True and false
  • Essay
  • Fill in the blank
  • Multiple response questions

Quiz documents must follow Respondus standard formatting before it can be processed and imported. Images embedded in MS Word files will import automatically. The Quiz Formatting Video below gives an overview of the formatting process.

Multiple Choice

Each question must begin with a question number, followed by either a period "." or a parentheses ")".

The question wording must follow the question number. (Note: at least one space should be between the question number and the question wording.)f

Example:
1) Which planet in our solar system is the largest?
or
1. Which planet in our solar system is the largest?

Each answer must begin with a letter followed by a period "." or a parentheses ")".

Example: 
1) Which planet in our solar system is the largest?
a. Saturn
b. Jupiter
c. Neptune
d. Earth

Correct Answers

Place an asterisk (*) directly in front of the answer choice (NO space between the asterisk and the answer choice). If the answers are formatted with lists instead of normal text, you can bold all correct answer and use the AsteriskMoveMacros.bas file (O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\SOFTWARE\Respondus Macro) to quickly add the asterisk. Please review the Quiz Formatting Video for further instruction.

Use Macro to Add Asterisks

  • Open the MS Word file you want to convert, and make sure cursor is at top of document.
  • Press Alt+F11 to open the VBA editor, click File, Import File and select AsteriskMoveMacros.bas file.
  • Click Run, then Run Macro, and select AsteriskBoldText.
  • Click Okay, and the macro will add an asterisk to the start of the line where any bold text is found.
  • Highlight correct answers and remove bold text.
Example: 
1) Which planet in our solar system is the largest?
a. Saturn
*b. Jupiter
c. Neptune
d. Earth

True/False

The following examples are both valid ways to format a true and false question for importing purposes.

Example: 
1) Jupiter is the largest planet is our solar system?
*a) True
b) False
Example: 
1) Jupiter is the largest planet is our solar system?
*a. T
b. F

Note that the "True" (or "T") answer choice must be listed prior to the "False" (or "F") answer choice in order for Respondus to recognize it as a true and false question type.

Essay Questions

The first line of formatting must begin with "Type: E". This is followed by the question number, and the question wording.

Example: 
Type: E
1. List five strategies that help prevent drug resistance.

Provide the answer immediately after the question wording, beginning the answer with "a." or "a)" (without the quotes). Note: Essay type questions need to be manually marked in Moodle.

Example: 
Type: E
1. List five strategies that help prevent drug resistance.
a) Education of patients; doctors should only prescribe antibiotics when needed; doctors need to prescribe the correct antibiotic; patients need to take antibiotics correctly; health care workers need to practice infection control. (Reference: Objective #2)

Fill-in the-Blank

For Fill-in-the-Blank questions, we use the Cloze question type in Respondus.

In the Word document, you will format the question as an essay type, using Type: E. This is followed by the question number and question text. The underlined blank space will be formatted with the answers as the example below. Lastly, include a. none as this will allow Respondus to pick up the question as an Essay question with an answer.

{:SA:=answer1~=alternateanswer2}

SA stands for short answer. If a question has multiple possible answers you can use the ~ icon to separate them. In the example below, students may fill in the blank with either the full name of the society, or may use the acronym. If we use proper formatting, either would be marked correct.

Once you get the question into Respondus, you will need to change the question from Essay to Embedded Ans. (Cloze). Click Modify Item, and then click Embedded Ans. (Close) on the left menu. It will automatically create the correct question type. Save the changes, and you will see the question has been converted to a Fill-in-the-Blank.

Matching

The process of importing a "matching" question is similar to what is described above for importing multiple choice questions, but there are some key differences. The first line of formatting must begin with "Type: MT". This is followed by the "title" (which is optional), the question number, and the question wording.

Each answer (which consists of both parts of a correct match) must begin with a letter (a-t) followed by a period "." or a parentheses ")". The two parts of the match must be separated with an "=" symbol and there should not be any hard returns or blank lines within either parts of the answer.

Example: 
Type: MT
4) Match the correct name to the discovery or theory.
a. Michelson-Morely = Speed of light
b. Einstein = Theory of Relativity
c. Marconi = radio waves

Spaces before or after the "=" symbol are optional, but it is important that an answer only uses the = symbol for the purpose of separating the two parts of the match. If you plan to list correct answers for other questions at the bottom of the document, simply skip the number for all questions that are of the matching variety.

Multiple Response

The logic for importing questions that allowing multiple responses is similar to what is described above for importing multiple choice questions. (Multiple Response questions are, essentially, multiple choice questions in which more than one correct response can -- and generally should -- be selected by the student). The primary difference is that the first line of the formatting must begin with "Type: MR" (as an alternative, you can use "Type: MA" which stands for "Multiple Answers"). This is followed by the "Title" (which is optional), the question number, and the question wording. Each correct answer is designated with an asterisk.

Example: 
Type: MR
3) Which of the following individuals are credited with determining the exact speed of light?
a. Albert Einstein
*b. Albert Michelson
*c. Edward Williams Morley
d. Thomas Edison

To include a "title" or "feedback" with the Multiple Response question, follow the same formatting rules described above for multiple choice questions. For instance,

Example: 
Type: MR
3) Which of the following individuals are credited with determining the exact speed of light?
@ Albert Michelson and Edward Williams Morley collaborated on a series of experiments that eventually led to the exact determination of the speed of light.
a. Albert Einstein
*b. Albert Michelson
*c. Edward Williams Morley
d. Thomas Edison

General Feedback

Although there is an option to format General Feedback so it appears in Respondus, it frequently glitches. The best way to add General Feedback is to add it in to Respondus AFTER the questions have already been added to Respondus.

Keep the General Feedback in the master document, and add it in using the information in the images below.

Point Values

Point values can be set for each question or for a group of questions. Points are set by adding "Points:" followed by a space and the point value. The points value is used for the next question and all following questions until a new point value is set.

Example: 
Points: 2.5
1) Which planet in our solar system is the largest?
....
2) Which planet in our solar system is the smaller

Both questions 3 and 4 will be given a value of 2.5 points.

item.title: Moodle
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Overview

Moodle is the main Learning Management System (LMS) for both campus and Open Learning TRU students.

Moodle Dashboard

The Dashboard is a customisable page for providing users with details of their courses and other important details. In the centre is the Course overview block which allows students and teachers to easily track required activities and filter courses.

Improve Course Search with Custom HTML Block

Moodle current global search (beside user information in the top-left) often includes addition search results, which are not needed when we're trying to locate specific OL courses. To resolve this issue, we've created a custom HTML Block that can be added to the Moodle Dashboard page that provides accurate search results.

How to add the Custom HTML Search Block

  1. Login into Moodle at https://moodle.tru.ca/ using your TRU network credentials
  2. Select the Customize this page button in the top-right
  3. In the left-hand main Moodle navigation menu (press the three-line menu at the top-left to show/hide main menu) select the Add a block item
  4. Select HTML from the Add a Block pop-up and a new HTML block will be added to the right-hand side of your Moodle Dashboard.
  5. Press the gear icon on your new HTML block and select the Configure... option
  6. On the Configuration screen:
    • Leave the HTML block title blank
    • Toggle the HTML code view in the Content editor using the HTML button
    • Copy/paste the code below into the Content editor
    • Once complete, select Save changes, and you'll be redirected back to your Moodle Dashboard with your new Course Search block.
<p><strong>Course Search</strong></p>
<form class="card" id="SearchForm" action="https://moodle.tru.ca/course/search.php">
    <fieldset class="coursesearchbox invisiblefieldset">
        <div class="card-body">
            <div class="input-group">
                <input class="form-control" type="text" id="coursesearchbox" size="30" name="search" value="" aria-label="Search courses" style="margin-right:5px;">
                <span class="input-group-btn">
                    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit" onclick="searchStandard()"><i class="fa fa-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
</button> <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit" onclick="searchAdmin()"><i class="fa fa-cogs" aria-hidden="true"></i>
</button>
                </span>
            </div>
        </div>
    </fieldset>
</form>
    <script>
        form = document.getElementById("SearchForm");

        function searchStandard() {
            form.action = "https://moodle.tru.ca/course/search.php";
            form.submit();
        }

        function searchAdmin() {
            form.action = "https://moodle.tru.ca/course/management.php";
            form.submit();
        }
    </script>
<br><p><strong>Useful Production Containers</strong><br></p>
<a href="https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=5764" target="_blank">DEV_OL Content Samples</a><br>
<a href="https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=10218" target="_blank">TRU OL - OLFM Intro Videos</a>
<a href="https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=7149">DEV_OL E-Learning Support Technician Testing</a><br>
<br><p><strong>Administration</strong></p>
<a href="https://moodle.tru.ca/admin/user.php">Moodle Users</a>

Using the Custom HTML Search Block

The Course Search provides two search options/icons:

Standard Course Search/Magnifying Glass Icon - Selecting this button (or pressing Enter) will take you to the standard Moodle search with a list of course containers that match your query. Clicking on the course title will take you directly into the course.

Admin Course Search/Gears Icon - Selecting this button will take you to the Site Administration search with a compact list of course titles that match your search query. Selecting a course title will open up another section near the bottom of the page with additional course information and options, including a View button to access the course.

Basic Navigation and Course Structure

NOTE: This example will change in the upcoming Moodle 4 upgrade.

Below is an example of our current OL course structure in Moodle. We do have older and unique formats, but this standard layout we create from the Word documents provided to Production. A Moodle course often consists of:

  • Left-hand navigation bar automatically generated by Moodle
  • Course tabs running across the top, which are a combination of Moodle course settings and the structure we set up in the Word/XML documents
  • Under each of the course tabs there is a combination of Moodle Activities (e.g. Assignments, quizzes, etc.), Books which contain the bulk of the course material, and other File resource need to complete the course
  • Right-hand block area where Production has inserted built-in "widgets" to improve student navigation, progress tracking and other useful information.

item.title: Final Exams Overview (Archived)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
UNDER DEVELOPMENT

The Final Exams process mainly consistes of two workflow streams and communication channels:

  1. Final Exam setup durning course development using the PROD Jira project course Exam task and the olenvironmentdev@tru.ca shared inbox/email. .
  2. Exam support including corrections, accessibility requests, new exam versions, etc. using the OLCONTS Jira project and the olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca shared inbox/email.

  • If sent to personal email, forward request to the corresponding shared inbox in order for a JIRA task to be assigned.
  • When an exam submission is received, it should also be logged in D4P under the proper version of the course within Exams section.
  • All steps of exam process should be tracked through JIRA with Workflow changes and comments

As of March 2019 all exams should be submitted after being edited. D4P notes in editing should confirm. Check with course editor/lead if you are not sure.

Using Exams JIRA Project - Unclassified Content

Exam Material Storage

The curriculum development side of exams are stored on O:drive: O:\Open Learning Share\Final Exams and Keys\examrepo

New exam material should be saved in appropriate versioned folder under a directory called Working. Other sub-directories may be created within this level eg. Internal Review, Online.
  • If exam is requested to be pulled by Exams Department, put Word, PDF's into "Pulled" subfolder within versioned folder. Make sure to remove copies in exams folders.

Exam Forms Naming & Documenting

Naming

Paper Based Forms Only

  • If Exam is designated as no change and only has minor typos then no form letter change is required.
  • Form letter will be next available letter up to Letter Y (Letter Z is reserved for challenge exams). The form letter that is given on received files is MOST OFTEN not the letter that is assigned.
  • Include the version number in the file name to help make it unique.
  • Dates should only be attached to paper exams on upload, while working on and waiting for signoff there should be NO Date in file name.

Online/Paper - Set forms

  • Form letter will be next available letter up to Letter Y (Letter Z is reserved for challenge exams). In Moodle the Exam should be numbered on the front end. For example, Form A and Form B are being used. Setup in Moodle should have (1) and (2) showing to students with Form letters only provided in categories in back end.
  • Paper and Online exam form should match so it is clear that content is the same.

Online/Paper - Pool based

  • Online
  • Creating a Paper from online exam: Choice 1 - build out from Respondus. This requires that exam is setup properly in respondus. (note Randmization as RND Form Letter in D4P and on form header) OR Choice 2 - export a randomized attempt. This produces a PDF that will need adjusting (leave as PDF). Note: Print formatting does not need to be exact if just creating a PDF version of online exam.

Exam Documentation

  1. JIRA:
    • For courses that are part of typical curriculum development cycle (New/Major/Maintenance/Amendment), exam task should have a record that is linked to production course task. **This includes courses with no exam or change in exam.
    • Stand alone exam material will not have a link to production task.
    • Classification of Exam task will reflect either D4P2 (curriculum development) OR whatever is appropriate for exam.
  2. D4P2: will maintain the accuracy of the D4P information & JIRA

Material Processing

Overall Process

Starting JAN 2020, exam material process and production material process has been integrated.

Course material and the relevant exam material are more integrated as the result of online assessments. The following image shows general workflow for curriculum development work.

Data Tracking and Formatting are being done separately.

  • The Exams Liaison Officer is tracking all exam related material and doing formatting of midterms/exams.
  • The E-Learning Support Technicians are tracking and formatting all other course documentation.
    At the internal review stage the two processes combine.
    The E-Learning Support Technician who is doing an internal review of course material should also be reviewing all exam material (paper and online) at the same time. Each Internal Review is tracked separately in JIRA so two tasks are generated. The ELO will need to assign the Internal Review sub-task to EST. ELO keeps the main task on their list. The Internal Review from Exams goes back to Exams Liaison Officer position.

Integration between the two workflows is being accomplished by a JIRA task coming from Production Project called Exam Status (sub-task).

  1. EST will assign this production sub-task to ELO when they start of formatting course material. This lets the ELO know that course formatting is beginning and allows ELO to inform EST about type of exam material to come - paper only; paper & practice PDF; paper, practice PDF & Online versions. The ELO should respond back (assign back to EST) as soon as possible to allow correct structures to be built.
  2. EST will assign same sub-task back to ELO when the course material is ready for internal review, the EST doing Internal Review should be listed on sub-task. ELO will send back with confirmation that exam material is ready for internal review. ELO will then assign their JIRA Exam project IR sub-task to designated person.
  3. EST will assign task back when course is about to go to External Review. ELO will provide any passwords required for online material back to EST using same task.
    1. The External review can either be separate or together depending on what type of development cycle work as follows:
      1. Maintenance: Course Material to Naomi, online exam to Naomi first, paper exam to OLFM, once online material looked at by Naomi then OLFM put into container to look over. EST will have to let ELO know when online material can be sent to OLFM (basically at signoff)
      2. Major: Course Material to ID, online and paper to ID.
      3. New: Course Material to ID, online and paper to ID.

Process for Non-regular Final Assessment material

With advent of COVID-19 there has been a push to get more final assessments online. Courses have either had a proctorU exam added or an alternate assessment added to allow students to complete a course. These updates to courses are completely independent to course updates. This material has a different workflow process.

  1. In JIRA, Special Online Assessments are classified as "Online Exam" - green cloud with up arrow symbol
    1. Components to add: "COVID-19", Faculty course belongs to and either "Alt Assessment" or "ProctorU"
    2. Summary should clearly state Course Code/master number - whether Alt Assessment or Final Exam in ProctorU -if there is a relevant Form letter it should be added
    3. JIRA workflow is Queue, In Progress, Internal Review, External Review/Sign off, Waiting for Upload/, Uploaded

Note: Unlike regular workflow the main JIRA tasks gets moved between team members AND Internal Review AND External Review both have changes done by person reviewing. Waiting for Upload to Uploaded needs to be coordinated with either gap in ProctorU exams or with Exams group.

Exam Status Requests

Production E-Learning Support Technicians will be assigning an Exam Status sub-task from production process

  • Response should be sent back as soon as possible as it indicates start of formatting process
  • If require a response back for inserting material - please indicate
  • Responses back will come when production material is ready for internal review and should be dealt with right away

Exam File Requests

Final exam requests will come from Instructional Designers and Curriculum Services.

  • All exam requests should be sent to csexams@tru.ca, where a JIRA task will be assigned.
  • Check D4P for most current version, cross check against master spread sheet provided by Tod until confirmed all data records up to date.

Special Need Exams

Special Need Exam requests will come from the Exams Supervisor. The request will specify the special accommodation needed for the final exam (i.e., extended time, split into two sittings, enlarged font, etc.)
When modifications are complete, a final review will need to be made. Sometimes there are "suggested times" listed throughout the exam that will no longer be applicable, so a final review is crucial.
Once satisfied with the modification, print out the exam(s) and deliver to the Exams Supervisor.

Challenge Exams

Challenge exam requests will come from the PLAR Department. They will go through the same process as a final exam, except they will always be given the form letter "Z". They are also uploaded as a pdf file to the Printshop Folder.

Hello #####,

Currently, the winter university hours are 8:30am-4:30pm and will change to 8am-4pm in the Summer (May to August). To better align with the general university hours and the various departments/people we work with, and still provide some flexibility in our work schedule, we would like to have a standard Production team start time between 7:30 and 9am with corresponding end time of between 3-5pm depending on if you take a 30 minute or 1 hour lunch. This will help improve communication efficiency amongst Production Team members and between Production and other areas within TRU. As always, there is some flexibility and we just need to have discussions beforehand so we can adjust accordingly.

By the end of the week, can you please send me (cc Carolyn) your preferred start time, and work hours, so we have it on file?

If changes to your work schedule are needed (e.g., start time, vacation, sick, etc.), please send the communication as soon as possible by email to myself (cc Carolyn). Our work environment allows for additional flexibility and unforeseen circumstances come up, we just need to have those discussions/communications in advance whenever possible. Please don't hesitate to let me know if you have any questions. Thank you!

Moodle doesn't display the current version unless you have Moodle site administrator privileges, but version information can be pulled from a course backup file using the following steps.

  • Create a backup of a recent course you've worked on
  • Download the .mbz backup file to your desktop
  • Right-click on the file, got to 7-Zip and select open archive
  • Double-click the file in the 7-Zip application to see a list of included XML files
  • Extract/drag and drop the moodle_backup.xml file to your desktop and open with OxygenXML
  • Locate the <moodle_release> tag which contains the version of Moodle used to create the backup. E.g. <moodle_release>4.0.3+ (Build: 20220909)</moodle_release>

item.title: Accessible Readings
item.dc:creator: cteare
item.content:encoded:
Many accessibility requests come with requirement that material be able to be read by a screen reader. There are two types of screen readers.

  1. Visual Assistance type - this type of software is used by someone who may need enhancement of the material as they may not be able to process in standard format. For example, they may be using software to change appearance of material (contrast, size) or to have it be read out loud to them. TRU has a site license to Read&Write which would be this type of software. Some of our common software (Office, Adobe Acrobat) also have their own tools to support this type of need. There is a visual interface for this type of software. This is the most common type of software that is used.
  2. Visual Replacement type - this type of software is used by someone who is just using auditory directions to navigate their whole computing environment. Examples of this type of software are JAWS (paid commercial) or NVIDIA (open source). There is no visual interface for this type of software, only keyboard commands making it difficult to test against.

Evaluating Reading Format

Readings must be in a structured screen readable format.

A word document with proper headings would be in correct format although you may need to make adjustments to add alt-text to images.

PDF's could already be in correct format but you do need to check by either just looking at or trying to select individual words or turning on Read out Loud feature in Adobe. Check through whole document as sometimes hit or miss.

If PDF is not in a readable format:

  1. Try and find same source in digital format. Many journals are now fully online and it may be possible to find a version online that we can direct a student to OR when we converted web material we did not do it in best way possible eg. web pages saved as images instead of documents.
  2. Convert the reading into readable format - see process below.

If PDF is in a readable format, it is still best to run through Acrobat accessibility wizard to check if generally okay.

Converting a Scanned Reading

Presuming above steps failed it will be necessary to try and convert through Acrobat. The steps involved are typically OCR, tagging and reading order.

Method 1: Adobe Acrobat all the way

  1. Save a copy of your source PDF.
  2. Open in Acrobat, go to Accessibility Wizard tool and run document through.
  3. Look at results. If output showing a mess - words split, tables not processed and document long then stop and switch to next method.
  4. If results okay, then use tools to make sure things are tagged correctly in terms of structure and reading order.

Method 2: Adobe plus notepad++, HTML cleaner, Oxygen and Word

Although more pieces of software this method can be more efficient that trying just using ADOBE tools alone.

  1. Open a copy of your source PDF.
  2. Go to OCR option and convert to readable text.
  3. Export result to HTML file.
  4. Clean HTML via online software. https://html-cleaner.com/ seems pretty good
    • Open HTML in word as will need to copy/paste all text into cleaner window.
    • Set options to clean semi-agressively - you want basic HTML as it is easier to re-add formatting than to change.

item.title: How to Edit Moodle Email Notifications
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS***

Quiz Notifications

Changing the email wording for Moodle quiz notifications involves editing the language strings within Moodle. This is typically done by an administrator.

https://docs.moodle.org/405/en/Quiz_submission_email_notification

  1. Understand Moodle's Language System: Moodle uses language packs to manage all text displayed on the site, including email notifications. Each piece of text is a "language string" identified by a unique name.1
  2. Identify the Relevant Strings:
    • For quiz notifications, the key strings are usually found in the quiz.php language file, which is part of the "mod" group.2
    • The common strings you'll want to modify are:
      • emailconfirmsubject: The subject of the confirmation email sent to students after they submit a quiz.3
      • emailconfirmbody: The body of the confirmation email sent to students.
      • emailnotifysubject: The subject of the notification email sent to teachers when a student submits a quiz.
      • emailnotifybody: The body of the notification email sent to teachers.
  3. Access Language Customization:
    • Log in to Moodle as an administrator.
    • Navigate to Site administration > Language > Language customization.
    • Select the language pack you want to modify (e.g., "English (en)").
    • Click "Open language pack for editing."
  4. Find and Edit the Strings:
    • In the "Filter strings" section, you can use the "Only strings containing" field to search for keywords from the existing email text or the string names (e.g., "emailconfirmbody").
    • Alternatively, you can select "mod" from the "Components" dropdown and then look for "quiz" to narrow down the search.
    • Once you find the string you want to change, you'll see its current definition. You can then enter your new wording in the "Local customization" field.
  5. Use Available Placeholders (Variables):Moodle email templates often use placeholders (variables) like {$a->username}, {$a->quizname}, {$a->coursename}, {$a->submissiontime}, {$a->quizurl}, {$a->studentname}, etc. These variables are automatically replaced with specific information when the email is sent. Make sure to include these in your custom wording where appropriate to provide relevant details. The Moodle Docs article on "Quiz submission email notification" (which was one of the search results) provides a comprehensive list of available $a parameters.
  6. Save Changes:
    • After making your changes, click "Save changes to language pack."
    • Moodle will then compile the new language pack, and your changes will be applied.

Important Considerations:

  • Impact on Upgrades: Modifying core language strings directly might be overwritten during Moodle upgrades. While Moodle's language customization feature is designed to handle this gracefully by keeping your "local customizations" separate, it's always good to be aware.
  • Backups: Before making any significant changes, it's a good practice to back up your Moodle site.
  • Testing: Always test your changes thoroughly after modifying the email wording to ensure they appear as intended and that all necessary information is included.
  • Theme Overrides (Advanced): For more extensive changes to the email layout or if you want to include custom HTML/CSS, you might need to explore overriding Moodle's email templates within your Moodle theme. This is a more advanced topic and typically involves working with Mustache templates.
  • Default Settings for Notifications: As an administrator, you can also set the defaults for quiz submission notifications (e.g., enabling/disabling email or pop-up notifications) under Site administration > Plugins > Message outputs > Default message outputs.4 You can also control user permissions related to sending and receiving quiz notifications in Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles (e.g., mod/quiz:emailnotifysubmission for teachers and mod/quiz:emailconfirmsubmission for students).5

Assignment Notifications

item.title: Adding New Exam to Active Course/Session
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS***

Initial Final Exam Setup

D4P

  • Add new exam records to D4P (online, paper, etc.)

Online Final Exam: Course Development Shell

In the DEV Moodle shell:

  • Ensure hidden tabs are set to invisible
  • Create OBSOLETE tab and move current final exam activity into new tab
  • In the Question bank section create a "OBSOLETE - DO NOT USE" category and move all old final exam categories, questions into new "OBSOLETE" category. It's also recommended to add "OBSOLETE_" to all sub-categories to avoid accidental usage in the future (e.g. OBSOLETE_PSYC1111_FE_SW4)
  • Create new final exam activity using standard setup practices

Paper Final Exam: Subversion/O: Drive

Create new paper form and answer key following standard formatting practices

Final Exam Review Process

Similar to the standard course development process, new final exam material should go through the Internal, QA and External review stages.

  • Once the initial setup is complete, ask the Production Supervisor where to send the final exam Internal Review task.
  • Complete, both the Internal Review and QA Review steps and send out for External Review

LIVE Final Exam Setup

Online Final Exam: LIVE Course Shells

In all impacted LIVE shells:

  • Ensure hidden tabs are set to invisible
  • In the Question bank section create a "OBSOLETE - DO NOT USE" category and move all old final exam categories, questions into new "OBSOLETE" category. It's also recommended to add "OBSOLETE_" to all sub-categories to avoid accidental usage in the future (e.g. OBSOLETE_PSYC1111_FE_SW4)
  • From DEV, export the new final exam quiz bank categories in XML format
  • Import the new Final Exam quiz bank categories into LIVE
  • Review/adjust the question bank category setup as if needed
  • In the Final Exam tab, create new Final Exam quiz activity and hide immediately, so students don't accidentally access the activity
  • Setup final exam activity to match DEV
  • Once the final activity is complete and ready for students:
    • Create OBSOLETE tab and move current final exam activity into new tab
    • Update the on the new final exam activity to "Show" so student can access
  • Review/update gradebook for any adjustments needed (e.g. percentage calculation)

Paper Final Exam: Subversion/O: Drive

  • Complete the final exam archive and upload process for new paper forms

D4P

  • Update D4P exam records

item.title: TRU Network Drive (O:)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Network Drive access is needed for many Production tools and other shared files and directories. Use the following instructions to set up a .bat file on your desktop.

1. From your Windows start menu, open Notepad 2. Copy the following text into Notepad  

net use H: /delete
net use O: /delete
net use H: \\tru_vfiler1.tru.univ\home\JSMITH * /user:TRU\JSMITH
net use O: \\tru-univ-dc1.tru.univ\Shared * /user:TRU\JSMITH
pause

3. Replace the three JSMITH names with your username
4. Save this file as “TRUNetworkDrives.bat” to your desktop

You will need to run the BAT file every time you restart your computer/VPN.

If you have issues, make sure you don’t already have an O:Drive taken up by something like a USB stick.

Original instruction are from: https://www.tru.ca/its/employees/remoteaccess/MapNetworkDrives.html > Mapping network drives on Windows.

item.title: Microsoft Word
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft Word is used extensively in the course development process, and it also used to create print courses and other print materials. Before starting any course print formatting, it is recommended that you add the Templates button to the Word interface and learn how to attach the OL styles to a document. Additional formatting standards and information is covered in the Print Course Development & Print Material Formatting section.

Add Templates button to Quick Access toolbar (Office 365):

  • Goto File/Options/Quick Access toolbar
  • Select All Commands from the dropdown, locate Templates in the list, click Add and then OK

You should now see a Templates button at the top of your Word document:

Attach OL Styles To Document

  • Save the OL_STYLES_DEC2014.dotx template file to your desktop
  • Click on the Templates button and then Document Templates
  • Click the Attach button, select the OL_STYLES_DEC2014.dotx file and press Open
  • Check the "Automatically update document styles" option and press OK
  • OL styles should now be visible in the Style panel

Word Macros

Macros are powerful tools that automate repetitive tasks in Word. Below are instructions on how to enable/add macros in Work and list of macros that may be helpful for certain workflows and steps in the Production process.

Step 1: Enable the Developer Tab

The Developer tab contains all the tools you need to work with macros. Here's how to turn it on:

  • Open Microsoft Word and click File in the top-left corner
  • Click Options at the bottom of the menu
  • In the Word Options window, click Customize Ribbon on the left side
  • On the right side, you'll see a list of Main Tabs. Check the box next to Developer
  • Click OK

Step 2: Understand Where to Save Your Macros

For a macro to work in any document, you need to save it in the right place:

  • Normal.dotm - This is Word's global template. Macros saved here are available in every document you open
  • This Document - Macros saved here only work in that specific document

For macros you want to use anywhere, always choose Normal.dotm.

Step 3: Adding Macros

  • Click the Developer tab
  • Click Visual Basic (or press Alt + F11)
  • Find Normal and expand it
  • Right-click on Modules and select Insert > Module
  • A new code window will appear - this is where you copy/paste your macro
  • Paste your VBA macro code here
  • Click File > Save Normal (or press Ctrl + S)
  • Close the Visual Basic Editor

Step 4: Run Your Macro

There are several ways to run your saved macros:

Method 1: From the Developer Tab
  1. Click the Developer tab
  2. Click Macros
  3. Select your macro from the list
  4. Click Run
Method 2: Create a Keyboard Short Cut
  1. Click the Developer tab
  2. Click Macros
  3. Select your macro
  4. Click Options
  5. Assign a keyboard shortcut (like Ctrl + Shift + F)
  6. Click OK
Method 3: Add to the Ribbon or Quick Access Toolbar
  1. Right-click on the ribbon and select Customize the Ribbon
  2. Under "Choose commands from," select Macros
  3. Find your macro in the list
  4. Create a new group on the ribbon or add it to the Quick Access Toolbar
  5. Click Add to move your macro there
  6. Click OK

Helpful for print on demand or other documents where the web URLs need to be fully displayed beside the text. Note: Email links may may need minor formatting adjustments. You can search for "mailto"

Sub A_ExtractAndDisplayURLs()
    Dim hl As Hyperlink
    Dim url As String
    Dim i As Long
    
    ' Loop backwards through hyperlinks to avoid indexing issues when links are removed
    For i = ActiveDocument.Hyperlinks.Count To 1 Step -1
        Set hl = ActiveDocument.Hyperlinks(i)
        
        ' 1. Extract the full URL
        url = hl.Address
        
        ' Handle cases where the link might be to a sub-address (like a bookmark)
        If hl.SubAddress <> "" Then
            url = url & "#" & hl.SubAddress
        End If
        
        ' 2. Display the URL in parentheses after the linked text
        hl.Range.InsertAfter " (" & url & ")"
        
        ' 3. Remove the active link from the text
        hl.Delete
    Next i
    
    MsgBox "Finished extracting URLs!", vbInformation
End Sub

Helpful when you don't need separate sections in a larger document.

Sub A_ConvertSectionToPageBreaks()
    Dim i As Long
    Dim rng As Range

    ' Loop through all sections except the last one
    ' (The last section mark is the end of the document)
    For i = ActiveDocument.Sections.Count - 1 To 1 Step -1
        Set rng = ActiveDocument.Sections(i).Range
        
        ' Collapse range to the end of the section (where the break is)
        rng.Collapse Direction:=wdCollapseEnd
        rng.MoveEnd Unit:=wdCharacter, Count:=-1
        
        ' Check if the break is a section break and not just the end of the doc
        ' Then replace it with a standard page break
        rng.Select
        Selection.InsertBreak Type:=wdPageBreak
        
        ' Delete the now redundant section break
        ActiveDocument.Sections(i + 1).Range.Characters(1).Previous.Delete
    Next i
    
    MsgBox "All section breaks converted to page breaks!", vbInformation
End Sub

Helpful to remove empty/extra paragraph marks in text, for example XML to Print tables. 

Sub A_DeleteEmptyParagraphMarks()
    '
    ' DeleteEmptyParagraphMarks Macro
    ' Removes paragraph marks that have no text or content before them in the selection
    ' Works with regular text and table cells
    '
    
    Dim rng As Range
    Dim para As Paragraph
    Dim tblCell As cell
    Dim tbl As Table
    Dim paraText As String
    Dim deletedCount As Long
    Dim i As Long
    
    deletedCount = 0
    
    ' Check if there's a selection
    If Selection.Type = wdSelectionIP Then
        MsgBox "Please select the text where you want to remove empty paragraph marks.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Store the selection range
    Set rng = Selection.Range
    
    ' Turn off screen updating for better performance
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    
    ' Process tables in the selection
    For Each tbl In rng.Tables
        For Each tblCell In tbl.Range.Cells
            ' Process paragraphs in this cell
            For i = tblCell.Range.Paragraphs.Count To 1 Step -1
                Set para = tblCell.Range.Paragraphs(i)
                
                ' Get the text without the paragraph mark
                paraText = para.Range.Text
                paraText = Left(paraText, Len(paraText) - 1) ' Remove paragraph mark from end
                
                ' Check if paragraph is empty (only whitespace or nothing)
                If Len(Trim(paraText)) = 0 Then
                    ' Delete the paragraph mark
                    para.Range.Delete
                    deletedCount = deletedCount + 1
                End If
            Next i
        Next tblCell
    Next tbl
    
    ' Process regular paragraphs (outside tables)
    ' Work backwards to avoid index issues when deleting
    For i = rng.Paragraphs.Count To 1 Step -1
        On Error Resume Next
        Set para = rng.Paragraphs(i)
        On Error GoTo 0
        
        If Not para Is Nothing Then
            ' Skip if this paragraph is in a table (already processed)
            If para.Range.Tables.Count = 0 Then
                ' Get the text without the paragraph mark
                paraText = para.Range.Text
                paraText = Left(paraText, Len(paraText) - 1) ' Remove paragraph mark from end
                
                ' Check if paragraph is empty (only whitespace or nothing)
                If Len(Trim(paraText)) = 0 Then
                    ' Delete the paragraph mark
                    para.Range.Delete
                    deletedCount = deletedCount + 1
                End If
            End If
        End If
    Next i
    
    ' Turn screen updating back on
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    
    ' Show results
    If deletedCount > 0 Then
        MsgBox "Deleted " & deletedCount & " empty paragraph mark(s).", vbInformation
    Else
        MsgBox "No empty paragraph marks found in the selection.", vbInformation
    End If
    
End Sub

Macro will convert all hypertext links to blue. Helpful for OLMFG and other documents where the links need to be highlighted.

Sub A_ChangeHyperlinksToBlue()
    '
    ' ChangeHyperlinksToBlue Macro
    ' Changes all hyperlinked text in the document to blue color
    ' Skips hyperlinks in the Table of Contents
    '
    
    Dim hyperlink As hyperlink
    Dim doc As Document
    Dim tocField As Field
    Dim tocRange As Range
    Dim skipLink As Boolean
    Dim changedCount As Integer
    
    ' Set reference to active document
    Set doc = ActiveDocument
    
    ' Check if there are any hyperlinks in the document
    If doc.Hyperlinks.Count = 0 Then
        MsgBox "No hyperlinks found in this document.", vbInformation, "No Hyperlinks"
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    changedCount = 0
    
    ' Loop through all hyperlinks in the document
    For Each hyperlink In doc.Hyperlinks
        skipLink = False
        
        ' Check if this hyperlink is inside a TOC field
        For Each tocField In doc.Fields
            If tocField.Type = wdFieldTOC Then
                Set tocRange = tocField.Result
                ' Check if hyperlink is within the TOC range
                If hyperlink.Range.Start >= tocRange.Start And _
                   hyperlink.Range.End <= tocRange.End Then
                    skipLink = True
                    Exit For
                End If
            End If
        Next tocField
        
        ' Change the font color to blue if not in TOC
        If Not skipLink Then
            hyperlink.Range.Font.Color = RGB(0, 0, 255)
            changedCount = changedCount + 1
        End If
    Next hyperlink
    
    ' Notify user of completion
    If changedCount > 0 Then
        MsgBox changedCount & " hyperlink(s) changed to blue. " & _
               (doc.Hyperlinks.Count - changedCount) & " TOC hyperlink(s) skipped.", _
               vbInformation, "Complete"
    Else
        MsgBox "All hyperlinks are in the Table of Contents. No changes made.", _
               vbInformation, "Complete"
    End If
    
End Sub

item.title: Microsoft Outlook
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added information regarding "New" Outlook version and shared inboxes.

Outlook is used by the Production team to communicate with various departments with TRU using shared inboxes so that various people on the team can send and receive information from a central location.

Adding Shared Inboxes (e.g. olenvironmentdev@tru.ca)

Note: Currently the "New" version of Outlook does not support shared inboxes and the "Try the new Outlook" toggle in the top-right needs to be switched to Off.

Here are the instructions for the adding addition emails to desktop Outlook.

  • In Outlook, click the File menu options and then click the Add Account near the top that will activate a pop-up window. In the pop-up:
  • Enter the email address you would like to add from the list below
  • Below the email field, click the Advanced options and enable the Let me set up my account manually option
  • Click the Connect button
  • On the Advance setup page, select Exchange and you will be asked to enter login information
  • Select the Sign in with another account option, use your personal TRU credentials and complete the two-factor authentication process
  • On the Exchange Account Settings, you can leave as is and click the Next button
  • You'll receive an Account successfully added message and you'll need to restart to activate the new inbox.

Shared Inbox List

Complete the steps above to add the following Shared Inboxes

  • olenvironmentdev@tru.ca
  • olcontentsupport@tru.ca
  • olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca
  • fixmycourse@tru.ca
  • olcisupdates@tru.ca

Viewing Shared Inboxes

The shared inboxes (e.g. olproduction@tru.ca) function a bit differently due to the Jira login process. Jira is watch for new emails in the shared Inbox folder for each account and once it has processed the email it moves them to a Jira Logged folder under the Cabinet folder (e.g. Cabinet/OLprod JIRA_logged):

Sending From Shared Email Address

Note: Communications to other areas in TRU should be sent from the corresponding shared inbox, (e.g. olproduction@tru.ca) and not from personal email accounts.

When replying to a shared inbox message, Outlook will automatically adjust the "From" address to match the shared inbox, but if you are creating a new email, click the "From" drop-down button to select the correct email address or use the "Other Email Address..." option to add the required email.

Email Filters for Jira Communications

Comments and Updates Filter

This filter will sort out incoming Jira email notifications for any updates and comments for tasks that are assigned to you into a separate folder that you can add to your Favourites section in your Outlook application for quick at-a-glance.

  1. In Outlook, right-click on your Inbox folder, New folder and create a Jira folder with a nested Comments folder
  2. Click on File and select the Manage Rules & Alerts button
  3. In the pop-up window: Click New Rule... and select the Apply rule on messages I receive and click the Next button
  4. Enable the "with specific words in the body" and add "commented on" and "updated an issue"
  5. Enable the "with specific words in the subject" and add "[JIRA]"
  6. Click the Next button
  7. Enable the move it to the "specified folder" option and select the Jira/Comments folder created in the first step
  8. Click Next twice (skipping exceptions)
  9. Give your rule a name (e.g. [JIRA] Comments and Updates) and click Finish
  10. Locate the "Comments" folder in your list, right-click and select Add to Favourites to bring it to the top of your Outlook lists

Assigned to Me Filter

This filter will sort out incoming Jira email notifications any tasks that are assigned to you into a separate folder that you can add to your Favourites section in your Outlook application for quick at-a-glance.

  1. In Outlook, right-click on your Inbox folder, New folder and create a Jira folder with a nested Assigned - Me folder
  2. Click on File and select the Manage Rules & Alerts button
  3. In the pop-up window: Click New Rule... and select the Apply rule on messages I receive and click the Next button
  4. Enable the "with specific words in the body" and add "assigned an issue to Firstname Lastname"
  5. Enable the "with specific words in the subject" and add "[JIRA]"
  6. Click the Next button
  7. Enable the move it to the "specified folder" option and select the Assigned - Me folder created in the first step
  8. Click Next twice (skipping exceptions)
  9. Give your rule a name (e.g. [JIRA] Assigned - Me) and click Finish
  10. Locate the "Assigned - Me" folder in your list, right-click and select Add to Favourites to bring it to the top of your Outlook lists

Web Access

All personal and shared inboxes can be accessed from the web as well: TRU Webmail

item.title: Subversion/TortoiseSVN
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added link with instructions to move Desktop out of OneDrive.
- Added updated Subversion URL and Subversion password reset information.

All course files for OL Production are stored using file versioning software on an independent server (not part of standard IT drives) called Subversion and, we use an application called Tortoise SVN to download/upload files to our Subversion server.

Install and Connect Tortoise SVN

If your computer doesn't have Tortoise SVN installed (right-click on your desktop and see if you have "SVN Checkout..." and "TortioseSVN" options in the menu) use the following instructions. (Note: If you're on Windows 11, see information regarding right-click menu further down)

  1. Download the current 64-bit version of the Tortoise SVN application from https://tortoisesvn.net/downloads.html
  2. Complete the installation process, no changes required in the installation setup.
  3. Right-click on your desktop and select the "TortioseSNV>Repo Browser" option
  4. In the URL field, enter https://olsvnapp01olpd.tru.ca/svn/production/trunk/Courses/ and click OK
  5. On your first connection, login with your SVN username and password. This login is separate from your TRU network login and will be provided to you. If you don’t have your login details, ask Sean for a password reset email.
  6. You should now see a current listing of all our courses currently saved in Subversion

Once you have Subversion up and running, you can find out more information about how to use Subversion in the Course Communication, Documentation and File Management section.

Tortoise SVN Fixes for Common Issues

Moving Desktop Out of OneDrive

Windows 11 "helpfully" includes your Desktop in OneDrive, but that causes conflicts with Tortoise SVN (missing icons) and also automatically syncs any course files checked out from Subversion to the cloud, which is unnecessary. Use the following solution to quickly move your Desktop out of OneDrive: https://www.addictivetips.com/windows-tips/move-the-desktop-folder-out-of-onedrive-on-windows-10/

Windows 11 Right-Click Menu Fix

Windows 11 "helpfully" hides some additional right-click menu items, including Subversion under a Show more option item. Here are some instructions on how to open the full right-click menu by default on Windows 11.

Tortoise SVN Icons Missing (Windows 10 and 11)

Solutions from: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1057734/tortoisesvn-icons-not-showing-up-under-windows-7 and https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31964627/tortoisesvn-icons-overlay-not-showing-after-updating-to-windows-10

Windows can only show a limited number of Overlay Icons (15 total). Programs like One Drive, Adobe Creative Cloud, etc., will hijack a bunch of the 11 possible overlay icons, which will cause the Subversion icons to not be visible. To fix this issue:

  • From your Start Menu, open the Registry Editor
  • Copy/paste this location into the Registry Editor navigation bar:
HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\explorer\ShellIconOverlayIdentifiers
  • Locate the Tortoise SVN entries (e.g. Tortoise1Normal, Tortoise2Modified)
  • Right-click on each of the entries, and add additional spaces before the name so that they are indented one more space than the OneDrive entries (5 spaces total)
  • Hit F5 to refresh the entries and confirm that all the Tortoise SVN entries are at the top of the directory
  • Once registry changes are complete, restart computer and confirm that Subversion/Tortoise SVN folders icons are visible.

item.title: Oxygen XML Editor
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent changes: 
Added additional suggested shortcuts to the Add Oxygen Editor Keyboard Shortcuts section

Overview

Oxygen XML Editor is the main XML editing/authoring application used by Production in course development process. Once set up, Oxygen XML will allow you to structure course data, view/edit course content including text, images, and other media, use shortcut keys and more. Course XML documents are our master documents for OL courses, and the XML format allows use to be efficient and consistent with our course material.

Oxygen XML Initial Setup

Note: VPN and TRU Network drive (O: drive) connections are required to complete setup and style sheets to display XML content correctly.

Import Global Settings

  1. Open Oxygen XML Editor on your desktop
  2. In the top menu bar, select Options > Import Global Options
  3. In the file selection window, navigate to O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\DEVELOPMENT\_OXYGEN_XML and select the truolcourse_oxygen_global_settings.xml file and click Open in the bottom left-hand corner (Note: If you get pop-up message stating that "The file you are importing may not contain settings for all Oxygen options." click OK to proceed)
  4. Close Oxygen XML Editor and restart the application to apply the changes
  5. Open a course XML file to confirm it is displaying correctly

Install Graphic Entity Button

The Graphic Entity Button in Oxygen XML Editor allows use to quickly add the extra code needed to link resource files (Word documents, PDFs, images, etc.) directly in the XML. To install the Graphic Entity button:

  1. Close Oxygen XML Editor
  2. Locate the GraphicEntityButton folder in O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\DEVELOPMENT\_OXYGEN_XML i
  3. Copy/paste the whole GraphicEntityButton folder ino C:\Program Files\Oxygen XML Editor ##\plugins\
  4. Open Oxygen XML Editor and the new Graphic Entity button should be visible in the top toolbar.

Note: Instructions also on O:Drive (O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\DEVELOPMENT\_OXYGEN_XML)

Add Oxygen Editor Keyboard Shortcuts

Oxygen XML Editor keyboard shortcuts allow you to quickly apply formatting (e.g. bold, italics, etc.) and insert additional tag (e.g. headings, notebox, image, etc.) Keyboard shortcuts are created through the "Code Templates" section of the Oxygen XML Editor. You can add/edit/remove specific code templates by accessing this section at in the top toolbar under Options>Preferences>Editor>Templates>Code Templates. To install the OL Production default shortcuts:

  1. Copy the Code_templates_for_oxygen.zip file from O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\SOFTWARE\PRODUCTION SOFTWARE\Oxygen XML and Math Flow\ to your desktop and unzip the file.
  2. In Oxygen XML editor, locate "Code Templates" in under Options>Preference>Editor>Content Completion>Code Templates
  3. Click the “Import” button near the bottom and select the XML file you downloaded
  4. Once the import process is complete, review the Code Templates list to confirm the shortcut have been added. (Click the Shortcut column heading to sort, and you should see the various keyboard shortcuts available)
  5. Click "Apply," "OK," and restart Oxygen XML Editor

Current Keyboard Shortcuts

How to Create Your Own Shortcuts

  1. To create your own shortcut, start by going into the "Code Template" section and selecting "New"
  2. Enter a name you would like to refer to this shortcode as, a description of what the shortcode is, select "XML" for editor, and a shortcut key you would like to use
  3. Enter the content for the shortcut - the easiest way to do this if you are unsure of what tag to use, is to copy from one of the basic shortcuts above and reverse engineer the new tag. Note: You can also duplicate one of the current basic code templates and just edit everything from there rather than selecting new
  4. After you put in the associated tag, place ${selection} where you want the highlighted text to appear (or alternatively where you want your position to be once you use the shortcode if nothing is highlighted)

Additional Suggested Shortcuts

Shortcut Alternative

If you do not wish to use keyboard shortcuts, you can also select enter twice in oxygen to bring up a search area where you can access commonly used tags. Start typing to access a search of a specific tag

Apply Line Break Fix

Oxygen XML Editor automatically adds line breaks to files based on a line width setting. This can affect autolinks in Moodle, as the line breaks in the HTML will cause Moodle to ignore text we intended to auotlink to a resource. To avoid this, you can open Oxygen XML Editor and do the following:

  1. In the top toolbar, select Options>Preferences in the top toolbar, then go to Editor>Format on the left-hand side
  2. Check the "Use zero-indent, if detected" checkbox.
  3. Increase the "Line width" value to a very high number such “1000000”
  4. Click "Apply," then "OK" and restart Oxygen XML Editor

Note: This will only help future cases, and not fix existing XML files that already have line breaks within.

Install Dark (Dracula) Theme

The Dracula theme is available for Oxygen XML that can be combined with a custom CSS file for improved highlighting of tags and elements. To set up this theme, follow the steps below:

  1. Open an XML file in Oxygen XML
  2. In the Window menu, go to Configure Toolbars...
  3. Ensure that "Author Styles" is checked and click OK
  4. You will now have a Styles drop-down in the ribbon. Note: this may appear on a second row on the far-left side of your screen. In the menu, choose Dracula.
  5. In the top menu bar, click Options>Preferences
  6. In the Appearance section, choose the Graphite theme and click OK
  7. Restart Oxygen XML and enjoy the dark theme!

Here's what your Oxygen XML should look like after installing the Dracula dark theme:

Instructions for Offline Use/No TRU Network Access

If you want to use Oxygen without being connected to VPN+O:Drive then copy the _OXYGEN_XML folder to your machine. (Found in: O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\DEVELOPMENT\)

  1. Then in Options > Preferences > Document Type Association > Locations, add your local folder location to the Additional frameworks directories. If you get a CSS error when opening a course xml, then you probably don’t have VPN+O:Drive or a local template setup correctly.

item.title: JIRA
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
JIRA is a web-based workflow management tool. It was designed as a software development tool, but allows easy customization to any workflow requirements. This is a shared tool used by many sections within Open Learning, each has set up a program to meet their needs by creating Projects.

URL: https://truol.atlassian.net/

Important: We have migrated to Jira Cloud and the screenshots below may not reflect all aspects of the new interface, but they are similar in most cases.

Jira Dashboards

Jira Dashboards allow you to view and organize Production tasks in various ways.

A basic EST Dashboard template has been created to get started, and then you can adjust your Dashboard to what works best for you.

EST Dashboard Setup

  1. Login in to JIRA
  2. In the top menu, click the Dashboards menu and select View all dashboards
  3. In the Search field, enter "EST Dashboard" and the results will update automatically
  4. Locate the "Production - EST Dashboard" row and in the corresponding More actions column, click the 3-dot menu and select Copy Dashboard
  5. Enter a name for your new JIRA Dashboard (e.g. My Dashboard), skip the other field/sections and click the Save at the bottom of the form
  6. Your page will refresh and you'll be automatically redirected to your new EST Dashboard
  7. In the top-right click on the star beside the link icon and Refresh button to add it to your favourites, you should now see your new dashboard in the Dashboards menu item at the top of the page
  8. Your JIRA Dashboard can now be access by using the Dashboard drop-down menu

EST Dashboard Overview

Not Started (Red) - These are tasks that have been assigned to you, but the Jira status has not been updated (e.g. QUEUE)

In Progress (Green) - These are tasks that you have started work on, and you have updated the JirA a stat us to reflect that these are

Unclassified (Blue) - These are new tasks that have been automatically created from emails sent to olenvironmentdev@tru.ca

Requires Updates (Orange) - These are task that haven't been updated in 7 days that may require follow up/review.

Jira Task Interface

Here is an overview of the Jira task interface:

  1. Task title: Should include the course acronym (e.g VTEC), number (1143) and version (ON1) plus a useful description. Titles are often generated from email subjects and we adjust them as needed.
  2. People: This section displays who the task is assigned to, who created the task and if anyone else is watching the task.
  3. Action Buttons: This section of buttons allows us to do certain actions such as assign tasks, create subtasks and change the status of tasks. Some buttons are context-sensitive and will change depending on the status of the task.
  4. Details: The area displays the task type, priority and other useful information.
  5. Status: This shows the current task status at a glance and can be changed using the Action Buttons (e.g. the "Start Work" button in the screenshot above). If you click the "View Workflow" link, you are able to see the various workflow steps the task can take in Jira. Note: It's important that the current status is accurate so that other team members can see where tasks are at if needed.
  6. Description: This area will often contain the main task instructions, which can be manually created (e.g. Course) or generated automatically from an email send to olproduction@tru.ca. Adding instructions may be included in the Comments section at the bottom of the page.
  7. Time Tracking: This section summarizes all time logged on tasks and subtasks. It is very important that we log time for all our tasks, as that information is often reviewed on an annual basis to determine how we can improve our overall processes and set team goals. You can click the plus button to open the time logging window.
  8. Attachments: File can be attached from emails, pasted screenshots, etc. and will show up in this section.
  9. Sub-Tasks: Many Production tasks will have additional Sub-Tasks that contain additional information, instructions and actions required. Some examples are external communications from other departments regarding the task, course review requests, and other updates. Sub-Task should be assigned to the appropriate person (usually the main EST) and not sitting on unsigned on a task. In most cases, all sub-tasks should be closed before closing the main task.
  10. Comments: This section should contain all email communications with other departments and general task notes that will be helpful if someone else needs to review the task. It is very important to keep this section up-to-date. More information about task/course communication is provided in the Course Communication, Documentation and File Management section.

Using JIRA with Outlook Emails

Creating a Jira Task with Outlook

If you want to create a Jira task based on an outgoing email communication, include olenvironmentdev@tru.ca in the Bcc field of the outgoing communication. The jira mail handler will automatically create an unclassified task within 10 minutes.

Adding a Jira Task Comment with Outlook

Jira Task Generated from Incoming Email

To add an outgoing email communication to a Jira task, reply to the original email that was used to generate the task in Jira and include olenvironmentdev@tru.ca in the Bcc. Jira will automatically capture your outgoing reply as a comment.

Jira Task Manually Created or from Different Project

To add an outgoing email communication to this type of Jira task, include the Jira task number, surrounded by square brackets, at the end of the subject line, Example: [PROD-7563] and include olenvironmentdev@tru.ca in the Bcc field. Jira will automatically capture your outgoing reply as a comment to the task number included in the subject.

item.title: QuickTagIt, QuickScript, and Production Tools
