item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
The Moodle Gradebook provides a lot of extra information that isn't generally needed. We can remove the unnecessary columns from the Gradebook on the Course Grade Settings screen. Click Grade, and then Course grade settings.


In the Grade items settings section, change the Grade display type from "Default (Real)" to "Real (Percentage)". Scroll down to the User Report section and set the highlighted items to Hide:

item.title: Moodle Course Container Creation and Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Updated Adding Participants with revised self enrolment information.

Development containers that start with "DEV_OL" are often called our "Master" containers and should be placed under the correct Open Learning sub-category in Moodle.

Create a New Container

  • Go to: https://moodle.tru.ca/course/
  • Click the More button on the right-hand side and select Add a new course

General Settings

  • Add in the Course full name (including the course title), and the Course short name (just the numbering).
  • Search for the correct course category. All DEV containers go under Open Learning Development and then their Faculty/Academic area. If you're not sure of the course details, confirm in D4P course record.
  • No course start/end date information or settings required, disable if enabled

Container Naming

Part 1: DEV_OL
Part 2: Course Code - Acronym and Number separated be space
Part 3: Master/Amendment Number
Part 4: Course Title - separated by space dash space

Other Course Settings

On the same page, please adjust the following settings:

  1. Course format/Format: Onetopic format
  2. Appearance/Number of announcements: 3
  3. Files and uploads/Maximum upload size: 100MB
  4. Completion tracking/Enable completion tracking: Yes

Adding Participants

Setting Up Self Enrolment

Note: Please ask the Production Supervisor for the list of Faculty enrolment keys that you can save to your desktop or add to your password manager.

Setup self enrolment as follows: ol_maintenance, ol_library and associated faculty name (e.g. ol_art, ol_abe, etc.)

  1. Custom instance name: Add ol_maintenance, ol_library and associated faculty name (e.g. ol_art, ol_abe, etc.- Ask Production Supervisor for document if needed)
  2. Add corresponding Enrolment Key
  3. Adjust the Unenrol inactive after dropdown to:
    • ol_library - Never
    • All other users - 60 days
  4. Skip other fields
  5. Click the Add method button at the bottom of the page to save the enrolment method

Moodle Container Information for D4P

When we create a Moodle DEV course container, we need to add/update the details under Production in the course D4P master. The following fields should have information:

  • Moodle Container Name - The name used in the container setup
  • Moodle Container ID - This number is found at the end of a container URL. E.g. https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=40028
  • Production Staff Member - Select your name from the drop-down if the field hasn't been added to you

item.title: Curricunet Content Formatting (Web)
item.dc:creator: bforsyth
item.content:encoded:
Per instructions from Associate Director Naomi Cloutier, Curricunet content should be grouped together and shaded: Course Description, Prerequisites/ Exclusions, Learning Outcomes.

Editing should be flagging content as Curricunet approved in the Course Guide Word document. If there is a discrepancy, content will still be displayed as shown below.

If the three bulleted sections below do not match, we need to determine how it will be resolved - course adjustments or wait for Curricunet. Typically for an ID lead course, we will wait for Curricunet to catch up; however, if there are circumstances that require the course sooner then adjustments may be made. This typically becomes a discussion between Curriculum Services, Course Lead and others.

Formatting the Introduction in the Course Guide (Curricunet Information)

In the XML file, the following Course Guide headings will be put within a shaded box using the "note" tag with the "approved" attribute:

  • Course Description
  • Prerequisite (may include recommended and/or required as subheadings)/Exclusions
  • Learning Outcomes

The following image shows the desired output as it displays in Moodle:

item.title: Moodle Internal Review Process
item.dc:creator: bforsyth
item.content:encoded:
Preparing and Assigning an Internal Review

Preparing an Internal Review

  1. Ensure all files in Subversion are accounted for in course content - all files present should have a role. For a Maintenance course, look at old version to make sure all files are accounted for. Make sure you have formatted OLFM Guide material.
  1. Ensure all standard Moodle settings/blocks have been applied appropriately:
    • Key Course Milestones Block (All assessments are included, except for Final Exam)
    • Participants (Standard OL users and self enrolment added)
    • Grades (Grades areas matches assessment table and settings are correct)
  2. Review course for:
    • Correct title sizing
    • Standard components and verbiage on relevant tabs (Course Guide, Assignments Overview, Units/Modules, Resources, Discussions, Final Exam)
    • Links working, going to correct site
      • If linking to journal article, make sure full text is available.
      • Watch for errors being generated by http instead of https or missing http
    • Autolinks working correctly
    • Videos playing correctly, images and videos sized correctly
  3. Assessments using Quiz tool:
    • Set up using correct settings/layout including timing/review/activity completion
    • Headings and instructions where applicable:
      • Quiz/Self-Test - may not have any headings
      • Midterm - Instructions question at start with heading - outlining exam setup; Final Steps section at end; use headers in between to show different areas of exam
    • Setup a quiz review (eg Quiz 1 - for review) in "DO NOT COPY" tab. Use headings and page breaks for pools or different sections
      • Multiple short quizzes/self-tests can go in one quiz review but use headings to separate
      • Settings:
        • Unlimited time/attempts
        • All review items are checked for "Immediately" and "Later"
      • Word review copy of questions should be in Temp folder in Subversion

Note: The Final Exam and Practice quizzes are set up by the Exams Liaison Officer and information for those items will be provided in a separate Jira task. Make sure to communicate to the ELO who you send the IR to.

Assigning an Internal Review:

  1. In the Subversion directory for the course, open the Temp folder and within it create a new folder named Internal Review.
  1. In the Internal Review folder, copy and paste any files that the reviewer might require. For a web course, include all original Word documents, which will be used by the reviewer for comparison. For print courses, include any main PDFs that will be sent to the print shop (these will have item numbers).
  2. Commit the Internal Review folder and all its contents to Subversion.
  3. In JIRA, open the main task for the course. Near the top of the page, click Workflow and select Internal Review. This will automatically update the tasks status and will generate an internal review subtask.
  4. In the Description area of the new subtask list the relevant Subversion directory. If it is a web course, also include the development container name.
  5. Assign the subtask to the person who will be conducting the internal review, commenting on anything particular they should keep in mind while reviewing, such as providing context for differences that may occur between the content in Moodle and the original course files, or any outstanding questions with the course lead .
  6. Don’t forget to update the Exams Status subtask and assign back to the Exams Liaison Officer so the exam(s) can also be sent for Internal Review.

Conducting an Internal Review (Web)

Getting Started

  1. Log in to Moodle using the appropriate student login.
  2. Click on the container for the course you are reviewing. Because multiple containers often exist for different versions of a course, make sure you are in the right one.
  3. Check out the relevant Subversion directory.
  4. Open the Internal Review folder that should exist within the Temp folder. If such a folder does not exist or is empty, consult the primary EST for the course.
  5. Using the Word Docs found in the internal review folder, compare the original content against what appears in the course's Moodle container. Go through each file systematically, making note of any potential issues by using the comment feature found in Word under the Review tab.
  6. For issues not directly related to the content in the Word Docs, such as missing course banners or faulty structuring, make note as a comment within the internal review JIRA subtask.

General Things to Watch For:

  1. Styles - in Moodle, heading levels may be off.
  2. The inclusion of all standard elements: Announcements, Student Cafe, Standard Tabs, Key Course Milestones block
  3. Block settings
  4. Proper overall formatting of page content. What is in Moodle should more or less match what is in the Word documents.
  5. Symbols, equations, centre-aligned table headings, subscript, superscript, italics, bold, underline; these elements do not always convert properly and can be easily overlooked. Pay close attention for such details.
    Tip: You may find it useful to highlight these elements in the Word document being reviewed to make them more easily identifiable.
  6. Broken links. Be sure to click every single one to ensure that it is working and links to the proper website or internal content.
  7. Missing content.
  8. Image issues. Images may sometimes be missing, improperly sized, or put in the wrong place.
  9. Inconsistent or false instructions to students.
  10. Tools that are mentioned in the course but have not been created, ie. discussion topics, journals, blogs, groups, wikis, etc.
  11. Production notes that have not yet been removed. These will usually appear within square brackets, ie: [Production - please link to the TRU-OL Student Handbook].
  12. Any instructions or descriptions that seem specific to a print version of the course.
  13. Functionality of quizzes/midterms. Take each one to ensure that any settings specified in the course have been applied. Also check that no content is missing or improperly formatted. The question type being used should make sense for what is being asked in each case.
    Refer to the Online Assessment Internal Review Process page for further information.
  14. If unsure about whether something may be an issue or not, comment anyway just in case.

Course Guide

When reviewing the Course Guide, check for the following:

  • Are all standard elements included: Announcements, Student Café, Getting Started in Moodle, Key Course Navigation Features
  • Are all standard dropdown headings included and in the correct order? Are headings at the correct level within each section? Most courses have the following:
    • Introduction
    • Course Materials
    • Course Topics
    • Assessments
    • Suggested Schedule
    • Strategies for Success
    • Help Available
    • Course Contributors
    • Copyright and Credits
  • In the "Introduction" heading:
    • Course Description, Course Requisites, Learning Outcomes should be placed in an “Approved” notebox (the yellow box below)
  • Course Materials: ensure students are directed to contact OL Materials with relevant questions. If the course includes an additional course site or digital textbook, ensure it is linked appropriately.
  • Course Topics: Ensure course unit/module/topic titles align across all sections of the course.
  • Assessment: Ensure all assessment titles/weights align across all sections of the course
  • Suggested Schedule (standard web)/Course Schedule (online):
    • Ensure Unit/Module/Assessment titles match across all content
    • Ensure assessment information is included in the appropriate unit/module to match the suggested deadline
    • Ensure Word document format has been included.

Assignments/Assessments Overview:

When reviewing the Assignments/ Assessments Overview tab, check for the following:

  1. Appropriate headings have been included to differentiate Assignments from other assessments (quizzes, final projects)
  2. Assignment settings match the details of the assignment: accepted file types, grade, submission types (if video submissions are required, ensure online text submissions are enabled and Kaltura submission instructions are included). Ensure activity completion is set.

Quizzes/Self-Tests/Practice Exams/Final Exams

If the course has quizzes, self-tests, practice exams, etc. use the Online Assessments Internal Review Process documentation to check the material during the IR process.

Note: If the course has a Final Exam, the Exam Liaison Officer will assign you a separate Exam IR task in Jira.

Units/Modules

When reviewing the Units/Modules, check for the following:

  1. Are the chapter/subchapters appearing correctly?
  2. Overview/Introduction: Ensure titles and descriptions of course topics, learning activities, assessments matches across unit/module and rest of course.
  3. Assessments chapter: should have minimal information while linking directly to the assessment(s)
  4. References should ideally be located as the last chapter

Participants

When reviewing the Participants area in Moodle, check for the following:

  1. Self enrolment has been set up correctly
  2. Standard OL default/student accounts have been enrolled (e.g. s_arts, s_all)

Grades

When reviewing the Grades area in Moodle, check for the following:

  1. In the Grades/Setup tab:
    • The order of the assessment activities matches the table in the Course Guide
    • The assessment weights and marks (max grade) match the information provided in the Course Guides and Assignments
    • If there is a final exam in the course, confirm that we have a custom (Final Exam) grade item with the correct weight value
    • Ensure that any final exam activities are greyed out/hidden
    • Confirm no practice exam activities/quizzes are showing
    • Confirm the Course total row is hidden
  2. In the Grades/Setup/Course grade settings area, confirm sure the settings match our standard OL Grades settings

Final Steps

When you have finished your internal review, re-commit all reviewed files to Subversion, add notes/comments to task, and assign the JIRA internal review subtask back to the course's primary EST.

Note: It is extremely important that all course material changes are captured in the XML, as that file becomes the master document for Open Learning and will be used for future revisions of the course.

item.title: Online Assessments Internal Review Process
item.dc:creator: bforsyth
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added checking/disabling autolinking to the Assessment Setup Check section

Following are the steps involved in reviewing Online Assessments, including Quizzes, Self-Tests, and Final Exam. For most internal reviews, the reviewer is to document errors/ discrepancies, not directly adjust them. There are exceptions, however, in some cases in which assessments are not part of the regular curriculum development cycle. If it is unclear, check with the person that sent the review.

Before You Begin

Ensure you have the correct source files:

  • Quizzes/ Self-Tests: should be located in Subversion or Examrepo/Course/Working/For IR if set up by the Exams Liaison Officer.
  • Final Exams/ Practice Exams: located in Examrepo/Course/Working/For IR. If files are not there, follow up with the person who sent the internal review. The internal review sub-task should clearly state what you are expected to review and what files you should find.
    • Final Exams will be either a “pool” document or an individual form for online.

Question Content Check

  1. Locate correct Moodle shell
  2. Within Moodle you should see a "Do Not Copy" tab - on this tab should be quizzes that contain questions for checking

Check quiz settings before beginning quiz

  • Make sure no time limit
  • Make sure unlimited attempts
  • Make sure all review options are checked for "Immediately after" and "Later"
  • Check to see if you have a password to use
  • Maximum grade should be set to 0 so the quiz for review does not appear in the gradebook

Use Source Document(s) to check questions

  1. Start quiz
  2. Check questions match source document - no missed formatting, no glitchy formatting, spacing is consistent. Note that the structure of the quiz in the Do Not Copy tab will not reflect the structure of the quiz made available to students.
  3. Make sure answers are not highlighted, all distractors present
  4. Note if correct mark is showing for question - watch for different marks for questions described as a random pool - all questions in a pool must have the same value
  5. Enter correct answer for self-marking questions
  6. Submit quiz to get feedback - if incorrect answers, figure out why - you clicked the wrong value or answer is wrong
  7. For questions that are not self-marking, check that answers have been added in the Grader Information section and are formatted correctly
  8. Document issues in documents using the comment function

Assessment Setup Check

Locate the actual assessment within the Moodle container. Final Exams should be located in the Final Exam tab; Midterms/Quizzes/Self-Tests may be located in the Assessments Overview tab or their own tab.

Check Quiz Settings Before You Begin

  1. From the main activity page, confirm Activity names auto-linking under Filters (More dropdown>Filters), set to Off if needed
  2. Make sure time limit is correct (check against course guide/instructions near quiz) & auto submission is enabled for timed quizzes
  3. Make sure number of attempts are correct - Final Exams/Midterms - one attempt; Quizzes/ Midterms - read course guide/course content on how many are permitted; Self-Tests – usually unlimited
  4. Check what Question Behaviour should be: If "yes", you will need to watch for “all of the above” questions
  5. Make sure appropriate review options are checked for "Immediately after" and "Later" or for paced courses "Closed." Final Exams - nothing shown at all. Midterms - Immediate - marks, correct and feedback then Later just Marks, Quizzes - see course for details or check in with someone. Self-tests - all options checked
  6. Make sure Final Exam has a password set - currently setting unique passwords
  7. For all except Final Exam, make sure activity completion is set (Student must view; Student must receive a grade)
  8. For alt. assessments - check for conditions

Use Source Document(s) to Check Layout

  1. Review Instructions in the Description box - are they clear and complete? May include: materials permitted, review options, number of attempts permitted, time limit, context for what will be on the quiz/ exam.
  2. Go to Edit Quiz
    • Look for headings -the longer the assessment, the more headings
      • Final Exams/Midterms should have the following headings: Instructions, Section headings, Final Steps
      • Tests: Instructions/Final Steps – in-between headings if long
      • Short Quizzes: May have no headings
    • Look for randomization - shuffle, pools - look at source to see if possible if not done - just note
    • Look for Page Breaks - good rule of thumb is about 5 marks per page but there are reasons why it could be more
    • Look at marks per question - do they match - especially important for randomization
    • Make sure Total Marks and Maximum Grade match
    • Switch role to Teacher and make sure Notifications are on for graded assessments (everything except self-tests)
  3. Try quiz as a student - does it feel complete, are there enough instructions to explain layout, how program behaves

item.title: Course Documentation and Tracking (JIRA and D4P)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent Updates
- Added additional status information to the Tracking Milestones in D4P section.

JIRA

JIRA is our web-based workflow management tool that OL Production uses to track and document all work and task communications. Review the JIRA instructions on how to get your first dashboard set up for keeping track of your assigned tasks and how to use Outlook to log information.

Jira at a Glance

  1. Task number - We include this number in our Outlook email subject (e.g. GEOG 1191 SW5 - Reading for External Review - [PROD-32423] so that replies are automatically added to our tasks.
  2. Task title - This should also contain the course name, number and version (e.g. GEOG 1191 SW5) and additional context if needed (e.g. GEOG 1191 SW5 - Unit 1, Topic 2 Link Adjustment). We often receive emails/tasks with titles that aren't helpful, please adjust as needed.
  3. Task Management Menu - These buttons allow us to assign tasks, change status, change tasks types and create subtasks. This area is important for managing the day-to-day tasks in Jira and is used often.
  4. Task Details - This section provides information should as task type, priority, status, etc. and should be updated as needed.
  5. Task Description - This area should contain the main instructions for a task. When an email is sent to OL Production (olproduction@tru.ca) an "Unclassified" task is automatically generated and the body of the email is included in the Description section. Sometimes the formatting doesn't carry across well, and we may need to review the email directly.
  6. Sub-Tasks - Course and other Production tasks will often include additional sub-tasks. This may include the various team review tasks, external communication to other areas in OL, copyright reports, etc. If you receive an "Unclassified" task, make sure to move it under the correct main task, using the More > Move drop-down option in the Task Management Menu.
  7. Task Comments - All task communication (e.g. emails), task updates and other related info should be logged in the Comments section of the task. This area is the most updated across our regular tasks and should include any relevant information to the task for current and future review. More information on comments below.
  8. Additional Task Data - This section included Assignee information, Dates, and most importantly Time Tracking. Production logs time on tasks in order to gather long-term data for the team on our overall processes to identify efficiencies and challenges to improve our workflow whenever possible.

Subtasks Organization

Assigned Jira Tasks

Comments

Anyone on the Production Team should be able to go to comments under main issue to determine overall status of course. eg. 1/2 modules formatted, out for internal ...some sort of comment which gives snapshot of course status. Note: This information should be kept up to date daily!

Logging Time

Similar to above, anyone should be able to see time worked on course with a comment describing work (eg. 2h formatted modules 1 and 2) Your time worked for a course assigned to you should be logged under main task. This information should also be kept up to date daily.

Note: Time information is used to aggregate data from our tasks (courses per year, course development time, time on non-course related task, number of course fix requests, etc.) to make informed decisions regarding our workload, future capacity and other variables that may affect our team and other areas in OL. It is very important that this information is kept up-to-date and is as accurate as possible.

Task Management and Updates

All tasks sub-tasks have an assignee (no unassigned tasks) and have correct workflow status. (In progress, External ...). Anyone should be able to determine the sub-task by its description (be specific). Any time logged should be from someone who is not the main EST for course.

Anyone should be able to see that percent complete and generic comment that goes with it up to date. There should be some correlation to what is shown here and what is in the comments/work logging. (From a data maintenance point of view, this would be secondary to what is listed above)

Please make sure your comments/work logging are up-to-date. As a courtesy to each other, please be specific in your comments information.

As material can move among team members, it is important that our documentation on courses is clear.

Creating Jira Tasks and Logging Comments with Outlook

Often we have questions (e.g. content issues) or require feedback (e.g. External Review) from people outside the Production team, and it's extremely important to capture that communication process in Jira. The easiest way to create a Jira task that will capture future email comments is to compose an email (give is a useful subject that includes course name/version) and Cc the olproduction@tru.ca email address. This will automatically generate an unclassified task in Jira that can be assigned, added as a subtask and will automatically capture external replies as task comments. You can also add your comments to the task by cc'ing olproduction@tru.ca on any replies you send out on the same email/task.

Manually Logging Comments

IMPORTANT: If outgoing and incoming communications aren't being logged using the email method above, it's important that the email communications are being manually copied/pasted into the related tasks so that other Production team members can review the communication chain without having to dig through various inboxes and emails. The Jira task/subtask should contain a FULL record of incoming and outgoing email communications.

D4P2 (Data 4 the People 2)

The D4P2/D4P (Data 4 the People 2) database application in used by various teams in Open Learning, such as Curriculum Services, Instructional Designers, Editing, Production and other to organize and track various aspects of the Curriculum Development process. D4P provides a high-level view of the course development process and progress to different areas in Open Learning. Production team members update our current course development milestones in D4P on w weekly basis. More information on those milestones in provided below.

D4P at a Glance

Course Listing Page

  1. Course Search - You can search by acronym, course number or both
  2. Course Modality - These boxes describe the modality of the course (Standard Web, Online and Print) and contain information regarding the various versions of the course.
  3. Course Masters - Each master describes a version of the course, the scope of development work, the current development phase and key dates.
  4. Master View Button - This button takes you to a new section with further information regarding this course master and also provides additional navigation options to other pages, including the Production area that we update on a regular basis in course milestones as we work through a course.
  5. Print Course Modality - If the course also has a print version, there will be a separate modality box with Print master information and navigation options.
  6. Course Attributes - This section includes additional course metadata that can be useful when trying to find additional information such as academic area, college (used on resource title pages) and previous course codes
  7. Course Exams - This area in maintained by the Exams Liaison Offers and describes the status of current and previous exams for both online and print. Production uses this section to determine which files are needed for course file requests.

Course Master Page

  1. Course ID/Lead - This section identifies the person managing the development for this particular master. Often they will be the main contact for course related questions, but review the Course Communications section for additional details.
  2. Master Sections - This is where other teams in Open Learning can add updates and other information to be viewed by other D4P users. We use the Production section to add Moodle container information, dates and progress updates on a regular basis.
  3. Progress Summary - This area pulls information from the other master sections for a summary of the course development process. This information is useful to see who is working on the course from other Teams in case we need to reach out for additional information.

Production Course Master Page

  1. Production Master Information - The Production Supervisor and ESTs add information to this section during the course setup and development process. Often, ESTs will fill out the Moodle Container Name and Moodle Container ID information while working on a course.
  2. Progress Updates - This section is where ESTs will provide brief course milestone updates on a weekly basis. These updates are important as other areas of Open Learning use this information to set course development priorities and determine when courses are launched. Review the Production Course Development Milestones for more details on these updates.

Production Course Development Milestones

Tracking Milestones in JIRA

Course tasks should be evaluated DAILY. The Course workflow will automatically update to lowest Percent Complete on Transition.
In between values need to be manually updated.
Please estimate as best as possible using the following as guideline.

Tracking Milestones in D4P

Course records should be updated WEEKLY at minimum - currently Friday morning. Updating at Major transitions is greatly appreciated by others who use the database.

The following indicates how information should be documented in D4P.

item.title: Course Communications
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Update to course maitnance/amendment question communication as of August 22, 2024 (now going to Curriculum Services)
- Updated Start of Work email to reflect wording around new self enrolment keys/process.
- Added addition information around course development questions and communication.
- Added email example with additional information to include in communications to Curriculum Services when we have course related questions.

E-Learning Support Technicians need to communicate with the other teams involved with Curriculum Development.

All course email should come from the olproduction email address so if replies come back in, they get captured by JIRA. Best Practice is to copy & paste message into JIRA or BCC to olproduction with JIRA PROD number in subject line so communication gets captured as part of main task.

Note on Maintenance Courses and Amendments (non-ID lead):
- Most communications/questions regarding maintenance courses will go to Curriculum Services to be reviewed and sent to the appropriate individuals/team.
- Copyright questions will continue to back to Copyright team
- For External Review request, please send to Naomi via Curriculum Services email.

The following summarizes types of communication and who should receive.

Start of Work

Please send out the following communications when we start work on courses:

Process for Clarifying Course Information

Use the following details for addressing course questions that may come up.

Maintenance Revisions

  • Start with reviewing the previous version of the course to compare structure, setup, settings, resources, etc, as often those items will be carried forward to the new version.This may include things such as:
    • PDF resources and other files
    • Images
    • Quiz review settings
    • Assignment advanced grading setup (Rubrics and Marking Guides)
  • If we're not able to resolve by reviewing the previous version, you can ask the Production Supervisor for guidance on how to proceed.
  • General course content questions about formatting, consistency, spelling, etc. will go to the Curriculum Services to be reviewed/addressed.
  • Assessment questions regarding mark allocation, quiz timing, alignment issues (e.g. rubrics don't match the assignment information) can go directly to Course Lead which is generally Curriculum Services for Maintenance course. (Check D4P).

New/Major Revisions

  • Similar to Maintenance, it can be helpful to review the previous version of the course (if available). For example if resources were previously used, assessment setup/settings, etc.
  • If we're not able to resolve by reviewing the previous version, you can ask the Production Supervisor for guidance on how to proceed.
  • Content and assessment questions will go directly to the Course Lead (check D4P).

Communications Process Matrix

NOTE: Email is the most common form of communicating. However, in many cases it is best to communicate directly via messaging/video call to the other persons to explain in person or ask if they can discuss.

Review Stage Communications

NOTE: The Exam Status task will only be used at the start of course work to communicate final assessment information. Additional items noted in the table below will be added as comments directly on the corresponding Exam Jira task linked on the main Course task. The linked task also shows the current Exam status.

IMPORTANT:
- The Exam and Course task status should match
- The course should not go out for External Review if the Exam is also not ready for External Review


Example Emails

All should be from sent from OLproduction@tru.ca.

Start of Work:

Note: Update items in italics to match the course information.

Email Subject: ABCD 1234 Master No - Production Starting Course Work

Hello,

Production has started work on ABCD 1234 SW1. The Moodle development container is DEV_OL ABCD 1234_SW1 – Course Title.

(IF Additional Environments/Resources - This course includes an external PressBooks site as an OER resource which can be accessed at: https://sitename.pressbooks.tru.ca/)

Please let me know if any additional information is required and if there is a copyright report prepared for the course (OR The copyright report has been received).

Thank you, Your Name

To Start External Review:

Subject: ABCD 1234 Master No - Ready for External Review

Hello,

Course ABCD 1234 is ready for external review: Container Name goes here.
[If Print Course as well, state if print proofs on order: ie Print proofs are on order and will be delivered.]

Attached is the OLFM Guide/Material OR We did not receive any OLFM Guide.

Please send all changes to OL Production.

Thank you, Your Name

To Start External Review With Final Exam:

Subject: ABCD 1234 Master No - Ready for External Review

Hello,

Course ABCD 1234 is ready for external review: Container Name goes here.
[If Print Course as well, state if print proofs on order: ie Print proofs are on order and will be delivered.]

Please find attached the paper-based final exam, answer keys and the online information in order to do a final review and sign off.

Online exam information:
***LINK TO FINAL EXAM TAB***
Password: ***FINAL EXAM PASSWORD***
Please do not give password out to students.

You will see two tabs, the Final Exam tab and the DO NOT COPY tab. The one named Final Exam contains the exam the students will be receiving, and the DO NOT COPY tab is for ease of question review only.

Attached is the OLFM Guide/Material OR We did not receive any OLFM Guide.

Please send all changes to OL Production.

Thank you, Your Name

To Follow up after External Review changes done:

- reply to email you received

Subject: ABCD 1234 - external review changes made

Hello,

The changes requested below have been made. Please let us know if there are any more changes or if course is ready for sign off.

Thank you, Your Name

Email to CSA after Signoff

(cc OL Production to generate Jira task)

Subject: ABCD 1234 Master no. - OLFM and ECG Material (OR no OLFM material)

Hello,

Attached is the OLFM and Enhanced Course Guide material for ABCD 1234 Master no (OR We did not receive any OLFM material for ABCD 1234 Master no). Please let me know once the ECG has been prepared and uploaded.

Your Name

Email to Curriculum Services if Signoff from Lead

Hello,

The course ID,xxxxxx xxxxxx, has signed off ABCD 1234 master no. Production has finished all work on the course and final signoff can be done.

Your Name

Course Content Questions (Development, Content Support, etc.) #

This communication can be dynamic depending on the task and various factors involved. Our main goal is to provide Curriculum Services with as much course information and details as possible to make it easier for them to provide the information we require. Our communication should contain much of the following information below as needed:

  • Course acronym, number and version (e.g. BIOL 2341 SW2)
  • Who initiated the request (e.g. OLFM(s), Instructional Designer, etc. - include names)
  • Other affected stakeholders (OLFMs, other OL teams, etc.)
  • Brief summary of request details (include original email that generated the task, if applicable)
  • Include screenshots, copy/pasted text, documents, etc., if that helps provided additional context for the request
  • If LIVE assessments are involved, provide the full name of affected containers and the number of students who have completed the assessment for each one
  • Provide any other relevant information

item.title: Working with Course Files (Subversion)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
All course files for OL Production are stored using file versioning software on an independent server (not part of standard IT drives) called Subversion and, we use an application called Tortoise SVN to download/upload files to our Subversion server. You'll need to set up Subversion before starting any course work.

How the Subversion Process Works

All content is located in repository.

  1. User checks out material to work on it on local hard drive.
  2. User checks back material when done or wants to commit work done to date.
  3. User deletes local copy (best practice).

Database keeps track of all changes, previous versions can be recalled at any time.

Checkout Course Files

Commit Course Files (After Changes)

Course Data Structure within Subversion Repositories

All current course material is found in: /production/trunk/Courses directory. Each course has its own directory: EG. APEC1671. Previous versions of course material are found in: /production/tags/Courses directory, specific version is noted in folder name.

Within a Course directory are 4 permanent directories:

  • \Content
  • \OLFMG
  • \Resources
  • \Revision Notes

A temporary directory may be created while material is being worked on.

  • \Temp

Course Root Folder

XML files should be stored in the root/main folder.

  • The file name should include the version such ABCD1234_sw1.xml.
  • All xml files are left in folder (eg. sw1, sw2 ...)
  • For moodle transition project an "_m" has been added to mark same version but different LMS setup.

\Content Folder

This folder contains the main TRU created material including:

  • Course Guide(s)
  • Units
  • Assignments
  • Assessments (quizzes/midterms)
  • Images
  • Other Standard Components: Suggested Schedule/Strategies for Success

All content for all methods of delivery are stored within this directory.

Sub directories may be created is large amount of content.

If print/web material, file name should indicate print files (will have item number in title)

If Word files were only used to create the original XML file and were not updated as part of the revision cycle, please put into a clearly marked folder that indicates "do not" use. Eg. _SCRIPTED_DO_NOT_USE

\OLFMG Folder

This folder contains material for Open Learning Faculty Member (OLFM) which would typically include OLFM Guide and if required for a particular course other files required by OLFM eg. Excel files…

\Revision Notes Folder

This folder can contain information from Curriculum Services, Editing and Copyright
The files may include:

  • CMP file - describes what was done during the revision.
  • Copyright report

\Resources folder

This folder contains material which is supplemental to main content such worksheets, readings and images, and will container two additional subfolders:

  • \Images
  • \Files

\Temp Folder

The only material within this directory should be temporary files of limited duration. This material would include:

  • PDF titlepages
  • Review notes from internal review

Any content in this folder can be deleted once the course is signed off.

Other Sub-Folders

\Temp\Previous Version Folder

This folder contains a temporary copy of the previous version of course. This is most commonly done for courses which are in Maintenance as not all files may be returned to us.

After all files needed are transferred to proper folders, then this folder can be deleted.
item.category: Course Communication, Documentation and File Management

item.title: How to Use Subversion
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added additional information regarding the inclusion of course acronym, number and version in the Subversion Comment Details section.

IMPORTANT:
Keep your course files fresh (especially if potential for more than one person to working on that directory). The most important step in using system is that you do a fresh checkout or update before you start working on files. Check it Frequently

Checking Files Out Of Subversion

  • Open Windows Explorer
  • Select Desktop
  • Right click to bring up context menu and select SVN Checkout

Windows 11 Users:
Windows 11 "helpfully" hides some additional right-click menu items, including Subversion under a Show more option item. Here are some instructions on how to open the full right-click menu by default on Windows 11.


  • OR
    Just Right-Click on your Desktop
  • Provide name of location you want to access. (yellow area above)
    • A. Copy and Paste URL of repository from JIRA task
      or
    • B. If directory accessed before can click down arrow to access history
      or
    • C. Click dots at end to browse repository to get to directory you need
  • Provide name of checkout directory: Usually let program decide (purple area)
  • Click Okay

Files will be copied out of repository to desktop folder. and will show as follows.

Understanding Tortoise SVN icons

The program provides graphic indicators for status of files.

Green Check Mark

On checkout, folder and files will show green checkmarks.

Red Exclamation Mark

As soon as a file is changed, icons will change to red exclamation marks

Changes are shown at both the highest level and at specific directory/file level. As shown below. The red exclamation mark shows at the highest level GEOG1221 and when the subfolders are looked at it shows that change only occurs in Temp folder. All other folders have green checkmark indicating no change.

Red Exclamation Mark Means

That Content is Out Of Sync with the version stored in the Master Database.

It is a less than subtle reminder to COMMIT changes.

Committing/Checking In Files With Comments

  1. Go to your directory with Red Exclamation Mark.
  2. Right click to bring up context menu and select SVN Checkout…
    On the screen that appears:
    • You can enter a comment to describe changes in top portion. (A)
    • You can see listing of what is being committed. (B)
    • Click OK to proceed (C), a Processing screen will come up (somewhere on one of your monitors – look for turtle icon )

Processing Screen, Click OK, to finish.

Icon should now be green checkmarks.

You can Commit at any level – individual file, subfolder, directory. Committing at highest level will capture all levels below.

Get in the habit of Commiting Changed Content at regular intervals (I recommend at major breaks in your day – lunch, end of day)

A fully committed folder can be safely deleted from your desktop.

Subversion Comment Details

Ensure that you add a comment each time you commit. Comments should include the course acronym, number and version similar to Jira task titles, a basic summary of changes, and if useful, a brief reasoning behind it. For example, after preparing before an internal review, the comment might look something like this: "CONV 1041 SW2 - Internal Review file and content added to TEMP folder. Course now entering Internal Review."

Managing Files and Folders in Subversion

How To Add New Files

Adding new files to a checked directory is different from changing existing content.

Until file(s) has been registered in database, icons on folder will NOT change.

Actual File may show a question mark icon  or no special icon at all. 

  • To Add:
    • Select file name in Windows Explorer
    • Right click to bring up context menu
    • Select TortoiseSVN menu, then Add.
  • Icon will change to a plus sign.
    The directory icon will now change to Red Exclamation Mark
  • Perform the Commit/Check in procedure above to complete process.

How to Delete Files

  • To remove material, simply delete from checked out folder and then run a check in (commit) to folder.
  • When Commit is made the deleted files will show on list.
    • Make comment (recommended)
    • Select tick box to acknowledge deletion.

This will turn on OK button.

Click OK to continue.

All future updates/checkouts of that folder will no longer have that material.

How to Create Folders

Adding a Empty Folder

Adding a empty folder is similar to adding a normal file with one extra minor step. After right clicking the folder you wish to add, scrolling down to TortoiseSVN, and selecting "Add", the following window will appear:

The folder you wish to add should already be selected (if not, select it), so you can simply select "OK". This will set the folder to be added the next time you commit it.

Adding a Folder Containing Files

While similar, adding a filled folder differs slightly when the window appears. Again, right click the folder you wish to add, scroll down to TortoiseSVN, select "Add" and the following will appear:

Note the extra files which appear. These are the files which exist inside the folder. Simply ensure that they are all selected, and click "OK". This will set the folder and all of the content within it to be added the next time you commit it.

NOTE: you do not need to add the files within a folder individually. Simply checking them off at this point is sufficient.

Two or more people using the same folder

  1. Any number of people can check out the same folder.
  2. Be aware of who else is involved in working on those files.
  3. Never assume that a copy left on your desktop is up to date (even if it has a green checkmark), always do an update before working on it if any time has passed.

In general for multiple people: If each is working with different files within the folder, there will be no conflict. If each is working on the same files then a conflict can arise. The program will highlight problem and ask you to figure out course of action.

THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF PROBLEMS IS POOR UPDATING AND CHECKING IN PRACTICE.

Tagging/Copying Previous Version of Course Files

This step is usually completed by the Production Supervisor when preparing course files for Production work.

Within a given course repository there is typically only one version of the course which is the most recent launch (could be master or amendment).

Note: There can be exceptions to this rule but there should be a folder system to clearly mark.

Before adding new files to course directory, the previous version should be "tagged/branched". This process creates a new directory with files at that specific time.

Tagging/Copying Steps

  1. Right click on main folder for the old course version you wish to tag. Under "TortoiseSVN" select "Branch/tag..."
  2. Set the "To path:" to http://phoenix.tru.ca:9880/production/tags/Courses/COURSENAME_VERSION
  3. Include a log message that describes the version of the course you are adding and any additional relevant information eg. HRMN 2821 - tagging SW5 before starting SW6
  4. click HEAD revision in the repository
  5. Select "OK" to create

Note: Previous version can be checked out Tagged area for reference or to grab files as needed
item.category: Course Communication, Documentation and File Management

item.title: Course File Cleanup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Course File Cleanup is removing unnecessary files from the course directory structure (Course checked out of Subversion).

Make sure you have:

  • After course has received sign off (from Course Lead)
  • Materials have been sent out (OLFM Guide, or print materials if applicable)

The JIRA task should document both sign off and any material sent out.

JIRA

  • When you reach this stage, the course should have a status of Signed Off but NOT cleaned.
  • Once files have been cleaned up and committed to Subversion, change Jira status to Closed and comment that files have been completed and committed.

What is Clean?

  1. All JIRA sub-tasks have been assigned and Closed.
  2. Files contain well named content – no extra initials or dates on files, for example ENGL1101_SW_courseguide.docx. (For Print Courses Only: Print items should have the current item number in the file name and files contain PDF's sent to the Print Shop.)
  3. If changes have not been made to Word Documents, please make sure they are put in subfolder called Source_Files_Not_Updated so it is clear next version of files must be created from XML.
  4. Main course folder should contain the following items (even if empty)
    • Content
      • The Content folder should contain ONE editable version of all content that we formatted (presuming we were provided with it). For quizzes, keep original and Respondus file. Please note, subfolders are fine as long as they are logical.
    • OLFMG
      • Should contain OLFM Guide and related material intended to go with it, if applicable.
    • Resources
      • Typically has Images and Files subfolders, should have one copy of each resource used in the course.
    • Revision Notes
    • The course XML eg. BBUS2211_SW3.xml
  5. Delete any Temp folders/files
  6. Delete Output folder from Scripting folder
  7. Put copy of FINAL xml in subversion root directory (overtime a number of .XML files could exist here). Should be one .XML file only per master (course version, example SW1, SW2, PR1 etc) unless one is for Blearn and one is for Moodle. (CHANGE July 10/14)
  8. Can easily be zipped up and sent out for next revision without any confusion on content or missing content.

item.title: XML to Print Web Application
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
The XML to Print program was created to allow Production to generate print materials from a single course XML (eXtensible Markup Language) file to be used as part of the curriculum development cycle.
This is most often used for creating Enhanced Course Guides (ECGs), and for retrieving up-to-date course content for Curriculum Services.

Website: https://olhub.tru.ca/xmltoprint/
U: xml
P: print

XML to Print Web User Guide https://olhub.tru.ca/xmltoprint/assets/xmltoprint_user_documentation.pdf
(Also linked within the XML to Word Converter under the label Documentation)

item.title: Word Structure & Print Document Layout
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
Course content is typically developed in Word.
Production staff need to be familiar with how to quickly and efficiently manipulate Word documents to extract or format content. Files that are linked within the LMS (Moodle) or Wordpress are required to have the same formatting standards as print documents.

Viewing Word Document Content/Structure

How to Use Outline View

Outline View shows the structure of documents based on defined styles (Headings 1, 2,3 etc. and body text).
In the Ribbon, you should see a Developer tab. Before you begin working with your document, make sure the Document Template (the styles created and used by Production) has been loaded.

Use Outline View to:

  1. Look at structure overall - helps to see consistency and missing headings
  2. Adjust structure quickly over large parts of the document
  3. Move entire sections of the document

If the structure seems to be missing, revert to normal Page Outline View.

Creating Word Document Structure

Creating Structure

Section Breaks within Word Documents allow you to precisely control formatting of your document such as:

  • Margins
  • Header/Footer Layout (includes page numbering)

Both the above can be set for whole document or just a section. Understanding section breaks is critical to large document formatting.

Here is the type of structure that needs to be created for a one of the more complicated structures, seen within a study guide of multiple units.

Documents such as a Course Guide or an Assignment file follow a similar format without the complexities of units and therefore unit titles. For example, your average course guide might look something like this:

Note that the Course Guide may appear in a Study Guide, and would then be given the same breaks and structure as one of the units in a multi-unit document.

The main difference between the first outline and the second is the individual units, each requiring their own title page, as well as their own table of contents. Unlike the outline above, these individual units do not require a Copyright page. The first one would start after the master table of contents. Each unit will look something like this:

The second main difference is that there are multiple Table of Contents is set up through bookmarks.

Table of Contents

The Table of Contents will pull from the titles which have headers applied to them. This means you should avoid using heading styles on titles which shouldn't appear in the Table of Contents (ie: the copyright page, or things such as the actual title to the table of contents page). Instead set these as the Normal style and manually shift them to bold Arial 14-18 font.

Creating a Simple Single Table of Contents

Start by opening up the References tab. Select the Table of Contents icon located on the far left, and click Custom Table of Contents.

This will open up the Table of Contents window. Generally the only thing you will change is the Show levels option under the General Section. The number selected will be the highest level of heading that will appear in the Table of Contents. The most commonly used is 3, however you may decide to show more or less depending on the nature of the document.

Formatting information for Table of Contents is at the end of the Content table on the Word/Print Formatting Page.
To clean up the Table of Contents, remove the leader line and page Number for H1.

Creating Multiple Table of Contents

In long documents where each section requires a table of contents you need to define sections as bookmarks then use specific Word field codes to generate each TOC.

Add Bookmarks

  1. Select the section that you want to create a table of contents for.
  2. On the Insert tab, in the Links group, click Bookmark.
  3. In the Bookmark name box, type a name for the bookmark and Add.
  4. Repeat steps 1-4 for each section that requires a table of contents.

Create Each Table of Contents

  1. Click where you want to add a section table of contents.
  2. On the Insert tab, in the Text group, click Quick Parts, and then click Field.
  3. Under Field names, click TOC.
  4. Click Field Codes, and then click Options.
  5. In the Switches list, click \b, click Add to Field, and then click OK.
  6. In the Field codes box, type the name of the bookmark for that section.
  7. In the Switches list, click \o, click Add to Field, and then click OK.
  8. In the Field codes box, after \o, type in the leves you want to show ie. 1-3 or 2-3
    [NOTE: The file Field Code will look like TOC \b BOOKMARKNAME\o 1-3]
  9. Click OK and repeat for each section that requires a table of contents.

How to Search and Highlight Formatting

Finding and highlighting formatting, such as bold, italic, superscript etc., can be helpful when converting to XML, creating print documents, and reviewing courses.

Advanced Find Tools

Adding/Deleting Comments and Tracking Changes

Production adds comments to documents at several stages in the process:

  • When reviewing initial course content from Editing, to comment on anything that requires clarification/missing content.
  • When a course is in internal review (IR) (checking another staff members course for consistency)

Add/Delete Comment

To insert a comment into a Word Document, simply select the text you wish to comment on, and go to the Review tab in your ribbon, and select New Comment. To delete a comment, right click on the comment and select Delete Comment.

Track Changes and Viewing Comments

Track Changes is used by Editors, Instructional Designers (IDs), Open Learning Faculty Members (OLFMs), and the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs).

If you are having problems viewing the comments or the track changes, locate the Show Markup menu located in the Review tab on the Ribbon. Ensure that what you wish to see is checked off, and under Specific People that All Reviewers is selected.

When you initially get a course, Track Changes if often on. To clean up your view, so you can work with the document, locate the Accept menu in the Review tab on the Ribbon and select Accept All Changes.
item.category: Print Course Development & Print Material Formatting

item.title: Word/Print Formatting
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
OL Formatting Standards

Word Layout for Web Courses

Course content is typically provided to Production staff in Word documents. These documents are converted to XML, and then HTML to be uploaded to Moodle. You can find this information in LMS Course Development.

Print courses and other course documents such schedules, OLFM Guides, and other resources may be formatted Word documents which may then be converted to PDF. Below are the standard OL formatting guidelines for printable documents created in Word.

Print Document General Format

OL Styles Template

Before you begin working with your document, make sure the Document Template (the styles created and used by Production) has been loaded.

Add Templates button to Quick Access toolbar (Office 365):

  • Go to File/Options/Quick Access toolbar
  • Select All Commands from the dropdown, locate Templates in the list, click Add and then OK

Attach OL Styles template to document:

  • Save the File:OL STYLES DEC2014.zip file to your desktop and extract
  • Click on the Templates button and then Document Templates
  • Click the Attach button, select the OL_STYLES_DEC2014.dotx file and press Open
  • Check the Automatically update document styles option and press OK
  • OL styles should now be visible in the Style panel on the Home Ribbon

Page Layout

Note: Select Different Odd/Even Header, but DO NOT select Different First Page

Content Area

Document Title Pages

Standard Title Pages

Many of our course documents such as course reading PDFs and OLFM Guides require a basic OL title page that contains information such as the course code, course title, resource title, faculty name and possibly copyright credit details. To create these title pages, we use the OL Title Page Creator tab in Production Tools, app found in O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\SOFTWARE\PRODUCTION TOOLS. The Production Tools app allso allows us to bulk create resource title pages directly from a Copyright Report Excel document using the © Title Pages tab.

Note: For OLFM Guides, we insert "NOT FOR STUDENT USE" in the Item Number field when generating the title page.

TRU Brand Template Cover Page

The Print Material Branded Cover PDF below contains the front and back covers for material being printed at the Print Shop. You will need to download to your desktop so that form fields can be used.

Print Material Branded Cover PDFDownload

Placement (example below)

  • Front cover should appear as first page, followed by a blank page then regular the inside cover
  • Back cover should appear as last page, either one or two blank pages between it and the last page of content (one if last content page is even, two if last content page is odd)
Cover Placement ExampleDownload

item.title: MathType (Equations in Word)
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
Although Word has an equation editor built in, OL uses the program MathType within Word documents as the formatting transfers to Moodle accurately.

MathType should be loaded on your computer, and should show up in the Ribbon when you Open a Word document.

Shortcuts in MathType

Identifying a particular shortcut in Mathtype is simple and easy. Just hover over the item in which you want to know the shortcut, and the name as well as the shortcut will appear in the bottom-left status bar of the window.

item.title: Enhanced Course Guide/Course Outline Requests
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added information about file naming structure.
- Adjusted information and link to make it more clear where to find course code and consortium details in the Course Code Cross-Reference and Consortium PDF document and the TRUSpace Academic Calendar Archive.

Overview

Enhanced Course Guide (ECG)

  • Created once course is 'Signed Off', general overview of the course

Course Outline Request

  • Typically comes from Enrolment Services (ESO), they are requesting an Enhanced Course Guide
  • Locate or create if needed and email the appropriate ECG to ESO, according to the start date in D4P

Locate ECG for Course Outline Request

  1. Ensure you have either the student's start date or the month/year that the ESO's are requesting. Find out which version you need by searching D4P (eg. SW1, SW2, ON1 etc)
  2. Check Enhanced Course Guides-O365 Teams folder and download correct document. You may want to scroll alphabetically as the search function doesn't always work.
    • Review document and make sure the 'Course Reference' on the Copyright Page matches the version (SW1, SW2 etc)
    • Reply to the course outline request email and attach document, ensuring you include the JIRA task number in the subject. Do NOT send directly to the student.
  3. If you cannot locate the document in Teams, check Subversion.
  4. If you still cannot find the document, search JIRA to see if we have done this request before. If so, check outgoing OLProduction emails.
  5. An ECG can be created from a newer course by extracting Word content from the XML file in Subversion. The document will require formatting, which you can find below.
  6. If the request is for an older course guide, the course code may have changed, or it may have been through another institution, which is referred to as a consortium course. There are a few way to find this information:
    • Start by searching in D4P and it should show you the new course code if it has been updated.
    • If no results come up in D4P, refer to the Course Code Cross-Reference and Consortium List to find the updated code or consortium institution details.
    • If we still can't locate the course files/info, refer to the TRUSpace Academic Calendar Archive, locate the corresponding calendar year and course information.
  7. To search for the course guide (specifically for older courses):
    • Start your search in O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\COMPLETED
    • Continue to O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\GROUPWISE EXPORT if nothing is found
    • If we still can't find anything start a File Explorer search of the entire O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES directory (Note: When searching for files there is no space between acronym and number in the folder/file (eg. BIOL3001))
    • The document will need to be cleaned up and/or formatting. Ask if you are unsure.

IMPORTANT: Please review ECG documents for formatting/setup issues, missing information or any other concerns as the files are being sent to other institutions. If changes are required, please update both Subversion and the shared teams version.

Create/Format Enhanced Course Guide

UPDATED: CSAs now format the ECG documents after course sign off. Production will continue to create older ECG files when requested by other departments.

New/Maintenance/Amendment Courses

  • Create an unformatted ECG document using XML to Print with the sections noted below and a PDF title page
  • Include the unformatted ECG file and title page in the standard OLFM Guide communication to the CSAs. CC OL Production to generate a Jira task to be added to the main course task and assign to yourself.
  • We can complete the course clean up process and close the main course task. Keep ECG task open until CSAs send back file.
  • Once files received, commit to Subversion, comment on task and close.

External ECG Requests for Older Courses

For older courses, Production uses the XML to Print tool to create, format and save the ECG documents using the following details:

Content Required

  • Title Page (Course Guide)
  • Copyright (should fit on one page)
  • Table of Contents
  • All current Course Guide sections
  • Course Overview
    • Unit/Module Title
    • Overview
    • Learning Outcomes

Formatting Steps

  1. Remove Excess Content (Word Outline Mode)
    • Remove all content in each Module/Lesson/Unit after Learning Outcomes - content left will include Module Title, Overview heading/para's, Learning Outcomes heading/para's
      NOTE: if Course Summary option used in XML to Print then delete course content between end of Course Guide and start of Course Summary. Some clean up of content may be required within Course Summary.
  2. Adjust Structure (Word Outline Mode)
    • Move Copyright & Credits to front of document (use Word Outline Mode)
    • Adjust headings (use Word Outline Mode)
      • Course Overview (Heading Level 1)
      • Module Number/Title (Heading Level 2)
      • Overview & Learning Outcomes (Heading Level 3)
  3. Adjust Page Structure
    • Set Header/Footers to be 0.75"/0.5" , set Different Odd and Even Pages
    • Add Next Page Section Break before Copyright & Credits for Title Page
    • Add Odd Page Section Break after Copyright & Credits for Table of Contents page
    • On Table of Contents Page:
      • Use Formatting Style Normal for Table of Contents heading (so it doesn't show up in Navigation Pane), Arial 18pt, bold, 6pt before 12pt after
      • Add a couple of para breaks, then another Odd Page Section Break (this break should land you on first page of Course Guide)
    • Unlink Title Page, Copyright page, Table of Content Headers and Footers. Make sure first and second page of Course Guide are unlinked (since using Different Odd and Even Pages)
    • Link all subsequent Headers and make sure Page Numbering is continuous  from page 1 onwards
    • Odd Page header (beginning on first page of Course Guide after Table of Contents):
      • Left Side - Course Code: Course Title, right alignment tab, Page Number
    • Even Page header:
      • Left Side - Page Number, right alignment tab, Course Guide
  4. Content Clean Up
    • Use Print Formatting Guide
    • Quickly run through and add page breaks or make spacing adjustments so it looks professional
    • If Course Summary had not be created in XML to Print then Add Level 1 Heading: Detailed Module/Lesson/Unit Outcomes (adjust to match term used in course) just above first section of summary content
    • Add: "Course Reference: Course Code Master Number " to copyright page between development team and address (eg. Course Reference: ANES 4011 SW1) - this may be present already.
  5. Final Steps
    • Insert a Custom Table of Contents - to 2 levels, format according to print standards

Saving Enhanced Course Guide

  1. Use the following naming convention with underscore, no spaces for all ECG documents, both Word and PDF: ABCD1234_SW#_ECG.docx (Adjust version type to SW, ON or PT as needed). For example PSYC1111_SW3_ECG.docx/.pdf.
  2. Save as Adobe PDF, create a Title Page, merge the documents, and upload to Teams folder. Commit Word copy of ECG to Subversion.

Note: If you see files in Teams that have spaces instead of underscore, please update as needed to help maintain the correct order.

Removing Student Data From ECG Request Jira Items

It's important to remove any student information included with request such as first name, last name, T-ID #, email address, etc. from the Jira task before sending out the file/communication as we do not what to keep those details stored in Jira.

  • Review the task title and body for student information
  • Delete or replace all student details with XXXXXXXXXXX
  • Click the Automation dropdown and select the Remove Student Data (History) option. This will delete the current task and you'll receive a notification in the Jira Notifications area that a new task has been created and assigned to you.
  • Double-check that all student data has been removed
  • Include the new work item number (e.g. [OLCONT-1235]) in the email subject and cc the inbox to capture the communication when sending out.
