item.title: Quality Assurance Check - Web
item.dc:creator: bforsyth
item.content:encoded:
To Start Quality Assurance Check

Once all internal review changes have been completed (Moodle and XML) and committed to Subversion, a quality assurance check will be completed by the Production Supervisor. To assign in JIRA, change the workflow status of the course task to "Quality Assurance." A "QA feedback" subtask will automatically be generated and assigned to the Production Supervisor. Be sure to add any information you deem relevant in the description field of the subtask.

Completing Quality Assurance Changes

Quality assurance feedback is given using Hypothesis, a web annotation tool. When you receive the QA feedback subtask back, it will include a link to join a Hypothesis group specific to the course you are working on.

Here's a quick overview of Hypothesis annotation basics before getting started.

You may approach making changes in one of two ways. First, you may refer to feedback on the Hypothesis group page while making changes to Moodle in a separate window.

Alternatively, you may select "Visit annotations in context" to open that specific Moodle page in a new tab.

An annotation sidebar will appear on the Moodle page and content will be highlighted where annotations occur. Note that only one annotation will be included when the page is first opened. To view all annotations on the page, selected "Show all."

Note: Similar to the Internal Review updates, it is extremely important that all course material changes are captured in the XML as that file becomes the master document for Open Learning and will be used for future revisions of the course.

item.title: External Review & Sign Off - Web
item.dc:creator: bforsyth
item.content:encoded:
To Start External Review

Once all quality assurance changes have been completed, you may email the course lead (Instructional Designer or Curriculum Services) to notify them the course is ready for external review. An example of an email communication is shown below. You may also include any pending questions that need to be clarified.

In Jira, create an External Review subtask, assign it to yourself, add your email content to the description and include the PROD number in the email subject similar to the example below.

Subject: ABCD 1234 Master No - Ready for External Review - [PROD-#####]

Hello,

Course ABCD 1234 is ready for external review: Container Name goes here.
[If there is a Print version of the course, please give a brief status update (e.g. I'm current formatting the material, the course is currently in QA review, etc. just so the Course Lead is aware. It's common for the SW version of a course to be signed off before the PT version is complete.]

Attached is the OLFM Guide/Material OR We did not receive any OLFM Guide.

Please send all changes to OlProduction, attn. your Name

Thank you, Your Name

Receiving Course Sign Off

Once sign off has been received, there are a few final steps required:

  1. Add sign-off communication task to main course as an External Communication subtask
  2. Update main Jira task status to Sign Off Received
  3. Send OLFM material and unformatted Enhanced Course Guide material (XML to Print) to CSAs (csa@tru.ca - example communication):
    • An Enhanced Course Guide subtask will automatically be generated once the main course task workflow has been changed to "Sign Off Received." Refer to the Enhanced Course Guide/Course Outline Request page for further information on creation and saving of Enhanced Course Guides. We'll keep this task open until we receive the formatted files back and upload them to Subversion.
    • OLFM material may include OLFM Guide and/or additional files, alternate assignments, etc. If no OLFM material, we still send note to CSAs letting them know. They don't need to know if there is no alternate assignments. Log communications in JIRA task.
  4. Complete the Course File Cleanup process.
  5. Update D4P with 100% and Course Signed Off
  6. Add final comment to main course task "Course sign-off received, file clean up complete, and D4P updated. We can then close the main course task.

item.title: Moodle Course Development Overview and Workflow
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Course Development Overview

The bulk of Production's role is to take course content that is provided (usually in Word format) and transform that content into an online Moodle course using various processes and tools. Click through the following image gallery for a brief overview of what this process looks like:

Production receives Word documents that we then adjust the heading structure and other content to generate the XML structure and tags needed.

Using an application, we convert the Word to XML format and continue to make the necessary adjustment in order to convert the course to HTML and then into compatible Moodle backup package format with additional desktop and web tooks.

Using the Moodle backup file we can then import our course content directly into Moodle and the structure we started with in Word/XML will now be transferred over to Moodle (Tabs, Assignments, Books, etc.)

We confirm the content has transferred properly and is displaying correctly based on the original document provided, and then have team members review the material and provide feedback and adjustment (Internal and Quality Assurance Reviews).

After the review steps, we send the course for final External Review and course sign-off, and the process starts again.

Development Process Videos

The following videos provide a look at the main Moodle course development process from EST perspective:

Production Training Video - Part 1: Word to XML

Production Training Video - Part 2: Copyright, XML to Moodle

Production Training Video - Part 3: Moodle Setup

Course Development Workflow

Course Task Assigned in JIRA

  • Review course task details provided in Jira
  • Send out Starting Work communication using Outlook (Reminder: Always send course communication from olproduction@tru.ca)
  • Assign Exam Status task to Jenn with details related to Final Exams, Midterms, Practice Exams, etc. or note that there are is no Final Exam for a course.

Word To XML

  • Pull course files from Subversion
  • Quick review of overall course materials, structure, Production notes, additional resource files, etc.
  • Begin formatting of Word document, adjusting heading levels to generate XML course structure, extracting images, etc.
  • Review Copyright Report and add all image captions/attributions, download external resources (often PDFs) and link directly in Word (this will save future steps in XML)
  • Once basic formatting is complete, we use an application called QuickTagIt to convert our structured Word files to XML

Note: You can start to format your document, save and quickly script to XML to see if you're getting the required XML structure for the OL course. Scripting at this stage take minimal time and will help spot initial problems before moving to the next step.

XML to Moodle

  • We complete a content review to make sure the XML formatting matches the Word document formattings as much as possible (heading levels, list, links, media, etc.) and adjust where needed
  • Ensure all file resources (images, files, etc.) have been added
  • Review all included Production notes to ensure they have been addressed
  • Once our course XML is formatted and structured, we convert the XML to HTML, which we then convert to a Moodle backup package that can be easily uploaded in to Moodle

Note: All copyrighted content (images, captions, attributions, PDFs, etc.) should be included in the XML before moving to Moodle.

Moodle Setup

  • Create a Moodle course container if needed. Details included in JIRA course task.
  • Adjust course container settings, added additional Moodle users, and self-enrollment option
  • Import course content into Moodle
  • Complete a quick review of the imported course to make sure you have the intended course structure and formatting (Tabs, Books, etc.). Adjust XML, rescript to HTML and repackage if needed.
  • Set up course assessments (assignments, quizzes, etc.) and adjust settings to match our general OL settings or additional requested changes
  • Upload additional resource files as needed
  • Once the course is completely setup in Moodle, complete an in depth final review of the course content, settings, etc. before the Internal Review. Our goal is to have a minimal amount of errors at this stage.

Internal Review (IR)/Changes

  • For the Internal Review another EST will take an in depth view of the course material and compare the setup to the original document to ensure everything matches as close as possible.
  • Another member of the Production team will review the Moodle course setup, materials, assessments, etc. and compare with the course documents provided and add revisions and/or additional notes to the IR documents.
  • Assign the Exam Status task back to Jenn to let her know that the course has gone to internal review and also who the IR task was assigned to.
  • The IR task will be assigned back to you to update the course XML, Moodle and any other associated course material as needed
  • After the IR changes are complete, the course is now ready for the Quality Assurance review

Note: It is extremely important that all course material changes are captured in the XML as that file becomes the master document for Open Learning and will be used for future revisions of the course.

Quality Assurance (QA) Review/Changes

  • The QA Review is looking at the course setup as a whole, with a focus on assessments and consistency throughout the material.
  • The Production Supervisor will use Hypothes.is to add online notes to the course container with additional comments and summary included in the Jira task.
  • The QA task will be assigned back to you to update the course XML, Moodle and any other associated course material as needed
  • After the QA changes are complete, the course is now ready for the External Review

Note: Similar to above, it is extremely important that all course material changes are captured in the XML as that file becomes the master document for Open Learning and will be used for future revisions of the course.

External Review (ER)/Changes

  • After the review stages, we'll send the course out to the Course Lead for External Review. The communication will be sent to Curriculum Services (Naomi) for most maintenance and amendment revisions. For major revisions and new courses, the communication will be sent to the specific Instructional Designer.
  • Once the External Review revisions are received, we try to make the changes as quickly as possible and let the Course Lead know as soon as the adjustment have been made.

Course Sign-Off/Clean-up

  • After the External Review changes are complete, the Course Lead should send Production, Curriculum Services and other teams an official course sign-off email to let everyone know that the course is complete.
  • This communication is needed to trigger additional steps in other departments, so even if the Course Lead mention that the course is "ready to go" we will ask them to send out a sign-off communication.
  • After the sign-off email is received, we can proceed with the final course file clean up.

Jira Task Priorities

Courses are given a priority number in Jira when then are added to our course queue, but that that number does not necessarily reflect the order in which course tasks are completed due to various factors. There are times, we'll have courses with similar or lower numbers due to development delays that will need to move before higher numbered items.

One exception is the "Blocker" task, which is the one priority item that should be moved to the top of your list if you are assigned a task with that priority. It means Production has received instructions to move that task along quicker than our other tasks.

Task Order of Precedence

Our goal is to move the various course development steps along as efficiently as possible, which means we may need to switch tasks throughout the day depending on the items assigned to us. Here's an approximate order in which we want to complete the tasks as they are received.

Feel free to touch base with the Production Supervisor if you have any questions about which items to work on first.

  1. Blocker Priority Task: These can be course tasks or other specific items from this list that need to be completed before any other items.
  2. External Review Changes: Once External Review changes are received, we want to get them integrated into the course as soon as possible so that the course can be signed off.
  3. QA Changes: We want to get the QA changes implemented into the course, so we can send out the External Review communication.
  4. Internal Review Changes: Once the Internal Review notes are received from another EST, we want to complete those revisions in order to move the course to the QA stage.
  5. Internal Review/Exam Review: When you receive an Internal or Exam Review, it's best to save your current task in a spot that makes the most sense (e.g. finish formatting a section, complete the IR changes you were working on, etc.) and start the review.
  6. Course Sign-off/Clean Up: This item is lower priority, but an important step as we wrap up a course. Optimally, this task will be completed with-in a day or two of receiving the course sign-off.
  7. Formatting Course Material: This where a bulk of Production time is spent, even through it's lower on the priority list. This includes all the various steps from Word to Moodle. If there's ever a time when you feel that you're not able to get to course formatting for longer periods of time due to other tasks, please reach out to the Production Supervisor to review current workload.
  8. Content Support Task: These are often lower priority, quick tasks (Course Guide request, minor material adjustments, etc.) that we can complete within a few days of receiving the task. We often try to slot these in between the items above.

item.title: Moodle Rubric/Marking Guide Setup & Settings
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent update:
- Additional information regarding Rubric setup and settings

Should I Use a Rubric or Marking Guide?

Setting Up a Rubric

Important: Rubrics must have a final column worth "0" marks to ensure the grade is calculated correctly. Contact the Course Lead and suggest a "0 Marks, Did not submit column" if needed.

  • To attach a rubric to an already created assignment, go to the Edit settings menu in the Assignment.
  • From there go to the Grade section and set Grading method to Rubric.
  • Select "Save and display" to exit the Edit settings menu. This will take you to the Assignment Page.
  • Go to Advance grading and select Rubric
  • From this point you will have the option of "Define new grading from scratch" to create a new Rubric or "Create new grading from template" to select an already created rubric.
    • Select Define new grading from scratch if you wish to create a new rubric
    • Select Create new grading from template if you wish to use a previously created rubric:
  • Add Criterion, description and marks as provided to match the assignment instructions
  • Adjust the rubric settings to match the screenshot below and click the Save button

Setting up a Marking Guide

  • Select the Advanced Grading option near the top of the Assignment page
  • From the drop-down menu, select Marking Guide and either define new guide or create from template.
  • Once the Marking Guide is set up, click the Save marking guide and make it ready button

Changing Advanced Grading Type

***IN PROGRESS***

  • Is possible to change as long as info/marks match
  • Do no use regrade option when saving new type
  • Students will no longer be able to see marking guide/rubric feedback, only the "Feedback comments" section and total marks.

item.title: Student Instructions for Writing Final Exam
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
LMS Instructions

If a course contains a final exam then there should be instructions setup for how student can go about and ask to write final. These instructions occur in two locations:

  1. Course Guide: Assessments Section
  2. Final Exam Tab

Course Guide: Assessments Section

Within the Course Guide/Assessment section, there should be a heading for the Final Exam. Under this heading there should be information that describes the exam. This can range from one line to a number of paragraphs. There are no restrictions on this content. What is there will depend on the developer, of course.

After the information about exam, there should be a line that states:

Please see Final Exam Tab in your course for instructions on arranging to write the final exam. (note bold font)

That line should be the only information about writing the exam - any content about contacting exams@tru.ca etc. should be removed.

Final Exam Tab

Updates, pending.

Open Book Invigilated Exam:

Example Course: DEV_OL NRSC 3201_SW1 – Silviculture

Materials Permitted
  • This is an open-book exam
  • Textbook and notes
  • Non-programmable calculator

Online materials or electronic devices are NOT allowed at any time.

If you encounter technical issues during your exam, you must notify ProctorU immediately so that they can assist you in resolving the issue. If you are unable to resolve the issue with ProctorU, you must let exams@tru.ca know right away. PLEASE DO NOT submit any exam questions or files via email to your Open Learning Faculty Member. Exam questions MUST be submitted inside the final exam in Moodle. Any emailed work WILL NOT be graded.

Print Instructions

Course Guide: Assessments Section #

Similar to Moodle, within the Course Guide/Assessment section, there should be a heading for the Final Exam. Under this heading there should be information that describes the exam. This can range from one line to a number of paragraphs. There are no restrictions on this content. What is there will depend on the developer, of course.

After the information about exam, there should be a line that states: The Exam for this course will be a paper exam that will need to be taken prior to your course completion date and at an approved testing location.  You will be responsible for any associated fees.

Please contact exams@tru.ca a minimum of one month prior to when you would like to take the exam.  They will help you determine options in your area and guide you on how to schedule your exam.

item.title: Paper Exam Forms Internal Review Process
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
he following are the basic steps in reviewing Final Exams Paper Forms.

Before You Begin

Make sure you have the correct source files:

  • Final Exams/Practice Exams - Look in the Subversion/Exams/Content folder for the course \Working\For IR  - if files are not there, please ask person sending to put in. IR sub-task should clearly state what you are expected to review and what files you should find
  • Final Exams will be either a "pool" document or an individual Form. The files with the Form letter are the print exam.

Note: for most IR's you are not adjusting errors you are seeing, you are documenting. There are exceptions - extra assessments we do that are not part of curriculum development cycle - clarify with person who sends you review. Exam Form check

Exam Form Check

  1. Check front page block
    • Make sure correct course code/title/exam form listed
    • Make sure time correct (look at older exam)
    • Make sure materials Permitted/Provided are correct
    • Make sure total marks are correct (add up exam)
    • Make sure total pages is correct (look at total number of pages in file)
    • Make sure instructions at bottom of page are correct
  2. Exam content
    • Make sure header is correct: course code, form, page of total pages format and total pages are correct
    • Make sure headings are structured (look at navigation panel) and formatted
    • Make sure total marks per section are given
    • Make sure questions are sequentially numbered
    • Make sure sub-parts are clearly labelled using list structure (indented)
    • Make sure no answers are shown!!!
    • Make sure page breaks are logical
    • Make sure final page has "END OF FINAL EXAMINATION"
    • Make sure any extra materials are provided - answer keys, readings etc.

Note: Formatting in general is very similar to our course print standards

Exam Key check

  1. Make sure title page matches exam - title and form
  2. Make sure question numbering matches up to exam
  3. Make sure same formatting as exam with exception that answers should be typically be underneath each question in bold.

item.title: Open Learning Faculty Member Guides (OLFMG)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added information in the first section to keep all active links in the OLFMG document blue.

Open Learning Faculty Member Guides (OLFMG) are documents that are provided during course development that often include some general course information (Course Guide), specific instructions for Open Learning Faculty Members and assignment/assessment answer keys. Our OLFM Guide documents are kept in the Subversion OLMFG folder.

Editors and Course IDs work together to create the OLFM Guide document, and if we don't have a file in Subversion, we'll often touch base with the Editor or ID to see if there is a document available.

During the course development process, Production may need to:

  • Format the document to our OL print standards
  • Keep ALL external links in blue text. If needed there is a Word macro to make all active links blue in the Production Software and Web Applications section.
  • Copy/paste answer keys into the OLFMG document
  • Update OLFMG document to ensure it matches the Moodle course material/changes (often around the Course Guide and Assessments)

Note: The OLFMG document should be fully formatted (title page, copyright, table of contents, etc.) and up-to-date before sending the course to QA Review.

Once a course is signed-off, we'll send the OLFM Guide to the Curriculum Support Associates to be distributed to the course OLFMs. There is an example of what that email looks like in the Course Communications section.

Additional Information for OLFM

In some instances, we insert additional information for OLFMs to provide clarity regarding course setup and function. This is often around assignments and quizzes. Below are examples of text we can insert into the OLFMG document as noteboxes to provided helpful details.

Quizzes

Note: Some question types in this quiz require manual grading and answers are provided in Moodle where needed. After quiz completion and marking, students can see ****confirm review options****

Auto-graded Quizzes

Note: These quizzes are automatically graded in Moodle, but attempts should be reviewed regularly. Answers are provided in Moodle if needed.

Auto-graded Quizzes with Randomized Attempts

Note: Students receive a randomized set of ## questions for each attempt, and the order will not match what is presented below. These quizzes are automatically graded in Moodle, but attempts should be reviewed regularly. Answers are provided in Moodle if needed.

Assignments With Alternate versions

Note: This course includes alternate (ALT) assignment instruction for instances where another submission is required, but new assignment material is required. The ALT assignments are included on the Assignment/Assessment tab and are currently hidden from student view. Use the Participants/Groups settings to allow access to specific students.

  • Navigate to the Participants section, click the Gear icon and select Groups
  • Select the Group/ALT assignment you want to make visible for the student(s) and click the Add/remove users button
  • Select the student(s) details in the right-hand column and click the Add button.
  • All students in a group will have access to that corresponding ALT assignment

Once a student has been added to a Group, you can direct the student to the ALT assignment instructions and allow another submission on the corresponding assignment activity.

Assignments As Quizzes

Note: Many of the course assignments are completed using the Moodle Quiz activity. Students receive a randomized set of questions for each attempt, and the order will not match what is presented below. Answers are provided in Moodle where needed.

WeBWorK

Table of Content Notebox

Add the following notebox to the Table of Contents under the WeBWorK heading/reference:
IMPORTANT: Before you access your Moodle course, please review the WeBWorK section for more information.

Example

WeBWorK Section

Add the following table/notebox at the beginning of the WeBWorK section:

IMPORTANT:
You need to log in directly to your WeBWorK course at webwork.tru.ca using the provided username and password, then change your password in the User Settings section. After that, you can access your WeBWorK course through Moodle or the webwork.tru.ca.

  • Each WeBWorK course has its own separate account. This means your account for one course won't work for another, and it's not connected to your regular TRU account.
  • You need to access your WeBWorK course directly from the course list at webwork.tru.ca first. Do not try to go through Moodle until this step is complete.
  • To access your WeBWorK course, you'll need to log in using the username and password you were given. Once you're in, the first thing you should do is change your password in the User Settings to something you'll remember.
  • After you've logged in directly to your WeBWorK course for the first time, you can then access the WeBWorK course through either Moodle or the course link on webwork.tru.ca.
  • You can find more information on accessing and using WeBWorK in the OLFM WeBWorK Instructions & Resources in Moodle.

item.title: Moodle Blocks Setup and Settings
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Moodle Blocks Area

A block contains features/tools that loads in the right-hand side of a Moodle.

These blocks are automatically inserted with the Moodle Course Packager, but the following block requires additional setup once the course is uploaded to Moodle.

Key Course Milestones (Completion Progress) Block

The Key Course Milestones block is a time-management tool for students and OLFMs, providing a visual representation of activities to be completed.

There are a few additional step to setup up the Key Course Milestones block:

  • Click gear icon in the block and select Configure Completion Progess block
  • In the Blocks settings section, click the Show more link to view additional options
  • Adjust the following settings as needed
    • Alternate title: Key Course Milestones
    • Activities included: Selected Activities
    • Select activities: Highlight all assessed (marked) activities including Assignments, Quizzes, Discussions, etc., except for the Final Exam
  • Once the changes are complete, scroll to the bottom of the pages and click Save changes

item.title: WeBWorK Course Container Creation and Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Development Container

  • Login to Course Administration area: https://webwork.tru.ca/webwork2/admin/
  • Select the Add Course menu option and use the following settings/options:
    • Course ID: Similar naming convention to Moodle, but no spaces. E.g. DEV_OL_ABCD1234_SW4
    • Course Title: Add the full course title. E.g. Linear Algebra
    • Institution: TRU-OL
    • To add the WeBWorK administrators to the new course (as administrators) check the box below: Ensure both items checked.
    • To add an additional instructor: Leave blank for DEV. DEV users will be added once course is created to allow for single email message with details. More info below.
    • Copy templates from: select DEV OL Course Template
  • Confirm settings are correct and click the Add Course button

Adding Developers To Course

  • Login into WeBWork course and select Classlist Editor under Instructor Tools
  • Select Add from the options presented, input number of users required and click the Take Action! button
  • Input the following information:
    • Last Name
    • First Name
    • Student ID and Login Name - TRU network name or start of email address (Note: the username and password will be the same, and instructions are provided in the example communication to change their password immediately.)
    • Email Address
  • Confirm information is correct, select the Add Students button

Updating Developer Permissions

Note: Developers need to be added with WeBWorK admin permissions to be able to see Problem error messages.

Users are added to the course as students and developer permissions need to be updated to Professor.

  • Select Classlist Editor under Instructor Tools
  • Click the pencil icon next to the user to be updated
  • Select admin from the Permission Level drop-down menu
  • Click the Take Action! button to save changes

Example Developer Setup Communication

Subject: ABCD 1234 SW3 WeBWorK Login Information

Hello (Include Course Lead and all developers involved),

Here is the login information for the ABCD 1234 SW4 (INSERT COURSE INFO) WeBWorK development course:

URL: (INSERT LINK)

Developer Name
Username: (Insert Login Name from WeBWork)
Password: Same as username, please update on login.

Developer Name
Username: (Insert Login Name from WeBWork)
Password: Same as username, please update on login.

Note: Please update your password immediately after logging into WeBWorK. The Change Password option is located under the User Settings link in the left-hand menu.

If you have any difficulties logging in, please let us know. Thank you.

Live Container

IN PROGRESS

IMPORTANT T-ID needed for Moodle LTI to work (OLFMS)

Transfer of Courses Between Servers

Follow the instructions below should we need to import, export or transfer courses between servers.

WeBWork Course Export

  • Log into Server Admin and click on “Archive Courses”.
  • Select desired course(s) and click “Archive Courses”.
  • If the database structure is ok, click “Archive”.
  • Course(s) should now appear under “Archived Courses” on the Course Administration page. Click “Download/upload archived courses”.
  • Select desired course (you can only download one at a time) and click “Download”.
  • Course will download as a .tar.gz zipped file.

WeBWork Course Import

  • Click “Download/upload archived courses” under “Archived Courses” on the WeBWork DEV Server Admin page.
  • Select the .tar.gz archived course file you previously downloaded and click “Upload”.
  • Uploaded course(s) will now appear under “Archived Courses”.
  • Click “Unarchive Courses”.
  • Select the course you want to restore. If a new course name is required, tick the box next to “New Name” and type the updated course name. Click “Unarchive Course” when ready.
  • Click “Unarchive”.
  • The course will now appear in the Course list of the new server.

item.title: Print Proof Requests
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
For our print courses and in some cases for our print course amendments, we will require print proofs for the External Review. Once the QA Review changes are complete and the PDF files are ready for print, we can request the print proofs.

Requesting Print Proofs

EST Request for Course Print Proof

  1. In Jira, create a Request Print Proof subtask under the course/amendment you are working on
  2. In the description, note which files require a proof. Often these are:
    • Course Guide
    • Study Guide
    • Assignments
    • Readings
  3. Assign Print Proof task to Production Supervisor to compile the print instructions and email to Print Shop
  4. Production Supervisor will note Print Shop communication in task, organize print pickup/delivery to Course Lead and assign task back to EST once Course Lead has received the files.
  5. Print proof task can be closed by EST

Required Print Proof Information

When ordering from the Print shop, the following information is required:

  • Item number and title needs to be specified and should be included in the file name (e.g. PSYC1111_PT4_Study_Guide_206339.pdf)
  • Printing instructions for each item need to be specified, including:
    • Black and white or colour printing
    • Single/Double-sided printing
    • Binding type
    • Blue title page numbers (For Study Guide Module/Unit Title Pages)

Note on Colour Printing:
- If less than 10 pages than individual pages can be specified.
- Greater than 10 pages – full colour document

Example Instructions for a Print Item

Item XXXXXX Study Guide

  • Black/white
  • Double-sided
  • Saddle stitched
  • Blue title pages:  10, 23, 45, 59 (Provide page number in PDF file)

Print Item Binding Options:

Print Proof Communication to Print Shop

The print proof requests and files are sent directly to the Print Shop at printshop@tru.ca.

Example Email:

Email Subject: ABCD 1234 SW1 - Request for Print Proof - [PROD-12345]

Hello,

Can we please get print proofs for the following attached files:

Item XXXXXX Course Guide

  • Black/white
  • Double-sided
  • Saddle stitched

Item XXXXXX Study Guide

  • Colour
  • Double-sided
  • Coil bound
  • Blue title pages:  X,

Item XXXXXX Assignments File

  • Black/white
  • Double-sided
  • Saddle-stitched

Please let us know if you have any questions or concerns and if we could have them ready for pickup by Friday, July 15th, that would be great. Thank you!

Your Name

item.title: Fix My Course Overview and Tracking (JIRA)
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Overview

OL Production is tasked with maintaining both current Standard Web and Print courses and Fix My Course how we divide that work out in our department. Standard Web and Print course maintenance can include broken links, spelling, minor text adjustments, changes to assignments, quizzes, discussions, etc. and are most often initiated directly from the OLFMs by emails sent to fixmycourse@tru.ca. We are able to make minor fixes (spelling, broken links, etc.) without much external communication, but if the fix is significant we often work with Curriculum Services to determine how best to proceed and in some cases, fixes can become course amendments that are handled similar to our other course development tasks.

Fix My Course Does Not Handle the Following Items:
- Online-paced updates and fixes: These can be discussed with the Production Supervisor and will be moved to the correct Jira project (PROD
- Midterm, Practice and Final Exam updates and fixes

Fix My Course Synopsis and Jira Tracking

The basic process for Fix My Course is:

  • Email is received/task created in JIRA (ALIVE project)
  • We evaluate fix request to determine if it's possible to adjust without any feedback from external stakeholders (Other affected OLFMs, Curriculum Services, etc)
    • Basic Content Adjustment - Update course material (XML, Moodle, documents, etc.) and inform OLFMs once complete
    • Assessment (or larger) Adjustment - Prepare summary of request and send details for Curriculum services, proceed with adjustments as discussed (XML, Moodle, documents, etc.), and confirm with OLFMs once complete
  • Document in JIRA, log time and close task

JIRA Tracking

When a new fix request is logged into the system, it will go into the ALIVE Jira project queue.

  1. Select task then click 'Start Work' (don't forget to assigned to you). Clicking 'Start Work' will move the task to In Progress.
  2. Add the course number and update subject line, if necessary, to the summary for example: ABCD 1234 - Assignment 3 Mistakes.)
  3. Classify the Request Support Type (all tasks) and Originator (if not from OLFM of a Continuous Enrollment Course)

Request Support Type Field - select one

Originator (done via Components)

Not all issues will have components. They are being used to mark the exceptions of who is submitting content and a couple special situations of note.

Task Work Steps

From the 'In Progress' state you will start your investigation of the task:

  • Check D4P2 for the Modality(s) of the course and the latest version. (Note: some requests can pertain to previous version(s) that still has students taking it)
  • Identify effected course containers
  • Identify effected item numbers
  • Document full extent of the problem. If it goes beyond what was reported locate errors, take screen shots, find all instances. Remember: If the fix is simple and straightforward such as a broken url do check to see if it is in more than one location.
  • Use Workflow Options to help you manage status of task

Manage tasks by making on-going conversation sub-tasks to original request!

JIRA Workflow Options

Current Workflow for FixMyCourse. (Note: Production Supervisor set as Thomas Sandhoff, E-Learning Support Technician set as Alex Buckley)

item.title: Fix My Course Workflows
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added more information to the Fix Type: Assessment Adjustment regarding process and communication.

Evaluating Fix Request

  1. JIRA task created (Email received at fixmycourse@tru.ca and JIRA task created) - get into habit of using JIRA, using email only to reply or to get clarity on layout.
  2. Assess task to see if it should be in fixmycourse by gathering info from D4P
    • If fix is for Online paced course, notify OLFM that they are responsible for completing their own fixes, see the example provided in the Fix My Course Email Example section. NOTE: Generally online course fixes are completed by the OLFM, but there may be instances when we assist.
    • If it is a special case where we are assisting a Online Paced OLFM (ie: internal resource such as Barabus or PDF), move the task to the Production Project, and change the type to "Content Support". All future contact should then come from OLProduction@tru,ca
    • If fix is to an exam/midterm/practice exam - move to Exams project and assign to Exams Liaison Officer
    • If fix is for a course that has been signed off in last 3 months, move to Production and assign to EST who worked on course (task should be come sub-task of JIRA course task)
  3. If after evaluating, fix is still a fixmycourse task
    • Adjust subject line so that course code is stated at front (ABCD 1234 - description of fix); we want at front so it is easy to sort and see related issues
    • Tag with components to Identify Source of task (Faculty) & type of issue

NOTE: If after evaluating the fix request, it appears that an amendment may be required, we can note that in the communication back to Curriculum Services, so they are aware of the potential scope and determine how best to proceed. More information included in the Course Amendment Required section below.

Workflows Based on Fix Request Type:

Fix Type: Basic Content Adjustment (broken links, spelling, minor text adjustments)

  • Locate issue(s) in course content.
  • Update course documents (Word, PDF, XML, etc.)
  • If fix is more than just a basic adjustment, confirm fix with any other OLFMs before proceeding
  • Update master DEV container (Moodle)
  • Update LIVE containers (Moodle)
  • Notify affected Open Learning Faculty Members
  • Update JIRA and close task
  • Commit updated files to Subversion

Fix Type: Assessment Adjustment (assignment, quiz, discussion, anything graded)

NOTE: We need to contact Curriculum Services if there is going to be an direct impact on student grades (e.g. changing number of marks, weights, adding/remove questions, etc.) and for items that could potentially have indirect impact on student grades (e.g. changes to wording, spelling, and structure). When evaluating assessment requests, view the revision from a student perspective and ask if this change would effect the outcome of the assessment or if a student could say "I would have got a better mark if the change was previously made." For direct or potential indirect impacts to grades, we need summarize the request and other details below and contact Curriculum Services for feedback on how best to proceed. If unsure, touch base with the Production Supervisor or send to Curriculum Services for confirmation.

  • Prepare a summary for Curriculum Services and provide as much information as possible:
    • Course acronym, number and version (e.g. BIOL 2341 SW2)
    • Request details
    • Number of affected containers with names
    • Who initiated the request
    • Other affected OLFMs
    • Screenshots
    • Number of students who have completed assessment
    • Any other relevant information
  • IF requested by Curriculum Services: Email all OLFM(s) to inquire about adjusted marks and whether they notified students of the issue (example email). Notify Curriculum Services of their response.
  • Proceed as directed by Curriculum Services
  • Update course documents (Word, PDF, XML, etc.)
  • Update master DEV container (Moodle)
  • Update LIVE containers (Moodle)
  • Notify affected Open Learning Faculty Members of completion
  • Update JIRA and close task.
  • Commit updated files to Subversion

Fix Type: Print Course Documents

Some fix requests will affect our printed materials. This will affect the current stock and the document at the Print Shop. Some may be print based courses, some may be Standard Web with an optional printed Study Guide, and some may be offered in print and standard web modalities. If the fix involves an assessment, please see the Fix Type: Assessment Adjustment above.

  • Prepare summary for Curriculum Services (Provide as much information as possible: screenshots, documents, item number(s), etc.)
  • If the fix involves an assessment, a new item number may be needed. Curriculum Services will confirm.
  • Let Curriculum Services know if it is possible to sticker requested fix, or ask if we are just replacing the Printshop file. A sticker file will be sent to the appropriate CA.
  • If older document, replace with new TRU-OL cover page
  • Send updated file to the Printshop. (Example emails)
  • Update JIRA and move task to "Work Complete"
  • Commit updated files to Subversion

Type of Fix: Minor Typographical

Type of Fix: Multiple/Major Changes - Complex changes

Special Considerations

Waiting for More Information (Non-urgent/Minor Fixes)

Often Fix My Course receives request to fix minor items like broken links or other minor adjustments, but more information is required. We can spend a short amount of time looking for alternative resources/fix, but ultimately that information should be provided by the requestor. These types of requests can start to stack up in Fix My Course if we don't receive a response and here's the process to review, follow up and close tasks where no additional information has been provided:

NOTE: Major fixes that affect the student progress or assessments should continue to be followed-up on until addressed/fixed.

  • Spend a few minutes to see if we can find an alternate link/resource by title (the Wayback machine is useful http://web.archive.org/) send for confirmation or request they find/sent one
  • Follow up after 7 days
  • If still no response, follow up after another 7 days
  • Wait another 7 days and, if not a critical fix/resource, close the task after three weeks and note that no response received.
  • If it's critical, loop Curriculum Services in after the first two follow-ups, provide summary of request and ask how best to proceed

Course Amendment Required

If after evaluating the fix request, it is determined by either Fix My Course or Production that a requested course adjustment does not fit within the scope of standard changes (usually around assessments) we'll need to forward the information to Curriculum Services to evaluate, suggest we proceed with a course amendment and request Curriculum Services contacts olproduction@tru.ca to generate the amendment task. The email communication should include:

  • Course acronym, number and version (e.g. BIOL 2341 SW2)
  • Who initiated the request
  • Summary of request details
  • Screenshots
  • Number of affected containers with names
  • Other affected OLFMs
  • Number of students who have completed assessment
  • Any other relevant information
  • A request that Curriculum Services send a communication to olproduction@tru.ca to generate a course amendment task if required.

Depending on the Curriculum Services response:

  • If Curriculum Services determines an amendment is required, please let the Production Supervisor know an amendment in incoming, add a quick comment to the Fix My Course task (e.g. Curriculum Services proceeding with amendment, no further Fix My Course adjustments required), log time and request OL Production supervisor convert the task to an amendment.
  • If Curriculum Services determines the requested changes can be made without a course amendment, we can proceed with the updates through Fix My Course

OLFM Guide Changes

OLFM Guide changes require notifying sending the residing CSA an updated copy of the OLFM Guide as well as notifying them of the changes and whether a copy has been given to the OLFMs.

General Notes

Subversion/Course Files

  • Ensure the XML file is located in the root directory of the course
  • Edits only need to be completed in the XML file (except when documents are provided to students: eg. Suggested Schedule, Module PDF, Course Units, Assignments, etc.)
  • Move original Word files to new folder called "SOURCE FILES - USE XML"
  • Add comment with JIRA task name and number when committing to Subversion

Online Course Fixes

Generally, Online course fixes are not completed by Fix My Course, and we can send the standard Request from Online Paced OLFM message located in the Fix My Course Email Example section.

  • Exceptions – If it is a TRU resource (Barabus server, internal link, PDF)
  • In the case of a PDF the OLFM has two options:
    • They can contact FixMyCourse and describe the changes they would like made to the PDFs, and we will update accordingly.
    • We can provide the OLFM with the Word documents for the resources so that they can make adjustments themselves. Then, they can either convert to PDF and upload to the course, or they can send the adjusted documents back to us and we will do so.


When a fix comes from an outside source for an Online course, please draft an email with text similar to below, do not send the Online Fix My Course Message:

We have received the following email from (abc) notifying us of (...). If you would like to provide an alternative to this for your students, you should go into your course and do so, as this is part of your responsibility and opportunity when you teach an online course. FixMyCourse typically does not get involved in these updates, if any technical help is needed you can contact the E-Learning Facilitator at Elearningfacilitator@tru.ca.

item.title: Fix My Course Email Examples
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Example Emails

The email examples are a collection of emails that have gone out to OLFMs repeatedly. All emails should be sent from fixmycourse@tru.ca.

Assessment Fix OLFM Information Request

Standard email sent to OLFM(s) when a fix request involves an assessment (NOTE: should only be sent when requested by Curriculum Services):

Hello,

Thank you for your request regarding [COURSE NUMBER]. Because this change involves an assessment, we will need some additional feedback from all current Open Learning Faculty Members to pass along to Curriculum Services for review before proceeding with any changes to the course material. When you have a moment, can you please let us know:

  1. Have any students grades been adjusted/compensated due to this issue?
  2. Have you been advising students of the issue in the course material?

Your answers to the questions above will help Curriculum Services determine whether a new session is required, or if any additional steps are needed to help avoid student appeals. Thank you again.

Course Amendment Suggested/Required

This communication can be dynamic depending on the fix request and various factors involved. Our main goal is to provide Curriculum Services with as much information as possible to make an informed decision. Our communication should contain much of the following information below as needed:

  • Course acronym, number and version (e.g. BIOL 2341 SW2)
  • Who initiated the request
  • Summary of request details
  • Screenshots
  • Number of affected containers with names
  • Other affected OLFMs
  • Number of students who have completed assessment
  • Any other relevant information
  • A request that Curriculum Services send a communication to olproduction@tru.ca to generate a course amendment task if required.

Printshop Files

The following templates are to be used when a fix request involves printed documents.

New Item Number

New item number, but document is basically the same as previous version

Send To: Printshop and CSA

Subject Line: ABCD 1234 – New Item Number

Hello,

Because of a content change we have had to create a new item number for this course. Please use the attached file for all future printing.

Item: [number] [title] Printing Instructions: Please use the same printing instructions as for Item [number][title] which this item replaces.

Thanks

File Replacement

Replacing document with minor changes

Send To: Printshop and CSA

Subject Line: ABCD 1234 – replacement file

Hello,

Because of a [typographical error/minor content change] we need to update the file you currently have. Please use the attached file for all future printing. Total pages [has/has not] changed.

Item: [number] [title]

Thanks

Online Paced Course Fix Request

Request from Online Paced OLFM

Good morning/afternoon OLFMGNAME,

Thank you for your inquiry and for keeping the course content current. Please feel free to make any updates to the following items to ensure the course remains accurate and relevant for students in the online-paced format:

  • Replacing or updating broken links
  • Revising the wording of content (if it does not affect assessments or learning outcomes)
  • Adding new material (please note that third-party material uploaded to Moodle will need clearance from the Intellectual Property Office at copyright@tru.ca)
  • Updating to a new edition of the core textbook

You are welcome to make these changes directly in your online-paced Moodle course without needing to contact fixmycourse@tru.ca, olenvironmentdev@tru.ca or curriculumservices@tru.ca.

If you're unsure about how to proceed with any of the changes listed, the OLFM Hub resource in Moodle (https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=45196) is a great place to start. Should you need further assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out to moodlesupport@tru.ca, they’ll be happy to guide you through the process.

Thanks again for your attention to the course content.

Request from Online Paced OLFM - Detailed/Not Used Often

The following is the general response to OLFMs teaching online courses and looking for Fix My Course assistance:

Hello,

We have received your request to make a fix/change to your course.

As your course is being offered in an Online modality, you are responsible for making changes to your course container as per your contract agreement to keep the course current and accurate.

For your reference, please note the following from the Collective Agreement which explains what can and cannot be changed without approval from Curriculum Services:

Article 8.2
(1) The Role and Responsibilities of the Online Open Learning Faculty Member
c) To update course materials as needed or at least at the end of each course offering to ensure currency of the course materials.

(7) Course Maintenance and Revision
a) Open Learning Faculty Members are responsible as part of their regular duties to maintain all course material on a regular basis to ensure accuracy and currency. This work does not involve prior approval from the Employer.
b) Open Learning Faculty Members must obtain prior approval from the Employer for any changes to course materials that would involve altering the learning outcomes, course structures, evaluation weightings, evaluation method(s), evaluation instrument(s), workload for the Open Learning Faculty Member or the students, or copyrighted third party material.

Therefore, allowable content changes include:

  • Replacing/updating broken links
  • Changing wording of content (with no impact on Assessment weightings)
  • Adding new material (third party material will require clearance from Intellectual Property Office copyright@tru.ca )
  • Course updates to a new edition of the core textbook

All of the allowable content changes can be made without contacting fixMyCourse@tru.ca or curriculumservices@tru.ca. For technical assistance while you are making these changes to your container, you may contact the Open Learning E-Facilitator ([mailto:elearningfaciltator@tru.ca).

Content changes described in Article 8.2(7)(b) require prior approval, so please contact Curriculum Services if you are concerned with any of the areas (curriculumservices@tru.ca). These areas cannot be changed while a cohort is in progress. They include changes to:

  • learning outcomes
  • course structures
  • evaluation weightings
  • evaluation methods(s)
  • evaluation instrument(s)
  • workload for the Open Learning Faculty Member or the students
  • copyrighted third party material

Thank you for your attention to these matters.

CurriculumServices

OLProduction

item.title: Course Information Sheet (CIS) Maintenance
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent changes: Updated CIS Document Management section to reflect updates to D4P process

Overview

Course Information Sheets (CIS) are the HTML files that appear in the TRU-OL Course Search at the following location: http://www.tru.ca/distance/courses/

The content of a Course Information Sheet is maintained by the respective Curriculum Assistant for that course area. Information is compiled in a standard format Word Document. This Word Document is passed to Olproduction to convert to XML which is converted automatically to HTML on the tru.ca web server.

A Curriculum Assistant sends required information to the OLCISupdates email which is autologged to JIRA as a CIS task. The task summary should specify when the updated CIS is needed to be uploaded to the TRU website, eg: "FREN 1011 - CIS for upload today". (NOTE: Do not upload earlier than the day specified.) Within the task there will be an attached Word Document with all necessary updates shown using Track Changes.

Requirements

  1. Access to D4P
  2. FileZilla Installed with server connection setup (user name/psswd) (Or any other SFTP tool, Login provided by IT)
  3. OxygenXML editor with OL templates installed (see Oxygen XML Editor) if there are file errors

CIS Files Location

  1. The current CIS information is hosted directly in D4P, where they are edited
  2. The CIS files exported from D4P are found in the following folder with O drive: O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\CIS\_CIS_XML

FTP Setup

  • Download an FTP application such as Filezilla or WinSCP
  • Open the application, add the server information and login credentials and connect to the server
  • Confirm you have access to the CIS upload directory: home/olhistweb/courses/cisdata/xml/

CIS Document Management

Updating CIS Documents

To update and upload a course information sheet for a TRU course, follow the steps outlined below:

  1. Locate the course in D4P
  2. Click the Edit Offline Master CIS button in the Course Information Sheets (CIS) section
  3. Add latest History note to the Update Comment text box
  4. Based on the provided Word document, make any required changes to the CIS CONTENT section. Use the existing structure as a guide for inserting or removing information.
  5. Once the CIS information has been properly updated, click the Save CIS button and then the Export XML button to general the file needed for upload.
  6. Save a copy of the exported XML to O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\CIS_CIS_XML and overwrite the file in the folder as needed.
  7. Using FTP upload the XML to /home/olhistweb/courses/cisdata/xml/ on the TRU website. To do this you need permissions on server, if you do not have then you will need to ask someone who does to do upload. Currently Jennifer, Carolyn, Klaudia, Alex, Sean, and Thomas have permissions.

CIS Paper Only Exam Note

There are a handful of OL courses that can only have a paper final exam, and that information is highlighted on the course CIS above the assessment table with the following wording:

Note: The final exam for this course is only available as a paper exam and must be taken in person at an approved Testing Centre. Please email exams@tru.ca with any questions.

Important: The paragraph must start with "Note:" or it will not be highlighted on the website.

This note applies to the following courses/CIS documents:

Creating a New CIS Document

For a new CIS files, send course acronym, course name, credit amount to Sean Mauricio and ask it to be added to search, or it won't show up on the TRU website. Sean can also remove Courses from the course search if required. If Sean is not available, Carolyn or Thomas can also can update.

  1. Find similar course, copy/paste it and rename to new course.
  2. Update the meta tag to be the most recent information. (History will be documented with commits to git repository.
  3. Based on the Word Doc, make any required changes to the course's .xml file. Use the existing tag structure as a guide for inserting or removing information.
  4. Once the .xml file has been properly updated, save file.
  5. Using FTP, upload the XML to to /home/olhistweb/courses/cisdata/xml/ on the TRU website. To do this you need permissions on server, if you do not have then you will need to ask someone who does to do upload. currently Jennifer, Carolyn, Klaudia, Alex, Sean, and Thomas have permissions.
  6. See CIS Workflow for more information

Manually Adding Course To Search

!!!IMPORTANT!!!
If Sean, Carolyn or Thomas isn't available is and there is an URGENT request for a new course CIS (or name/code updated) then use the information below and proceed at your own risk. Make backups of files before editing.

  1. Upload XML as normal
  2. Add course to /home/olhistweb/courses/app/OLCourses/Data/olcs_courses.csv
  3. If new course acronym, add to /home/olhistweb/courses/cisdata/acronyms/olcs_acronyms.csv

Uploading CIS Document

To do this, open FileZilla and make sure the following fields are filled: Host, Username, Password, Port (you should have received an email with this information). Click on File > Site Manager to make sure that Protocol is set as SFTP.

  1. Once you have logged in to FileZilla, in the left hand window labelled Local site:, open the following folder which contains the newly scripted CIS file (currently stored offline): Computer > Organizational Folder (O:) > Open Learning Share > IDRG-production > COURSES > CIS > _CIS_XML
  2. On the right side of the screen, in the window labelled Remote site:, open the following folder which contains the files that currently appear online: home/olhistweb/courses/cisdata/xml/
  3. To upload the updated CIS, simply drag and drop the proper file from the left hand window into the right hand one. Click OK to overwrite an existing file.
  4. Next, visit http://www.tru.ca/distance/courses and find the course that you have just uploaded. Check to make sure that all updates have been properly added and that there are no formatting issues. If necessary, repeat all of the steps above until the CIS looks as it should.
    • If the course is not appearing, it may be a new course. Give Sean the course code, name, and credits so it can be added to the search list.
  5. Communication once all looks good: Email both CA and DSACourseMangement that requested the upload has done (make sure this is noted in the JIRA task) unless there is a note that DSACourseManagement does not need email.
  6. If completed, the task may then be closed.
  7. Email in OLCISupdates should remain in logged to JIRA folder.

item.title: Final Print Files to Print Shop
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Overview

Once all External changes have been made and print items are signed off, then the final print documents can be sent to the Print Shop.

  • Create a Final Files to Print Shop course subtask in Jira
  • Using the email examples below, prepare an email communication and attach files as needed to:
    • printshop@tru.ca,
    • cc: csa@tru.ca, olresources@tru.ca, olbookbuyer@tru.ca
  • Depending on the circumstances, we may need to adjust the information provided in the email:
    • If no changes to documents or printing instructions from the original print proof request, we list out the item numbers being sent.
    • If changes to the number of page in the document sent, let them know
    • If print job errors (you didn't get what you ordered) note in email
    • If NO Changes to proof files, email must still be sent.
  • Copy/paste email communication in to course subtask

Email Examples

Print Proof Accepted With No Change

If course/file sign off is received and no additional changes are required, we can use the following email example.

Subject: HLTH 4001 SW2 - Final File Sign0off Received - [PROD-4669]

Hello,

The proof for Item 700708 has been signed off. Please use the file you have for all future printing.

YOURNAMEHERE

Changes To Documents After Print Proof

If course/file sign off is received and additional changes have been made to the documents since the initial print proof request, we can use the following email example.

NOTE: If the page count had changed or if there is a change to the print instructions, we need to include that information in the email.

Subject: MATH 2111 SW2- Final Files for Print Shop - [PROD-4669]

Hello,

Attached are the final signed off files for MATH 2111. Please use for all future printing.  Please use same printing instructions as for proofs.

  • Item 206031 Course Guide
  • Item 206032 Study Guide
  • Item 401264 Assignment File

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Thanks,

YOURNAMEHERE

Digital Proof (No Hardcopy Proof Required)

In some circumstances, we may not request a hard copy proof if the updates to the print material are minimal, such as a course amendment to specific documents, and we'll send out a digital copy PDF for review and sign off. In those cases, we'll need to provide the print instructions when we send the final print document to the print shop. We can look back at the previous set of print instructions or provide new ones if needed.

Subject: MATH 2111 SW2.1 - Final Study Guide for Print Shop - [PROD-4669]

Hello,

Attached is the final signed off file for MATH 2111 SW2.1. Please use the file and following print instructions for all future printing. 

Item 206032 Study Guide
Double Sided
Coil Bound
Blue title pages:  10, 34, 76, 21

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Thanks,

YOURNAMEHERE

item.title: Firefox/Chrome/Edge
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Production work requires extensive use of web browsers between our internal online applications, learning management system and other tools. You are free to use your browser of choice, but it is recommended that you install an alternate browser for testing purposes, and some tools like Hypothesis require a Chrome-based browser.

Browser Download Links

  • Firefox
  • Chrome
  • Vivaldi (Chrome alternative)

Browser Specific Tips & Tricks

Firefox

Moodle Search from Address Bar

  • Setup Firefox to search Moodle from the address bar using the built-in keyword search functionality.
  • Open the Firefox Bookmark Manager by pressing ALT and then clicking Bookmarks>Manage Bookmarks
  • Click Organize>Add Bookmark
  • In the Add bookmark pop-up:
    • Give your Bookmark a name, e.g. Moodle Course Search
    • In the URL field, copy/paste the following URL: https://moodle.tru.ca/course/search.php?search=%s
      Note: If you would like to search for courses using the course administration interface, use this URL or setup another bookmark with keyword: https://moodle.tru.ca/course/management.php?search=%s
    • Enter a keyword or characters for searching with the address bar, e.g. ms ACCT 1221
  • Click the save button and close the Bookmark Manager window

To search for a Moodle course from the address bar, enter the keyword you used please the course info and press enter.

Chrome

Moodle Search from Address Bar

Similar to Firefox, you can search Moodle from the address bar using a site search shortcut. Use the resource below to set up Moodle search shortcut in Chrome.

item.title: Course File Requests
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Updated information/instructions about final exam paper forms and pools

File Requests come into Production from a variety of sources. Each source can have different needs as far as file format required.

Requests are sent to OLProduction and should be classified as File Requests if part of Course Life Cycle OR Content Support Request with appropriate Component (Print on Demand, Student Support) if from our student services. The exception is if the Course is Active in Production and request is part of producing a new master. These requests should go in as subtask under the relevant course.

File Request Video Overview

Type of File Requests

Files Request Process

We have created a training video that goes over the process. Please review for a quick overview of the process.

File Request Training Video

1. Confirm Course Version

For all requests, check in D4P to find out current version of course. Most requests are for the most recent version there can be exceptions for OLFM material but D4P will provide date references and master references.

2. Locate Course Files

Subversion holds the most recent version of all files. If requiring a Master completed before Nov. 2012 then you will need to look in O: drive as documented below.

Locating Older Course Files

  1. Check Subversion - Best case scenario, best file formats
  2. O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\IN PROGRESS - May have excess files and will need to sort out most recent copy, once cleaned up should be sent to COMPLETED and removed from IN PROGRESS.
  3. O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\COURSES\COMPLETED - If files have multiple dates and not clear which is best, pull from web container - print is typically straight forward, just check against print item list
  4. O:\Open Learning Share\IDRG-production\ARCHIVE - If nothing in other locations, check here (2009-2012 files) - usually only 3 digit code and usually a bit specious, better to recreate files
  5. No files in common spots - contact supervisor, or convert from web or from existing print PDF's (get most up-to-date copy from print shop)

3. Prepare Course Files: Standard Web and Print

NOTE: We can not send the Subversion files for online paced courses, as paced OLFMs are compensated to maintain their course material and our course files may not match. Please ask the Production Supervisor how best to proceed with online-paced course requests.

  • Use the XML to Print tool at https://olhub.tru.ca/xmltoprint/ (Username: xml | Password: print) to produce NEW word documents of course content.
    Do not use previous Word documents that have been through the scripting process, as they may no longer be accurate.
  • Clean up files (standard formatting not required):
    • Quickly compare to web (XML files should be up to date, but a quick compare is useful)
    • Remove extra para breaks
    • Remember that when we send out a file request, it is often sent back to us for a Maintenance revision. Although standard print formatting is not required, it is important to send out a clean file that you would like to receive back.
  • Confirm all files included:
    • Check tabs in course (Welcome (course guide), Assessments Overview, Modules etc), more info about quizzes and final exam below
    • Make sure everything that is in the course is included in the files (including images folder, resources)
    • Include the OLFMG

Final Exams/Practice Exams

For Final Exams use D4P to confirm which Exam Forms are currently active in the "Applies to:" field for the version of the course that is being requested.

If the Exams ARE NOT Pooled/Randomized (e.g. Form Based)
Locate the exam files in Subversion (Exams\Forms\Active) or on O Drive (O:\Open Learning Share\Final Exams and Keys\examrepo\). Select the appropriate exam form based on D4P. When possible, only send out the active Exam From Answer Key document(s) (e.g. ACCT1211_G_ak_05MAR20.docx). If the Answer Key document doesn't include the questions, please send both the Final Exam and Answer Key documents.

  • Track Changes should be off and all changes accepted.
  • All Comments should be deleted.

If the Exams ARE Pooled/Randomized

Export the exam/quiz/pools etc directly from Moodle.

  • Navigate to the requested course current DEV container
  • Go to Question Bank>Export
  • Select the Microsoft Word 2010 table format (wordtable) format
  • Select the top category that includes all the sub category questions
  • Click the Export questions to file button
  • Open the document in Word (in the Convert File pop-up, select HTML Document)
  • Add standard instructions/comments for SMEs/Editors (See example document in: O:\Open Learning Share\Final Exams and Keys) and save as .docx (Note: Files pull down as .doc, so you will NEED to save as .docx instead)
  • In the File Request communication, let the requestor know we can also provide a development shell with the pooled exam for direct editing if needed.

NOTE: Exporting an LMS Pool with the following questions may skip them in the export without warning:
- (Drag and drop onto image)
- (Drag and drop into text)
- (Select missing words)

If an exam/quiz has these types of questions, instead make a blank container and import the quiz activities and question bank into it.

We can set up the quizzes in a new container using the following naming convention:
DEV_OL ABCD 1234_SW# - Quiz Review/Update

No additional enrolments required. In the communication back to the requestor, let them know we can add the SME/OLFM directly to the container and will just need the details.

ERROR: Moodle XSLT transformation failed
Very rare, but it means some question(s) have some bad formatting inside them, usualy a <script> element that shouldn't be there.
Export the bank as XML, then do a search for a '<script' element. Once you find the offending questions, remove the script from the questions and try exporting again.
Failing that, you can export sub categories of questions to try and narrow down which question(s) are stopping exporting.

    3. Share Course Files Package on O: drive

    • If in Subversion create a ZIP file with Content (XML to Word files as noted above), OLFM and Resources folder then remove any extra content (PDF's if we have word version in there as well, only send correct method - ie only web if print is now closed)
    • Name file CourseCode_MasterNumber_Files and save that with files.
    • Copy the final ZIP file to O:\Open Learning Share\OL-production file transfer\Files from Production\CURRENTYEAR

    Prepare Course Files: Online-Paced

    ***UPDATES NEEDED***

    Other File Requests

    Will depend on who is requesting. If in doubt, ask requester for clarification of purpose. Typically, these requests have specific parameters so will need to meet. If it is for official purposes - make sure things look pretty.

    For special file requests, resulting file can be stored in: http://phoenix.tru.ca:9880/production/trunk/Courses/Misc File Requests
