item.title: Moodle Forums (Discussions) Setup and Settings
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
The Forum activity (Discussions), allows students and teachers to exchange ideas by posting comments as part of a 'thread'.

Forums Activity Overview

For most OL courses, forum activities will be created in a Discussions or Forums tab in the course, but if they are graded they should be included in the Assignment/Assessment Overview tab.

There is no standard wording for the tab as the forum requirements will often vary per course, but we can often pull a small description from the Course Guide or other course instructions if needed. If there is no additional information in the course, please touch base with the Production Supervisor on how best to proceed.

Forum Settings

Generally, watch settings for activity completion. Do the instructions specify whether the student should be creating a discussion or posting replies and how many?

Whole Forum Grading Settings

Whole Forum Grading means that OLFM's can grade forum participation for one student. Use the following information to adjust the forum settings for whole forum grading:

Whole Forum Grading Process for OLFMs

Here's an example of what OLFMs will see when using whole forum grading in Moodle:

item.title: LIVE Moodle Shell Review
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent Updates:
- Added section with Ongoing Moodle Content Updates details
- Reorganized process into sections
- Added Moodle Shell tracking details

Overview

Course uploads/shell copies are completed by DSA Course Management and then they notify Production so we can systematically check everything is correct. The upload requests are classified as TASKS and get assigned to an EST designated for review.

Moodle LIVE Review Process

Please review the following items for each shell copy:

Shell Settings

  • Review the shell title, make sure that the title matches the OLFM/session provided by DSA Course Management.*
  • In the course settings, confirm the Course ID details match the information provided.*
  • If an older course/amendment, use the Bulk edit activity completion options (go to More>Course Completion>Bulk Edit Activity Completion) to remove manual activity tracking (e.g. Mark as done box) from all items except for graded assessments, books and other items with specific completion requirements in both the recently copied LIVE shell(s) and the original DEV shell.

Blocks

Check to make sure blocks are complete and configured. Each course should generally have one of each block:

  • Activities
  • Progress/Key Course Milestones (there may be more then one depending on assessment setup)
  • Quick Links
  • Latest announcements

Content

  • Quickly glance over the Course Guide content to ensure that the correct shell content has been transferred. If amendment shell - has .#: check Amendment information in D4P to see what generated update, make sure fix is in live version.*
  • Delete the DO NOT COPY tab and any associated items from the shell if there is one
  • If an older course/amendment, check print/save instructions in Modules/Units/Lessons tab and if older language (e.g. use the gear icon) update to: The Modules/Units/Lessons CHANGE TO MATCH COURSE FORMAT for this course are presented in Moodle Book format. You can print or download each Book by selecting an item below and using the "More" menu located at the top of the Book section to choose a print option.

Ongoing Moodle Content Updates

This section includes a list of items that need to be checked to due updates across all Moodle courses. If you come across one of the updates that are not complete in the course list below, we should update DEV/LIVE shell(s) content and the MST project tasks to match.

If DEV/LIVE revisions are needed, please update the following MST task details:

  • Container Updates section to show updates completed
  • Status updated to next applicable Workflow step

The general idea is that we want to avoid adding to the MST project TO DO tasks by making the necessary revisions as we go through shell review process.

Current content items to check for/update:

  • Course Guide/Assessments: Wording above assessments table
  • Course Guide/Assessments: Academic Integrity wording

Navigation

  • Check that the left-hand navigation bar looks correct. E.g. no unusual labels or (copy) text included.

Quiz Activity Notifications

Confirm/enable quiz attempt notifications for OLFMs for any graded quizzes and Final Exams.

  • Online Paced Shells: We only need to have the Final Exam notifications turned on and not other individual quizzes.
  • Standard Web Shells: Notifications are required for any quizzes that need to be graded by the OLFM including the Final Exam. If the quizzes are auto-marked (e.g. only have basic multiple choice, T/F, etc.) then notifications are not required.
  • Assignments/Quiz Activities: Assignments that use the quiz activity should have notifications turned on.

Users

  • Review users to ensure the correct OLFM was added (may not have been done as DSA Course Management does after upload)*

OLFM Videos

Add OLFM Introduction video if available (See list below)

  • Check list of available OLFM videos at the bottom of the page
  • If video is available, click on main Action Menu (gear icon) and select Import
  • Search for "OLFM Intro Videos," select the shell and click continue
  • Uncheck all items except "Include activities and resources," click Next
  • Under Select, click "None," check Course Guide and the corresponding OLFM Video and then click Next
  • Confirm you are only importing the OLFM video, scroll to the bottom of the page and click Perform import
  • Once import is complete, confirm that the video is in the Course Guide section and move the video/URL resource below the Key Course Navigation Features button
  • If the course uses the "Welcome" page format, in the Getting Started list add new bullet under Save your Suggested Schedule document: Meet Your Open Learning Faculty Member and confirm item in autolinking

Final Exam

  • If an older standard web (SW) course/amendment course copy, confirm the Final Exam quiz activity visibility matches the current LIVE shells to ensure students have access to the active Final Exam. Online paced courses are checked by the Exams Liaison Officer.

* If you encounter any issues with these items, follow up with DSA Course Management and Program Delivery Associate who made the copy via email.

Moodle Shell Tracking Project Updates

The Moodle Shell Tracking (MST) is our inventory of Moodle shells. It is designed to track both existence of Moodle shells as well as status of any work done on them. For more information see the Moodle Tracking Project Overview. The LIVE shell review process now includes creating adding records for newly copied course shells for new courses and for current courses (e.g. paced or new OLFMs/sessions).

See the Ongoing Moodle Content Updates section above for specific revisions we're looking for.

Create New Active Moodle Shell Subtask

Summary: Create new subtask, fill in fields

  • Go to the Moodle Shells Sorted: Dev-Live Filter and search for course.
  • Select the primary DEV Moodle Shell work item
  • Create a subtask
  • Add/update LIVE Shell Records as noted in the table below
  • Update the following fields/info for new shell task
    • Enrollment Status – Active for new copy
    • Course ID Number – From Jira task/LIVE course shell

Clone/Copy Active Moodle Shell Subtask

Summary: Clone existing subtask and edit

  • Go to the Moodle Shells Sorted: Dev-Live Filter and search for course.
  • Select the most recent LIVE version copy subtask and clone task
  • Update the following fields/info for new shell task
    • Enrollment Status – Active for new copy
    • Course ID Number – From Jira task/LIVE course shell
  • Remove clone link

JIRA Task Update

Once you have reviewed/updated the shells(s) and add added record(s) to the Moodle Shell Tracking Jira project:

  • Add the MST component to the LIVE shell check task
  • Log your time
  • Leave a comment in the Jira task
    Example: Course shell review complete, record(s) added to MST project. [Please note any items adjusted, e.g. Navigation fixed, quiz notifications enabled, etc. ]

item.title: Request Moodle Container Backup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
In some cases we made need to request a backup of a Moodle course container from BCNet where our offsite backups are managed.  TRU's Moodle is set to make backups of courses on Sun, Tue, Thurs, Sat at 11:45 PM each night. Requests can best sent sts-moodle-ops@bc.net with the following details:

  • Container name,
  • Container ID#
  • Approximate date for restore (see info above)
  • Brief summary of reason for request

Example Email:

Subject: Moodle.tru.ca Course Container Backup Request

Good morning,
OL Production would like to request a Moodle backup of BUSN 6151_ON2 - Advanced Marketing Management (Fall 2022 Weischedel), ID# 40107, from Tuesday, October 18th if possible. The Open Learning Faculty Member is reporting a lost group assignment submission due to students dropping the course and the deletion of corresponding group in that time period. Please let us know if you require any additional details. Thank you very much.

item.title: Accessibility Requests
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Course accessibility requests will typically come from Accessibility Office via OL Materials. By law we MUST do our best to meet accommodation requirements.

Process for Accessibility

  1. Make sure JIRA task is tagged as Accessibility Services Request
  2. Clearly determine need of student - clarify exactly what will be required, the initial request may not account for all material. Look quickly through course and consider request.
    • Any questions are directed back to OL Materials who will follow up.
    • Give time line for initial assessment back to OL Materials so that they can keep student informed.
  3. Systematically go through course and create a spreadsheet documenting: Specific Location, title, original link if applicable. You are potentially looking at tables, images, audio, video, interactive media objects, scanned readings.
    • Third party material must also be evaluated - eg. Youtube material, websites etc.
    • Editing team may be able to help with this work
  4. Convey general results back to OL Materials - conveying - if there is material of concern, if so how long it might take to get ready
  5. Discuss with supervisor on materials conversions required as work may get split out to multiple people.
  6. Based on student requirements start processing material. See individual documents for material workflows.
  7. Material should be sent back to OL Materials as a package - UNLESS after discussion it has been determined segments would be more useful for student. A good example of this approach is if the student has already started the course and the request is trailing their start date.

Note: If material is complicated then is may be necessary to contact the student to clarify what is best for them eg. visually impaired person may be fluent in Braille or may just need audio. This is done by requesting permission to contact to OL Materials who will follow up. They will provide student contact info if they get go ahead. Also a third party expert may need to be hired to help create material. If this step is necessary then contact Curriculum Services

item.title: Print on Demand/Print Suitability Reviews
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent Updates:
- Added a FAQ section regarding some internal and external questions/requests we receive regarding Print on Demand material.

Production will often receive Print on Demand and/or Print Suitability Reviews from Enrolment Services and other departments in the university. In most cases, we're assessing a course to see if it can be completed by an incarcerated student with limited/no internet access and limited access to additional resources. The reviews are generally split into to types:

  • Print on Demand Review - Review of a standard web courses to see if the course materials, resources, media, etc. can be converted to a print course.
  • Print Suitability Review - Review of a current Print course to see if the student can complete the course with limited/no internet and access to other resources.

Review Process Overview within OL

Production related items are in bold.

  1. Student inquires with Enrolment Services about taking a print course, or a course that is not available in print format, the majority of these students will be incarcerated
  2. The Enrolment Services Offices (ESO) who fields the inquiry will email OL Materials to see if we already have reviewed the requested course and proivde the information if possible.
  3. If thier are no Print on Demand details in D4P, OL Materials will email Production to review the requested course for print suitability and we'll log/send that information back to OL Materials to send out.
    Note: Production will not create/order materials until it is confirmed the students in enrolled.
  4. The ESO will let the student know that if it is possible the cost of the course will be as per FLEX+ $95.00 for the additional printed items, and will take credit card and course information manually on a registration form and will inform the student they will be contacted prior to charging any credit card
  5. If the course(s) is suitable, OL Material will inform the ESO who will email deliverysupport2@tru.ca asking for a new CRN, and find an OLFM.
  6. Once new CRN and OLFM are provided, the ESO will ask OL Materials to request the material from Production. This step may require Production to create/order new print materials/documents or order previously sent files.
  7. The requested print material is sent to the Print Shop and delivered to OL Materials prior to being shipped out to the student.
  8. If Production is creating new files for a request, we'll create a new Print on Demand course task, create the print materials and complete a QA Review before sending to the Print Shop.
  9. Once new CRN and OLFM are provided, payment will be made, and registration form will be given to the Records department to process as they do now (register in the course using the new CRN and ordering any textbooks that are required as part of the course via WinPrism) and email both deliverysupport2@tru.ca and olmaterials@tru.ca
  10. Course textbooks and printed items will be sent to OL Materials prior to being shipped
  11. If not appropriate, OL Production will let the OL Materials know the course is not suitable, and that information will be passed along to the ESO to forware to the student.

Print on Demand/Print Suitability Review Workflow

Check Current Records (D4P/JIRA) for Review Information

  1. Check the Print On Demand Suitability Report in D4P to see if we have already completed the review process for the course.
  2. If there is no information in D4P, search JIRA (Course Name/Number, plus Print on Demand component) to see if there has been a previous request/review.
  3. If a previous review has been completed, check D4P to see if course has changed since then (new version, amendments, etc.) to see if evaluation might be still valid. Go to Step 4 if answer was yes and no recent curriculum changes.
  4. Check D4P2 for what methods of delivery existed, when signed off, especially important if recent print. - Things to look for is just closure of print with no new master/recent new master.
    • For Cancelled Print - as a safety check, go into D4P record and look for comments in Summary page, Production area for actual status of signed of material, THEN check our records in JIRA to see if we had official sign off.
  5. Review JIRA ALIVE Project (Fix My Course tasks) for course changes, especially if a potentially usable print course that was recently closed.

If an assessment of course is needed, proceed to the next section.

Review Course and Prepare Summary

IMPORTANT: If the steps 1 & 2 below show need for internet, then probably not a good candidate. If above is not conclusive, then complete the following steps as well.

  1. Review the Course Guide
    • Check materials section - does it mention electronic text books, or supplies
    • Check Assessments section - does it mention online quizzes, midterms, discussions, video submissions, etc.
  2. Review Assignments
    • See what it states about use of many external resources - ie. search, look for websites, use specific websites, access library, etc.
    • Note: just a simple research paper may not stop process.
  3. Review Module/Unit/Lesson Activities
    • Review context of external links and requirements for students to use web. (e.g. are they required for to complete any of the assessments or are they considered optional)
    • We can use the .xml file to help answer activities question and also use the Link Checker to identify all external links in course.
    • Review provided resources such as PDFs and other documents. If there are PDFs provided in Moodle that are required to complete the course and/or the assignments, we will need to contact the Copyright team (copyright@tru.ca) with the details and ask if the resources can be reproduced in print format for print on demand.
  4. Create a Summary
    • Document overall impression of material (e.g. suitable, potentially or not suitable) with brief description a summary of review and potential caveats that students should be aware of.

Example Summary for ESO
Subject: BIOL 1113 SW3 - Print on Demand Suitability Review (X00872343) - [PROD-23442]

Hello,
This course can be completed as a Print on Demand with use of a non-web-connected computer as with the following notes:

BIOL 1113 SW3 - Suitable
● The course references multiple digital resources, but all are optional exercises.
● The publisher's website is referenced throughout, but it is well documented that this resource may not be always available as put up by publisher.
● There are self-directed quizzes for web version within the LMS, which are optional and for practice. These quizzes CAN NOT be printed due to copyright restrictions.

  1. Document in D4P and Jira
    • Add the suitability status and comments to D4P under the Production section for future reference
    • Add summary to Jira as well and log review/communication time
  2. Send Report Summary
    • Send the summary back to the ESO or reply-all if multiple people were included on the initial inquiry. Note: Production will not create/order materials until it is confirmed the students in enrolled, and will generally involve a separate Jira task.

Prepare the Materials

For Suitable Print Courses

For suitable print courses, often there is nothing that Production needs to do, and the process will be completed without additional Production assistance. In some instances, Production may be required to package readings, provide alternative media formats (transcripts) that are determined on a per-case basis and will be noted in the main task.

For Suitable Standard Web Courses

If a standard web course is considered suitable and the student is enrolled, Production will prepare the course material as required. This includes:

  • Use XML to Print to generate the initial Word documents, usually this will include a Study Guide (Course Guide and Units/Modules combined), Assignments and possibly a Readings files.
  • Format the documents to match our OL print styles with title pages. Note: Print on Demand documents aren't required to start page numbers for each section (e.g. CG-1, U-2, U-2, etc.) and pages can be continuous. New sections should still start on right-hand side and blank pages shouldn't contain header/footer info.
  • Adjust structure for print and remove all Moodle/online reference that do not apply to the print material.
    • Review the course structure in Moodle. Sometimes the course is structured in an awkward way where you would need to combine mulitple tabs into a single booklet (HLTH courses and labs are bad for this)
    • Use ctrl+f to search for keywords like http, assignments overview, and other common keywords used in standard web courses
  • Remove faculty names from copyright sections and course developer sections
  • Complete QA Review of the material that was created/formatted before sending to the Print Shop

Order Print on Demand Materials

If either existing material at print shop is needed (no warehouse stock) or new printing is required, an email request should be sent to printshop@tru.ca.

  • For Existing materials: order one copy using printing instructions on file
  • For New materials: include printing instructions

Ask charges to be made to account: 103000-425510-800012
Ask to email when ready for pickup.
When ready, materials should be delivered to OL Materials and then let whoever sent request that material are ready with them.

Important: When Production orders the materials, we should remove faculty names from copyright sections and course developer sections before sending.

Example Email to Print Shop (customize to suit particular request):

Frequently Asked PoD Questions

What do we replace Moodle-specific assignment instructions with?
As soon as you have completed an assignment, save your document and submit it to your Open Learning Faculty Member. Any additional file naming or document formatting requirements remain as is.

Can we provide printed copies of copyrighted course resources such as PDFs, slides, etc.?
Yes, in general students are allow to print a hardcopy of the material for personal use and print on demand requests fall under similar usage senearios. If the resource or combined resources are over 100 pages, please check with Production Supervisor.

Can we send out PDF versions of the print on demand course files if requested?
Yes, but we need to remove the stadard Copyright page from each file provided and also the Course Contributor/Devlopment information from the Course Guide/Study Guide before sending.

item.title: Final Exam Wording for Print Courses
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded: The wording for print final exams has been updated and should be included/updated in all current print courses/amendments in Production. This information in usually included in the Course Guide/Assessments section, but can also be noted in other areas of the course as well. Replace as needed.

item.title: EDDL Course/Commons in a Box Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added additional Moodle URL/link updates to EDDL course site and student instructions in the Updating Moodle Course Link and Instructions section.

Commons in a Box Course Duplication Process

FUTURE UPDATES

  • Need to review OLFM enrolment process with DSA as it was previously handled by E-Learning Faciliator and manually adding users seems to remove course dicussions, calendars, etc. Need to investigate if they can be added earlier in the process.

Setting up EDDL course

Go to https://eddl.tru.ca/groups/type/course/ and click Create/Clone in the upper right hand corner. Complete the following steps:

  1. Make sure create New is selected (the clone option only works if you are the owner of the original site - it is usually easier to just create a new course/site)
  2. Give the course a name - it should be the exact same as the original, followed by "(Semester Year OLFM Name)" - for example, "Course Name (Fall 2020 Webster)"
  3. The URL should auto complete when you update the course name, but will likely need to be cleaned up. Make sure any leading or trailing hyphens are deleted, and that the URL starts and ends with an alphanumeric character (anything else and the URL won't be accepted).
  4. The avatar is the image that will appear on the course page - grab the avatar from the original course (would be handy to have the course files checked out on your desktop).
  5. Copy the description from the original course, but leave out the link. We will add a link to our new site home page later.
  6. The academic term should match the semester-year combination you used earlier in the course title.
  7. Set the course to Private in the Privacy settings.

Setting up EDDL Site

Click create and continue. You will be taken to a page asking to set up the new course site. The default options are fine, click next at bottom. This will complete creating the course - now we need to duplicate the pages for the actual site. At the top of your page on the tool bar, under TRU EDDL, select Dashboard. Once in the dashboard, select Pages -> All Pages.

  • Search in the search bar on the top right for the course name (just something like "EDDL 5101" is fine)
    • Note: Filtering by date makes this a lot easier, as some pages won't have an EDDL Prefix sometimes.
  • This should present all the pages from that course. Check with the live course to make sure you are not missing any sections
    • If a course is very large, some of the pages may be pushed to the second viewing page
    • You will probably have a lot of duplicate pages from different terms, try filtering by date.
  • Select pages from the most recent course version and choose "clone" under bulk actions - hit apply
    • Note: In most cases you want to only clone the root parent page, as it will also clone all it's child pages attached to it. If you end up with a bunch of duplicates, just trash the extra copies. This doesn't apply if the course doesn't use parenting.
    • Note: We used to maintain DEV pages, but now we treat this like an ON course, where the most recent LIVE is what we copy.
  • This will clone all the pages and by default add a semester-year combination to their name (this may be incorrect)
    • Tip: Now you can filter by 'Mine' and date, showing only the cloned pages.

Setting up EDDL site pages

  • Select "Edit with Classic Editor" for a single page to change its attributes (we use the classic editor as these courses were built with classic, and things break if edits are made in the block editor)

Home Page

  • Let's start with the main page - it should be close to the top of the list of pages (Make sure you are editing the new pages, and not the originals)
    • In the page, change the title so it reflects the correct semester-year-OLFM combination (example - "(Fall 2020 Webster)")
    • At the top, under permalink, clean up the URL slug so it looks something like this: eddl-5101-educational-technology-for-learning-fall-2020-webster (note there are no colons or extra hyphens)
    • Nothing should be broken on the page if using the classic editor, but a quick scroll through doesn't hurt
    • Click Publish on the right hand side to publish and save this page
    • This will show a tool bar prompt with the link for the new home page. Copy this link, and close the prompt

Pointing the EDDL course to the home page

Let's take a quick break away from the site pages to link our course home page with the site home page while we have it on our clipboard. Open the course page for the new course you are working on (not the original; you can get there by using the same link at the top of the page). It should look something like this:

EDDL Course Home Page Example

  • Click settings on the right tool bar, and in the text box for the description add an anchor tag at the beginning of the paragraph pointing towards the new site home page
    • Example: <a href="new-site-home-page-url-here">Full Name of Course here (EDDL 5101: Educational Technology for Learning (Fall 2020 Webster)</a>
  • If you click "Course Home" on the right toolbar, there should now be a link in the description box that direct you to the site home page. If not, something has gone horribly wrong. Perhaps make sure you have closed the anchor tag.

Editing other course pages

Follow the same steps as the Home Page for setting up the name and permalink, then move onto a few extras below.

  • On the right toolbar, under Page Attributes, make sure that the Parent Page is the new home page we just spun up - if not, select it from the dropdown. The order shouldn't need to be changed, but if it does just make sure it makes sense chronologically.
    • If you did the 'clone only root parent' trick, all the child pages will already be parented correctly.
  • The course prefix can be removed from the title ("EDDL 5101" or whatever it happens to be for your course) so that the title just starts with "Week"
    • Have the previous course open in another tab to check if this is required.
    • As long as the parent page is set, the pages will still be organized
  • You may need to remove the course prefix from the permalink also so that it just starts with "week"

Menus

Time for a frustrating amount of clicks. Once you have at least one normal page set up with correct name, URL slug, and parent page it is a good idea to set up the Menu to easily keep track of pages. There are three places we have to address menu making:

  • First, go to "Appearances -> Menus" on the left toolbar of the main WordPress dashboard.
    • Click create a new menu, and name it according to the course (example - EDDL 5101 - Fall 2020 Webster) - click create menu
    • Select all the pages for this new course that you have edited so far in the scroll section on the left (under the "Pages" section) and click add to menu.
    • For the top one (Should be the link to the home page) the name can be left as is. For the child pages, edit it so each link only starts with "Week..." (if it isn't like that already)
    • Next, under scroll section on the left select "Custom Links"
      • Go and copy the URL for the course home page (not the site home page) and paste it into the URL field
      • In the Link Text field name it "Return to course landing page"
      • Click add, and drag it to the top of the list
    • If items need to be visual children of other menu items, you can drag the menu item to the left or right
    • Make sure you save the menu, then move on to the next step
  • Second, go to "Content Aware -> Add New" on the left toolbar of the main WordPress dashboard
    • Title the sidebar appropriately (example - EDDL 5101 - Fall 2020 Webster)
    • Click "New Condition Group" and scroll down to select "Pages" under "Post Types"
    • Add pages where this sidebar will appear by searching for the name of the course (just typing in something like EDDL 5101 will bring up all pages with that course prefix)
    • Make sure you are adding the pages from the new site, and not the original
    • After adding all the pages, click save
    • Click on the Action tab
    • Under Target Sidebar find "EDDL Course Content"
    • Save changes
  • Third, go to "Appearances -> Widgets" on the left toolbar of the main WordPress dashboard
    • On the right hand side, locate the sidebar that you just made by name, and click the arrow to toggle it open
    • Search for the "Custom Menu Wizard" in the left window, and drag it into your open sidebar
    • Title the menu "Contents" and select the menu you made in the first step from the dropdown list
    • Under the "Container" toggle, make sure the Element is "div" and add the following classes to the Class field: profile-nav sidebar-block clearfix
    • Under the "Classes" toggle, add the following classes to the Menu Class field: sidebar-nav clearfix
    • Click save
    • If the menu didn't appear, double check the classes are in the right place.

Now when you go into a course page that you have edited and added to all the needed menu locations above, you will see a Menu widget displayed on the right. If it is not showing on a page, make sure you added the correct page in the Content Aware sidebar tool. The rest of setup is just rinse and repeat for all remaining pages in the course.

Updating links

  • Assignments
    • The assignment URLs will need to be changed to reflect the current semester - unfortunately you cannot just change the URL in WordPress (it won't be able to find the file)
    • Break all the links by clicking on them and clicking the "Break Link" icon in the toolbar
    • Highlight the text for an assignment (example - "Assignment 1") and click "Add Media" in the toolbar
    • On your desktop, rename the Assignment PDFs to have "-semesteryear" added to the end of each name (example - "EDDL5101_AS1-fall2020"), and drag and drop them all into the "Upload Files" tab of the Add Media window
    • Choose the assignment you are uploading, and on the right side change the title field to reflect the assignment name (This is what will show as the link text, it can be changed later)
    • After updating all assignments, click update, navigate to the live assignments page and test that all PDF links work and display the correct semester-year combination in the URL
  • Other Stuff
    • This is by far the worst part of cloning courses.
    • Internal links - make sure you test all internal links (links to other pages - most common are assignment redirects) so that they all point to pages on the new site, and not the original
      • I would suggest that instead of re-linking the assignment anywhere it is present, instead replace the link with a blurb like "Assignment #, which can be accessed on the Assignments Overview page" and then link to the assignments page.
    • External links - Although it is the responsibility of the OLFM in charge of the course to replace broken links, it is best to go through while you are in the fixing mode and find all broken links (easier to provide them with a list now than to have 10 broken links trickle in over 6 months). This doesn't take long, but is a lot of clicks.
    • Forum/Discussion Links - Watch out for these, if you miss them they usualy link to the previous course forum. They should point to the current course disussion forum that you find on the course home page on the right nav block. If it doesn't exist, in the same block go to settings, then settings again at the top. There should be a checkbox to enable discussion there.
    • Portfolios - Safely ignore anything related to Portfolios as students are usualy directed to this link. If you get FMC asking about why some students can't see other porfolios, it's usualy because they made them private by accident.

Updating Moodle Course Link and Instructions

The final step after setting up the EDDL course site is to ensure the corresponding Moodle courses are poiting to the new EDDL course home pages and include the the student registration instructions. In Moodle:

  • Search for the semester EDDL courses (e.g. EDDL Winter 2024)
  • Open the container(s) and locate the the EDDL #### Course Site URL resource/link that should be at the near the top of the course
  • Turn on Edit mode in the top-right, and select the Edit settings options for the resource
  • For the External URL field, copy/paste the full EDDL site URL that was just created (e.g. https://eddl.tru.ca/groups/eddl-5131_on2-designing-multimedia-for-curriculum-winter-2024-webster/)
  • In the description section add the following text and enable the Display description on course page option.
  • Scroll down to the buttom of the page an click Save and return to course. The end result should like similar to the following screenshot.

That is all. Well done! From here, you can email DSA Course Management, and it should be handled from there.

Wordpress Errors and how to fix them

Sometimes wordpress will break and Troy will need to reset the server, but here are some fixes for certain problems.

Page not found

Course pages suddenly not working with a 'Page not Found' error.
Admin > Settings > Permalinks > Save Changes
This resets page linking and should fix missing pages.

item.title: Online Quiz Activity Corrections
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
****IN PROGRESS****

Graded Quiz Activity Corrections (Quiz, Midterm, Final) - No Changes to Marks

  • Navigate to Quiz with corrections required, select the Questions tab and confirm quiz questions are set to use "Always latest" if pooled.
  • Locate the affected question(s) in the Question bank section, click the Edit dropdown and select Edit question
  • Make the required questions correction(s) to text and/or answers (IMPORTANT: We cannot change questions marks with this process, mark changes require different steps, please check with Production Supervisor)
  • Confirm the changes are in place, scroll to the bottom of the page and select the Save changes button to create a new question version
  • In the Question bank section, under the Comments column, click the "0" character/link to open the comment window
  • Confirm the correction version is selected in the top-left, add a brief summary of the change along with the Jira task number, and click the Add comment button
    Note: Current version comments can be accessed by clicking the number in the Comments columns, previous version comments can be viewed using the Edit dropdown beside the question and selecting the History option
  • Document changes in Jira, log time and contact the original requestor to confirm changes are complete.

Graded Quiz Activity Corrections (Quiz, Midterm, Final) - Changes to Marks, Headings, Etc.

Example Instructions for Quiz Correction where a new version of the quiz activity is required:

  • Duplicate the current quiz and hide from students
  • Confirm no students are attempting the quiz in the Attempts section
  • Close the original quiz:
    • Replace the description/instructions with "This version of ***QUIZ NAME*** is no longer open."
    • Adjust the close dates to the current date and time
    • In the settings and update the "After the quiz is closed" review settings to match the "Later, while the quiz is still open" section.
  • Update title of new quiz activity to include "v2" e.g. Midterm 1 (v2)
  • Make adjustments/corrections as needed.
  • Add restrictions to the new quiz that, so it is only available if the original quiz is incomplete and hidden to student that have already completed the new quiz.
  • Add Grades category with quiz weight, hide total with highest grade and Exclude empty grades options

There are some additional considerations if students are able to review their attempt, but since students can only see marks in this case, we can proceed with the info above.

IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS:

Midterms

  • Close the original midterm in the settings
  • Replace the description/instructions with "This version of ***MIDTERM NAME*** is no longer open."
  • Duplicate the midterm that requires updates and make adjustments/corrections as needed
  • Add restrictions to the new quiz that, so it is only available if the original quiz is incomplete and hidden to student that have already completed the new quiz.

Final Exams

Do the students get access to the quizzes afterwards?

It's only stuff that they are allowed to have access to after it closes...

Final Exam, we just move to a "Old material" tab, because we keep it on record.

But students no longer have access to it

Mid-term and other quizzes, we duplicate it and put restrictions on it

Examples:

https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=7024&section=1

https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=12015&section=3

item.title: Moodle Container Assessment Project
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
The purpose of the project is two fold:

  1. Final Online Exams Assessment for use secondary tabs and copy/paste functionality
  2. Overall container assessment for potential problematic content setup structures

Required Project Software

  • JIRA
  • Moodle
  • D4P2 (LMS exams report)

Project JIRA Tracking

All work for this project is to be documented in the following JIRA project:
Container Assessment 2023 (ID's prefaced by CA- )

The project has a unique record for each container to be assessed.

The project has unique fields to capture the information required.

Each record has a priority assigned to it from Blocker to Priority 12.
There is a further subset of records that have Not Yet Set as a priority. These records will have their priority set once all the Priority 12 records are done.

JIRA Dashboard setup:

Before beginning add "Container Assessment" Dashboard to your Dashboard list.

On this dashboard there three filters shown. The top one is the to be done or in progress work, the middle one will show containers that will need work and the bottom one will show containers with no more work required.

Recommended Project Workflow Setup

  1. JIRA Work Environment setup: Go to Container Assessment Dashboard, select total issue number of first filter (Container Assessment Priority Sort (Not done), adjust view so looking at detailed view. This will allow you to move easily from task to task. (see image below)
  1. Moodle open to dashboard - should have search panel setup.

Container Evaluation

There are five parts to each evaluation:

Part 1 - Locating Development Container

Using title given in JIRA, task search in Moodle for the Development container.

To go directly to correct container:

  1. Add DEV_OL term to front of name.
  2. Adjust format to match Moodle naming conventions

Using the example shown above:

JIRA record listing: "ANES4021-ON-002"

Moodle search term: DEV_OL ANES 4021_ON2

If the course has a double number, eg. VTEC 1713-ON-OO1-OO1, it will be represented as a decimal eg. 1.1

Moodle search term: DEV_OL VTEC 1713_ON1.1

Part 2 - Evaluating if Practice Exam

Determine if there is a Practice Exam (Presence of Practice Exam Tab)

If tab, determine the type of Practice Exam.

This information is recorded in the Final Assessment Field as follows:

Part 3- Detailed Exam Info (1): Secondary Exam Tab

Go to Final Exam tab and scroll down to exam.
Note: you may want to bring up course in D4P2 LMS exams report for this step.

First:

Look for Materials Provided Section

If material provided it will require a secondary tab - go fill in field.

If No Materials Provided Section, continue investigating.

Second (if not clear from above):

Edit the Exam and look at instruction sections/headings - looking for references to case studies, formula sheets... These is most common in Business courses.

If material provided it will require a secondary tab.

This information is recorded in the JIRA record as follows:

Part 4- Detailed Exam Info (2): Copy/Paste

A check will only need to be done on non-English language courses. Otherwise select "No".

Part 5: General Course Component Analysis

There are five different setups that need to be checked for. If one is present it is ticked off otherwise field should be changed to No Issues Found (Uncheck Not Evaluated). Each issue is illustrated below.

Parent/Child Tab Setup

Bootstrap Elements

Alternate Format

Alternate format is when a course has content posted in areas other than Moodle. An obvious note will be posted in course typically like the following image:

Hidden Resource Tab(s)

These tabs will have a range of labels (Resources, Quizzes, Discussions) but appear grayed out.

Extra Content up top

Looking for course where there is content that is displayed above tabs.

Description Field

If there are further notes to be made, add them to description field.

If there is existing text "Y, Duplicate" it will mean that exam material is shared with an earlier version of course. Please still fill out Exam information but it can be copied from previous analysis.

Completing Analysis

After filling in fields, move JIRA task to next status as follows:

If there were any Problem Course Components Identified then Click "Future Adjustments Needed" and Unassign.

If there were NO Problem Course Components then Click "Done", review values shown then click Done in bottom. This will close task and remove from this filtered list. Grab next task.

item.dc:creator: tsandhoff
item.content:encoded:
FUTURE CONSIDERATIONS: OLI updates their courses every August. We should confirm if/what changes are made to the courses by the OLFMs and if we should copy the current course or create a new one to have the most up-to-date material. This would also provide a work-around for the copy issue noted below.

OLI COURSE COPY ISSUE: The instructor on the copied course is the first instructor on the alphabetical-by-last-name list which in this case is Sheryl Aselstyne. For copies of courses, either copy a course where "OL Production" is the first last name on the list of instructors or let me know and I can make a copy for your account.

OLI CONTACT: Kim oli-help@andrew.cmu.edu

Both FRAN 1111 and 1211 use an interactive online French textbook developed by Carnegie Mellon University for their Open Learning Initiative (OLI). This textbook is connected directly to the course using Moodle LTI integration that shows up as an External tools activity.

IMPORTANT: New OLI textbooks/courses need to be setup and linked in Moodle each time a FRAN LIVE container is created so that OLFMs and students can access the resource from Moodle.

OLI Textbook/Course Setup

Overview of courses can be seen on https://oli.cmu.edu/ by clicking login and using the following credentials:

username: olproduction

password: 4n$Xb2E8t1!

By clicking 'my courses', up next to settings, you will be able to see all current courses for this account.

To duplicate a course, click 'manage course' on the course you want to duplicate, then choose 'copy section' near the bottom of the tool list. Make sure you change the key to something different (ie just change the last number) so that it is unique. Keep all the other settings the same, and don't enter a password (those passwords fields are if we want the student to enter a password, which we don't).

Moodle LTI/External Tool Setup

To set up a course in a moodle container, add the Coursereview2 as an OLFM Online in the Participants section of the FRAN course.

Sign out and re-sign in with the Coursereview2 credentials (important)

username: Coursereview2

password: StarWars!

Create an external tool and set it up with the Open Learning Initiative preconfigured tool.

Then, making sure you are logged into Coursereview2, click on the tool link. It should take you to the cmu site on a page where it will ask you to either create a new course or connect to one you already have. Use the 2nd option and insert the unique course key, and then input the OLI credentials mentioned above. This will set up that link to point to that OLI course.

Now someone accesses the tool through that specific Moodle container, they will be put into the associated OLI course in the role that their Moodle account has (so OLFMs will be inserted as instructors, and students as students).

item.title: Moodle Container Copies
item.dc:creator: tsandhoff
item.content:encoded:
Production may need to copy DEV or LIVE Moodle containers for various reasons, such as:

  • Course amendments where the changes are minimal
  • Containers for Instructional designer/Subject-Matter Expert review
  • Urgent course container requests from DSA
  • Paced-course container requests

Container Copy Process

To copy a Moodle container:

  1. Navigate to the course container you would like to copy
  2. Click the More tab/dropdown and select the Course resuse option
  3. Click the left-hand dropdown menu (Show Import) and select Copy course
  4. Enter both the course full name and short name (Update version number for amendments if needed). Refer to the Container Naming section in required.
    • DEV to LIVE OR LIVE to LIVE - Input the provided course ID information (e.g. NURS_3643_H04_202335) in BOTH the Course short name and Course ID number fields
  5. Search/Select the course category 
    • DEV to DEV - Same course category as original container (e.g. Open Learning Development/Science)
    • DEV to LIVE - The corresponding OL faculty (e.g. Open Learning Faculty of Science)
    • LIVE to LIVE - Same course category as original container
  6. Add/Remove the Course ID Number if required. No Course ID needed for DEV to DEV copies (e.g. amendments)
    • If we're copying a LIVE paced container for a new semester, add the Course ID number provided
    • If we're copying a LIVE container for review, remove the Course ID number
  7. Click Copy and view once the changes are complete to start the copy process
  8. After the copy is complete, click the link/name of the new container to access
  9. Add users as needed (e.g. standard OL accounts, ID for review, OLFM, etc.)
    • If the request came from DSA Course Management, we can notify them once the container copies are complete and they will add the OLFMs

Other Considerations

DEV to DEV Copies

  • Don't forget to update the version number in the course title and short name when required
  • If the copy is for an amendment, we need to update the course title and container ID number in the D4P amendment section.

DEV to LIVE Copies

  • After the copy is complete, delete the DONOTCOPY tab in the LIVE container if needed.

item.title: Paced-Course Final Exam Checks

****IN PROGRESS***

Each term Production needs to request an exam schedule from the Exams Supervisor (Tdenham@tru.ca) approximately a month and half into a term to review and adjust as needed.

Final Exam Review Checklist

Email Examples

Subject: Request for Summer 2023 Paced Exam Schedule

Hello Tod,
Can we please get a copy of the scheduled dates for the paced and BUSN course for [TERMNAME (e.g. Summer 2023)]? Can you also let us know if there have been any accommodations set up for the [TERMNAME] term in any current courses?

YOURNAME

OL Production Exams has completed the setup of your Final Exam for this term, and we have enabled Moodle notifications. Students will use the following password through ProctorU (please do not share with students):

item.title: Exam Accommodations (Copy & Paste / Splits)
item.dc:creator: tsandhoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS***

Final Exam Split Accommodation

Moodle

New tab, adjusted instructions if necessary on tab, restrictions for tab, within exam - duplication of instructions so they can be modified and then build out two exams that are as even as possible.

  1. Locate the student in Moodle: https://moodle.tru.ca/admin/user.php
  2. Find course link in student profile Course Details section
  3. In the main course settings, check that Course Format/Hidden sections is set to: Hidden sections are completely invisible
  4. Review active exam setup to ensure request split will work as expected, and review instructions in the final exam that reference time/duration as they may need to be adjusted. IMPORTANT NOTE: If instructions within the Final Exam need to be updated due to split/time changes (e.g. This is a 3 hour exam…) we MUST duplicate the specific questions in the setup process and move them to a new category as any changes would affect the active exam. More details below.
  5. Create a new Final Exam (XA) tab if there is not one and hide from students
  6. Duplicate the active exam, hide from students and move to hidden Final Exam (XA) tab
  7. In the duplicated Final Exam activity title, replace the number with "(XA)" or add if needed. Also add -Sitting 1, -Sitting 2, etc. (e.g. Final Exam (XA) - exam password provided by your invigilation service - Sitting 1)
  8. In the Question Bank, create any new categories required for split (e.g. HRMN4831_FormA_XS_JC). "XS" notes exam split and "JC" represents student initials.
  9. Duplicate questions as needed, move to new category and update to match split instructions
  10. Go back to the Final Exam (XA) tab, duplicate the exam for the number of parts required, and adjust the activity title as needed.
  11. For each exam activity:
    • Adjust the time in the settings to match the request
    • In the Questions section, delete the sections and questions not needed and replace any instructions that were adjusted for the split
  12. Review new XA activities and confirm setup and wording matches request
  13. Turn on OLFM attempt submission notifications for each Final Exam activity
  14. Add Restrictions to hide current exam, and show both new tab and activities using student T-ID
  15. Once setup is complete, please send to Production Supervisor for QA
  16. Make QA adjustments (if needed)
  17. Notify the Exams team the split is ready for the student

Examples

PSYC 1111
https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=39628&section=7#tabs-tree-start

PSYC 1211 (Requires more setup as SA questions from one giant pool, so need to duplicate pool then split in half otherwise student could get same questions on each part of exam)
https://moodle.tru.ca/course/view.php?id=46123&section=7#tabs-tree-start

Final Exam Copy and Paste Accommodation

  1. Locate the student in Moodle: https://moodle.tru.ca/admin/user.php
  2. Find course link in student profile Course Details section
  3. In the main course settings, check that Course Format/Hidden sections is set to: Hidden sections are completely invisible
  4. Check current exam Extra Restriction/Browser security settings to see if they are enabled. If it is set to "None", then no further set up is required, we can notify the Exams team to proceed with the current exam and close the task.
    OR
    We may already have a copy and paste exam accommodation set up, and we can use the Add Restrictions to hide current exam, and show both new tab and activity using student T-ID
  5. If a new Exam is needed, create a new Final Exam (XA) tab if there is not one and hide from students
  6. Duplicate the active exam, hide from students and move to hidden Final Exam (XA) tab
  7. In new XA final exam:
    • Turn on OLFM attempt submission notifications for the new Final Exam activity
    • Add Restrictions to hide current exam, and show both new tab and activity using student T-ID
  8. Once setup is complete, please send to Production Supervisor for QA
  9. Make QA adjustments (if needed) and make sure tab and quiz activities are not set to be hidden only restricted based on T-ID.
  10. Notify the Exams team the copy and paste exam is ready for the student

item.title: Updating to Moodle Welcome Page Format
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Updated Moodle packager link information.

Use the following steps to replace the current toggle Course Guide format with the new Welcome content:

  1. Make sure your course XML is up-to-date
  2. Use QuickScript to covert your XML to HTML and create a Moodle backup file using the Moodle Producer: https://olhub.tru.ca/moodle-producer/
  3. Uncheck Add HTML (Quick Links) Block and Add Common Activities
  4. In the Moodle course, delete all the item sunder the Open Learning heading (i.e. Open Learning ORGB 2811 SW7 - Organizational Behaviour)" except for additional resources such as MyLab Student Registration Handout.
  5. In Moodle, use the More > Course reuse option and then use the dropdown menu to select Restore
  6. Upload the backup package you just created and click Restore
  7. On the Destination page, go to Restore into this course and select the Merge the backup course into this course option and click continue
  8. On the Restore settings page, uncheck Include blocks and Include filters and click next
  9. On the Course Settings page, select ONLY the Welcome section and items and remove the checkboxes from all the other sections of the course. Click Next once complete.
  10. On the last Restore settings page confirm settings are correct and that only the Welcome page section and items are going to be imported
  11. Re-upload Suggested Schedule document
  12. Add image banner code above the Open Learning header:
    <p><img class="img-responsive atto_image_button_text-top" role="presentation" src="https://barabus.tru.ca/media/moodle_homepage/TRU-Banner1920-250.jpg" alt="" width="95%" height="250"></p>
  13. Updated tab title from "Course Guide" to "Welcome"
  14. Please dash in course title with colon, e.g. BIOL 2341: Introduction to Genetics

item.title: Submission Instructions Wording for Print Courses
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
For certain print courses the MA form is being removed (based on survey of OLFM's, list provided by Program Delivery). Being on the list is not guarantee 100% removal as if we are providing students will fill-in-the-blank type assignments we will keep forms.

For courses on list, print instructions should be updated to:

As soon as you have completed an assignment, save your document and send it to your Open Learning Faculty Member for marking. Attach your assignment to an email which has your name course and assignment number in the subject line. Alternatively, if you do not have access to email, you can mail a printed copy of your assignment to your Open Learning Faculty Member.

The following courses have been identified for MA form removal. 2nd column indicates status.

Assignment Submission Instructions

As soon as you have completed an assignment, save your document and send it to your Open Learning Faculty Member for marking. Attach your assignment to an email which has your name course and assignment number in the subject line. Alternatively, if you do not have access to email, you can mail a printed copy of your assignment to your Open Learning Faculty Member. Be sure to include your name, the course code, assignment number, and the date of submission on the title page of your assignments, so they can be easily identified, and you can get credit for all your work. Use headers in the body of your written assignments to make sure all components of your assignments are clearly identified (course code, your surname, assignment number, date [day, month, year]).

{In NOTE BOX} Keep a copy of your assignment before sending it to your Open Learning Faculty Member for evaluation so you can refer to your assignment during a telephone or email discussion with your Open Learning Faculty Member. Also, in the unlikely event that your assignment is lost, you will have an extra copy of your work. Many student writing manuals today suggest that students keep copies of all early drafts of their work as well, to protect themselves against mistaken charges of plagiarism.

As soon as you have submitted your assignment, and while waiting for your Open Learning Faculty Member to return it, begin the next module.

When your marked assignment is returned, review your Open Learning Faculty Member’s comments and queries. Take the time to carefully go over the marked assignment. If necessary, reread sections of the textbook or unit commentary that gave you trouble. What lessons can you apply to your next assignment? Phone your Open Learning Faculty Member if you have any questions or problems.

Your Open Learning Faculty Member is responsible for the grade you receive on an assignment. If you disagree with a mark, discuss it with your Open Learning Faculty Member right away. Also, the Open Learning Faculty Member alone decides whether you may or may not rewrite and assignment. You should know, however, that it is not customary to allow revisions of already graded work unless you make a formal appeal. This is why telephone contact with your Open Learning Faculty Member before assignment submission is important—particularly if you are having difficulty.
item.category: Print Course Development & Print Material Formatting

item.title: Comparing Course Container Content
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
In some instances, Production is asked to compare content between Moodle Containers due to changes made directly in the content (often by OLFMs). Smaller chunks of content (a paragraph or two) can easily be compared using online tools such as text-compare.com, but large pieces such as full assignments, modules/units, etc. can be compared with Word using the Compare feature under the Review tab.

Assignments

In order to ensure we're comparing the same formatting/content across Moodle containers, it's often easiest to Copy/Paste assignments directly into Word and use the Compare tool (see video below). Here's the general process:

  1. Copy/paste each DEV assignment, including title to separate documents (e.g. CONV1061_SW1_A1_DEV, CONV1061_SW1_A2_DEV, etc.).
  2. Use Moodle search to locate LIVE Moodle containers for comparison and complete the same copy/paste process as above, but save the documents with the OLFM name. (e.g. CONV1061_SW1_A1_Chevrier). Once we have all the LIVE assignments for comparison, we can start the comparison process.
  3. Open a new document in Word, click the Review tab and select the Compare tool to the right.
  4. Select the Original document (often DEV) and Revised document (often LIVE) you previously saved.
  5. In the Label changes with field, add a useful title or name (e.g. OLFM last) that will be used to highlight all changes between the two documents and click OK.
  6. Word will generate a new document that highlights all the differences between the two files selected as tracked changes.
  7. Save the document with highlighted changes with a new name (e.g. CONV1061_SW1_A1_Chevrier_Changes).
  8. Compile all necessary documents and send out for review.

Course Guide/Modules/Units (Books)

  1. Navigate to the first Course/Book section you want to compare
  2. Click on the item you want to save, select the More dropdown menu and select the Export book to Microsoft Word.
  3. Update document title to help differentiate (SOCI3991_M1_DEV)
  4. Repeat steps above to save addition content to compare
  5. Open a new document in Word, click the Review tab and select the Compare tool to the right
  6. Select the Original document (often DEV) and Revised document (often LIVE) you previously saved
  7. In the Label changes with field, add a useful title or name (e.g. OLFM last) that will be used to highlight all changes between the two documents and click OK
  8. Word will generate a new document that highlights all the differences between the two files selected as tracked changes

Using the Word Compare Tool

Here's a quick video overview on how to use the Compare tool in Microsoft Word.

item.title: Deleting Moodle Containers
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
We're not able to directly delete containers in Moodle, but we can flag them for deletion by a Moodle admin at a later date.

To flag a container for deletion, please make the following changes to the in the container Course settings area:

  1. Course full name - Replace the course title with "TO BE DELETED"
  2. Course short name - Replace Banner information with _DELETE (e.g. ABCD_1234_DELETE)
  3. Course category - Change to "To Be Deleted"
  4. Course visibility - Set to Hide
  5. Course ID number - Delete any banner information

item.title: Importing Quiz Questions to Respondus
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Import Questions from Word to Respondus

  1. After opening Respondus, click Import Questions.
  2. Select the file type. If you do not select the correct file type, your file will not be visible.
  3. Choose the Word file that you formatted for Respondus.
  4. Name using format ABCD1234_SWX_Quiz1 (eg, MDLB1221_SW1_Quiz1).
  5. Check off Use stem... This makes it easier to find and refer to questions in the future.
  6. Use Q1- as the stem for Quiz 1, FE- as stem for Final Exam. Make it logical.
  7. Click Preview. If no errors occur, click Finish to add questions to Respondus. If there are errors, you will need to review the formatting of your Word document and complete the steps again.
    Some possible issues:
    -Question skipped (may be that a question requires a type [essay requires Type: E] that is missing)
    -No answer (may have forgot to put "a." in front of correct answer for essay question)
    -Duplicate question number (may be duplicate numbers in the file [instead of 1, 2, 3, the list shows 1, 2, 2] OR there may be random numbers within questions [image below])

Review Questions in Respondus

  1. Click 'Preview and Publish'.
  2. Click 'Preview the File'.
  3. The 'Preview' window will pop up. Review the questions to make sure there are no issues or errors.
  1. If a formatting issue is found:
    • Click 'Modify Item'.
    • Make correct and save.

item.title: Setting Up Exam Percentages in Gradebook
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added new information for setting up Final Exam calculated grade items in the Gradebook.

Overview

Total exam marks are over what the final exam is worth.  This happens when there are more questions than students are asked to complete. This can cause confusion for OLFMs who may not be aware how quiz activities are set up and the new Calculated Grade item will provide the correct Final Exam total accounting for the additional marks.

Final Exam Example:
Short-Answer Questions (30 marks total)
Choose 3 of the 6 short-answer questions below. (10 marks each)

Students will only be receiving 30 marks on this section, but Moodle will see it as 60 marks. When this happens, we will have to adjust the Gradebook.

Calculated Grade Item Setup

In the container, select the Grades section.  Hit the drop-down under the Grader Report and find Gradebook setup as shown below.

Once you go into the Gradebook set up, you will select Add grade item.

It will take you into New grade item screen.

Under the Grade Item → Item name

I normally name it Final Exam percentage if there is only 1 exam.  If there are multiple exams, match them to their number.  Example, Final Exam 2 percentage; Final Exam 3 percentage.

Nothing else in this section needs to be changed.  I will usually select “Hidden” at this time, then Save changes.

You will see your new Final Exam Percentage title under the Final Exam.  Once you see that, you will be able to edit the Calculation.  Select the drop-down menu on the far right and select Edit calculation.

You will have to assign an ID number, see below: 

Once the ID number has been added, you can copy and paste it up into the Calculation section. The example below (CMNS 3201) shows an exam that is worth 70 marks total, because of the extra questions within the exam, Moodle thinks the exam is worth 105 marks.

Caclulation Example:

  • =([[FinalExamIDNumber]]/DefinedExamMarksTotal)*100
  • =([[Final Exam]]/70)*100

Here is an example where Moodle has the exam worth 170 marks due to the extra questions within the exam but is technically only worth 100 marks.  We set the ID number to match the name of the exam.

Caclulation Example:

  • =([[FinalExamIDNumber]]/DefinedExamMarksTotal)*100
  • =([[Final Exam 2]]/100)*100

Example Courses

Here are some courses that have a Calculated grade item for reference.

  • DEV_OL CMNS 3201_SW1 - Citizen and Consumer Identities in Networked Culture
  • DEV_OL SOCI 4311_SW1.1 - Sociology of the Family: Families in a Multicultural World (2 Calculated grade items)

item.title: WeBWorK Resources
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Created a spot to document various resources and information for WeBWorK DEV testing.

Development Server Access

  • Cert download and information for setting up DEV access - https://matter.tru.ca/open-learning/pl/8mdtf4579bfz38pub5y8b5jmza
  • DEV Server: https://wp6.tru.ca/webwork2
    DEV Server Admin: https://wp6.tru.ca/webwork2/admin

Online Resources

  • Manually configuring Firefox to trust your CA - https://www.techrepublic.com/article/how-to-add-a-trusted-certificate-authority-certificate-to-chrome-and-firefox/#Adding_the_CA_certificates_as_a_Trusted_Root_Authority_to_Firefox
  • Copying a WeBWorK Course (second section) - https://swatkb.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MOODLE/pages/20907042/Copying+a+WeBWorK+Course
  • How to set up Email Instructor feature -https://wiki.ubc.ca/Documentation:WeBWorK/How_to_set_up_Email_Instructor_feature
  • WeBWork Grade Passback - https://webwork.maa.org/wiki/LTI_Authentication_(for_WeBWorK_2.18_or_newer)#Grade_Pass_Back
  • WeBWorK at the University of Regina - https://webwork1.cc.uregina.ca/webwork_instructor_notes.html#webwork-at-the-university-of-regina
  • VCC Using WeBWorK - https://vcc.teamdynamix.com/TDClient/50/Portal/KB/?CategoryID=580
  • Homework Sets Editor (Date and Visibility) - https://webwork.maa.org/wiki/Homework_Sets_Editor#Using_the_Problem_Set_List
  • UBC WeBWorK Student Guide - https://lthub.ubc.ca/guides/webwork-student-guide/

Testing Required (In Progress)

  • Course/copy restore (e.g. DEV to LIVE)
  • Moodle/WeBWorK LTI connection with grades
  • Gradebook setup with WeBWork activities
  • Time between grade passback to between environments

Documentation Required

  • How to copy/restore WeBWorK courses
  • Process and setup required for new LIVE courses
  • How to update email preferences to contact OLFM instead of broadcast email
  • How to set up LTI to WeBWorK course and/or specific activities

General Moodle Setup

  • Copy both current MATH/STAT Moodle courses to Sandbox
  • Confirm LTI setup for activities (I think it has to be directly to the assignment?)
  • Confirm Grading/gradebook setup
  • Test student access (Elysia student account)
  • Using student account test grade transfer and confirm approximate time for grades to display in Moodle

General WeBWorK Setup

  • Emails to the OLFM
  • Dates adjusted (much later in the future?)
  • Assignment visibility
  • Number of attempts per question

Additional Considerations

  • How do we document which courses use WeBWorK for future copies
  • LTI/Assignment URLs will need to be adjusted for each OLFM container when they are copied

WeBWorK Graded Activity Setup

Moodle

  1. Add External tool item
    • Activity Name: Match to course info as needed
    • Preconfigured tool: Automatch, based on tool URL
    • Tool URL: Must link to specific WeBWorK assignment
  2. Privacy: Enable Accept grades from tool if activities are graded
  3. Grade: Adjust to match "Out Of" column in WeBWorK Grades section
  4. Activity completion:
    • If optional, leave as Student can manually mark the activity as completed
    • If graded, adjust to Student must receive a grade to complete this activity
  5. Save the activity
  6. Ignore: Common module setting, Restrict access

WeBWorK Homework Set Dates and Assessment Feedback Considerations

WeBWorK Homework Sets require 3 dates to be defined, which affects the feedback students receive after completing each problem.

This has some implications for continuous enrolment courses:

  • SW courses will need a Close Date set well into the future to ensure students can continue to attempt the assessments
  • The Answer Date can only be set to be the same or later than the Close Date, which can limit the feedback students receive (see more info/potential solution below)
  • For practice exercises, similar to self-tests, we would need to enable feedback per question in the code for SW courses, so student can see what they get correct/incorrect
  • TESTING REQUIRED - Need to confirm if set dates are kept when copying WeBWorK courses (e.g. DEV to LIVE)

Student Homework Set Feedback

Students can receive different activity feedback depending on the Close/Answer Dates and the question code. For example:

Question Solution Section

If provided with the questions, students can only see the "Solution" toggle after the Close Date, which would affect SW courses as we can't set a Close Date.

Question with No Feedback

Student submit each question and receive minimal feedback at the top of the screen.

Question with Partial Feedback

Student submit each question and can see the result (incorrect/correct) for each item in the question. This is defined in the question code and can be enabled/disabled. Some questions have this setup as default, but it seems like a majority do not.

Enabling Partial Feedback

It's possible to enable Partial Feedback in the question code by changing the $showPartialCorrectAnswer option value from 0 (disabled) to 1 (enabled). This would need to be adjusted for each question.
Note: Multiple use of $showPartialCorrectAnswer will override one another. If one occurrence is set to 0 (disabled), the entire question may default to that value. If Partial Feedback does not display, be sure to scan the question code for a second or third instance.

Moodle/WeBWorK Testing

  • Setup Moodle/WeBWorK graded assignment
  • Elysia login with student account
    • Confirm WeBWorK access using External tool
  • Submit WeBWorK assignment, confirm grade passback to Moodle and approximate time for grade to show
  • Once single assignment confirmed working with LTI access and grade passback, setup remaining Moodle/WeBWorK external tools and gradebook book.
  • Elysia complete additional assignments, confirm grade passback and time for

Other Testing Questions

  • What happens if student completes more than 1 assessment, are all grades transferred?
  • What happens if WeBWorK grade is changes, how long to update?
  • What happens if LTI activity grade doesn't match WeBWorK?

item.title: CIS Update Instructions
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
CIS Maintenance Workflow

  1. Using the instructions and details below, update the CIS content in directly in D4P.
  2. On the day that the CIS needs to be shown onlne, export a CIS document from D4P and send to olcisupdates@tru.ca to be uploaded. NOTE: CIS updates can be entered at anytime prior to the upload date, but please do not send the upload request until the document needs to be changed online.
  3. The Learning Environment Development (LED) team will upload the document to the TRU server and send an email confirmation once complete.
  • If there is an urgent request, you can message the LED Supervisor in Teams or Mattermost so they are aware.
  • If you have any questions about the CIS process, formatting, exporting, etc., please contact the LED Supervisor.

Viewing/Accessing the CIS content in D4P

  • Locate the course record in D4P by using the Course Search field or the Course List link located at the top of the page.
  • The Course Information Sheets (CIS) box is found on the right hand side (see image below). Within the box you can:
    • Click the View Posted CIS link to view the currently posted CIS on tru.ca website.
    • Click the Edit Offline Master CIS button to view/edit the current CIS content and generate a file to be uploaded.

Edit Offline Master CIS Screen Overview

Click "Edit Offline Master CIS" button to access the following screen.

  1. Update Comment Field: Enter your standard CIS update comments.
  2. Requested Upload Date: Select the upload date and D4P will finalize the CIS revisions to the database after this date has passed. You can edit the current CIS version until the end of the selected upload date.
  3. Action Buttons: Use the provided buttons to Save your current CIS revisions, Export an XML file to be uploaded, or Preview CIS in a pop-up window. 
  4. Last Updated By: This section provides information regarding who made the last CIS updates and when.
  5. Versions: This section will display the status of the CIS, allow you to download and preview previously finalized versions of the CIS. See the Versions section below for more information.
  6. CIS Content and Editor: This is the main text editing section for making CIS revisions. The top bar provides the formatting options (bold, italics, lists, links, etc.) similar to Word. See the CIS Editing/Formatting Notes below for more information.

CIS Versions

As noted above, you can make edits to the CIS until the end of the Requested Upload Date before it is finalized in the D4P database.

  1. Upload Date: When you click the Save CIS button, a new table row will be generated with the Requested Upload Date information
  2. Status: The Status column will show "In Progress" to indicate that the CIS information is saved and able to be edited up until the end of the Requested Upload Date. After the Requested Upload Date has passed, the CIS document will be logged to the D4P database and Status will be updated to "Finalized"
  3. XML: If the CIS is "Finalized" in D4P, use the Download link to export the CIS into an XML file to your local machine that you will send via email to the LED team to be uploaded.
  4. Preview: Select the View link to preview a draft version of the current CIS information directly in D4P.

CIS Update Steps

Locate the CIS material in D4P that needs to be revised and use the following steps to update and export an XML document to send to the LED team to be uploaded:

  1. Add the document History note to the Update Comment field.
  2. Select the Requested Upload Date. This date can be the current date or future date depending on the requirements.
  3. In the CIS CONTENT editor, add text updates. Note: Always use the browser Paste Without Formatting option when pasting content into the CIS Content Editor and use the editor tools to apply additional formatting e.g bold, italics, links, etc. as needed.
  4. Once the changes are complete, click the Save CIS button. As noted above, you can make edits to the CIS until the end of the Requested Upload Date before it is finalized in the D4P database.
  5. Click on the Preview CIS button to review the changes and confirm the document is correct before exporting the file
  6. Click the Export XML button to generate an XML file to your local machine that can be sent to be uploaded by the LED team.
  7. Email the exported XML files to olcisupdates@tru.ca, the LED team will upload as soon as possible and reply with a confirmation once the upload is complete.

D4P Update Example Videos

Minor CIS Updates (Direct Text Edits)

In many cases, small CIS updates will only require direct text updates made in the CIS Content Editor similar to making changes in Word.

Major CIS Updates (Copy/Pasting with Direct Text Edits)

Larger CIS Updates may require a combination of direct text edits and copy/pasting to capture revisions to larger sections of text. Note: Always use the browser Paste Without Formatting option when pasting content into the CIS Content Editor and use the editor tools to apply additional formatting as needed.
