item.title: Moodle Book Image Banners
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Using Book banner images provided by OL Media, manually add image banners to each module book by using the following steps:

  • A banner will need to be added to the General Description of each Moodle book so that it appears above every page (see https://moodle.tru.ca/mod/book/view.php?id=1601296) for an example of what this looks like in a book)
  • Use the following code to add the banners:
    <h2 class="wlcm-banner" style="padding: 50px 50px; color: #003e51; font-weight: bold; background: url('https://URL_FOR_BANNER_IMAGE_GOES_HERE'); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: right center;">MODULE TITLE GOES HERE</h2>
  • To get the Moodle image URL, upload the image into the description area, switch to HTML view, then copy the image URL into the above code. Make sure to also adjust the Module title to match as well.

item.title: Setting Up Quiz in Moodle
item.dc:creator: haleyfeller
item.content:encoded:
After you have added the quiz questions to Moodle from Respondus, you will need to set up the quiz.

Adding Categories and Pools

Once you get into the course, click More and then Question Bank. Under Select a category, select the quiz question bank that you just added.

Use the Questions dropdown on the top left and select Category. Then create a new category under the master category for your quiz (I called this one Questions, although if I had multiple sections to my quiz, I would make separate categories such as T/F, Multiple Choice, etc.)

After adding categories, go back to Questions. Select the questions you want to move (eg. multiple choice ) and click Move to... Finally, select the category you want the questions to be moved to (eg. MC). You will

Adding Instructions and Final Steps

Your master category should now be empty (questions sorted into various sub categories). You will now add Instructions and Final Steps.

Main Instructions and Category Instructions

Your master Word file should have information for the main instructions and/or category instructions (eg. Part A: Multiple-Choice).

Create a new Description question. Add the information from the master Word document as well as a heading (H3 or Heading (large) for Main Instructions and H4 or Heading (medium) for Category Instructions). Save the changes.

Note: It can be helpful to copy and paste text into Notepad++ to remove extra formatting from Word. You can also use the HTML view.

Final Steps

Create a new description question:

Final Steps (H3 or Heading (large))

After reviewing your answers remember to click "Finish Attempt" and then "Submit all and finish" button to complete quiz. (normal text)

Create Quiz Activity and Complete Quiz Setup

item.title: WeBWorK: Updating Problems/Questions
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Editing a Problem in a Homework Set

  • Click "Hmwk Sets Editor" found on left navigation menu.
  • Select the value (total number of problems in the homework set) found in the "Edit Problems" column for the desired homework set.
  • From here, you are able to view and edit each problem.
  • When editing the contents of a problem, it is important to note that you are directly altering the code. It's a good idea to click "View/Reload" before saving your changes to ensure there are no bugs and that the problem renders properly. Note that edits are saved as a temporary .tmp file.

Saving a Problem

  • Once edits have been made to a Problem's code, click the "Save As" tab and ensure the "Replace current problem" radio button is selected. Be sure to use the following naming convention for the new .pg file:
    • Library/TRU/OL/course code/lesson#/question#.pg
    • If we were planning on using a question as Q1 in Lesson 1.1 of STAT 1201 SW4, we would name the file the following: Library/TRU/OL/STAT1201_SW4/L1_1/01.pg

Common WeBWorK Problem Adjustments

Enabling Problem Feedback

It’s possible to enable Partial Feedback in the question code by changing the $showPartialCorrectAnswer option value from 0 (disabled) to 1 (enabled). This would need to be adjusted for each question. Use the above instructions to save and update the Problem after changing the feedback value.

item.title: Adding OLFM access to Student Emails
item.dc:creator: cteare
item.content:encoded:
As of November 22, 2024 any Moodle shell created between 2020 and now does not allow OLFM's to see student emails when the student profile is viewed. Containers with dates before 2019 have this permission and its loss is unexplained. We are working to restore that functionality and do see if bulk changes can be done but in mean time will address by OLFM request.

Process

  • OLFM contacts internal staff with request (most likely will email Program Delivery but it could show up in fixmycourse).
  • Environment Dev team will adjust/check all of the OLFM's Moodle shells as follows:
    1. Go into Course and Click Participants List
    2. Select Enrolled users drop down
    3. Under Permissions, Select Permissions
    4. In Filter, type email.
    5. The first response should be "Enable/disable email address": Add OLFM Online Permission

item.title: WeBWorK: DEV to LIVE Copy Process and Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS CHECK WITH THOMAS***

Using the following workflow when new courses with WeBWorK are launched/copied in Moodle.

Confirm WeBWorK Copies Required

Review the Moodle container copy communication sent from DSA Course Management to determine which OLFM WeBWorK courses need to be copied and which Moodle containers will need to be adjusted with new WeBWorK links.

Create/Copy the LIVE WeBWorK Courses

Similar to Moodle, the LIVE WeBWorK OLFM courses will be copied from our DEV courses. From the WeBWorK admin interface (https://webwork.tru.ca/webwork2/admin/), create/copy the new OLFM courses:

1. Archive DEV Course

IMPORTANT: DO NOT enable/select the Delete course option on this page.

  1. Navigate to Archive Courses
  2. Select DEV course from list of courses
  3. Click Archive course button
  4. Confirm no errors are flagged in the Database Tables or Directory Structure and click the Archive button

2. Unarchive DEV to LIVE Course

  2. Select DEV course name from list
  3. IMPORTANT: Enable New Name option and update to OLFM container name (e.g. OL_MATH1141_SW3_W2026_Rahmati). Note that a 40 character limit is in place.
  4. Click Unarchive Course button
  5. On the next page, confirm Unarchive Course details and click the Unarchive button

3. Update LIVE Course Title

  2. Select new the LIVE course from list
  3. Enable Change Course Title to option
  4. Insert full course title (e.g. STAT 1201: Introduction to Probability and Statistics (Fall 2022 Sharma)

4. LIVE WeBWorK Course Setup

  • Navigate to new LIVE WeBWorK course from the main WeBWorK course list interface (https://webwork.tru.ca/webwork2)
  • Select the Classlist Editor menu item and delete all users except ADMIN and OLEDEV

  • Manually enrol OLFM(s) and provide access to all question sets

    • Permission Level: professor
    • Generate and set randomized password from bitwarden.com, 10 characters, enable all additional options (e.g. upper/lowercase, numbers, etc.). This will be included in the communication based to DSA Course Management as OLFMs need to log into WeBWorK directly first.

Update WeBWorK/External Tool Links In LIVE Moodle Containers

item.title: Content Support Tasks: Student-facing Content and Exam Requests
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Overview

The Learning Environment and Development teams receives a number of student-facing inquiries, such as course outline/syllabus requests, exam resets, print-on-demand inquires, etc. We do not want to capture student personally identifiable data in Jira and have created a process to "clean" student data from Content Support (OLCONTS) tasks.

What is student personally identifiable data:

  • First/last name
  • Student Number
  • Email address
  • Any other information that can indentify the student

Note: You must include the Jira task number in the email subject (e.g. [OLCONTS-123]) in your replies when bccing the content support emails to ensure your communication in captured on the task in Jira.

Content Support Task Workflow (Contains Student Data)

If the original communication contains student data:

  • Email is sent to olcontentsupport@tru.ca or olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca.
  • Jira creates task, and add a note with summary content support task workflow at the top of the description.
  • Remove any student information (T-ID, Name, etc.) from the task title.
  • Review the task description for any student information and delete (be sure to check the entire description, especially if an email chain has been sent).
    OR
    Replace the task description with a brief summary of the request in the email (e.g. Student course outline request for ABCD 1234.) as we can go back to the original email for more information.
  • Once the student data has been removed, in the right-hand sidebar, select the Action dropdown and choose the Remove Student Data (History) item to clone the task, which will remove any remaining student info in the task history. This will also delete the current task.
  • Refresh the current page, it will reload and you should see a message that you do are not able to access the task to indicate the current task has been deleted from Jira.
  • Review your Jira notifications to locate the cloned/new task.
  • Update the Contains Student Data field to Yes (removed)
  • Complete the task as needed and ensure you include the new task number (e.g. OLCONTS-###) in the email subject to capture your outgoing communication as a comment and any replies.

Content Support Task Workflow (No Student Data)

If there is no student data in original communication:

  1. No additional data clean-up steps are required if there is no student data included in the task.
  2. Complete the task as needed and ensure you include the new task number (e.g. OLCONTS-292) in the email subject to capture your outgoing communication as a comment and any replies.

item.title: Calculated Quiz Questions
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Calculated questions offer a way to create and display variables based on a range of values, so that each student receives different variations of a question.

Due to the complexity of the question formatting and settings, calculated questions are often setup directly Moodle.

Calculated Question General Setup

  • Add a new Calculated question in Moodle and input a name
  • Copy/paste the question content into the Question text field, adjust formatting as needed
  • In the question text, replace all [ ] brackets with { } throughout to identify the variables/wildcards
  • Copy/paste the Incorrect Feedback to the General Feedback field

Calculated Question Answer Setup

  • Copy/paste the provided formula into the Answer formula field
  • Remove commas from large numbers
  • Similar to above, put curly brackets {} around the variables (e.g. {x}, {y})
  • If wildcard multiplication is required, place in brackets with multiplication symbol (e.g. 0.5{y} to (0.5*{y})
  • Set grade to 100%
  • Adjust the Tolerance ± field to match the Answer Range details
  • Note, you may need to delete and retype the math symbols in the formula field if Moodle is generating an error when you click save
  • Once there are no issues, you'll be moved to the Choose wildcards dataset properties page.

Choose Wildcards Dataset Properties

  • Confirm you are seeing the expected wildcards from the question
  • No changes required for the Mandatory wild cards present in answers
  • For the Possible wild cards present only in the question text, select will use a new private dataset from dropdown
  • No changes for the Synchronise the data section
  • Click Next page once changes are complete

Edit the wildcards datasets

  • Double check we have all the required wildcards
  • For each wildcard
    • Set the Wild card value to a number within the range
    • Set the Range of Values based on the information provided
    • Set the decimal places to match the question formatting
    • No changes to Distribution unless specified

Answers tolerance parameters

  • Click the show more link to expand
  • Review the equation to see if we're getting generally the expected result

Add

  • For Next 'Item to Add' set to forceregeneration of all wildcards
  • Click Get new 'Item to Add' now button
  • For Add item, select the number specified in the Number of Answer Sets or round up if needed and click the Add button
  • The new wildcard sets will display below
  • Once complete, click the Save changes button

item.title: OER Conversion Workflow - OpenStax / Pressbooks / Word
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS***

Summary of Taki's work on ASTR OpenStax Word document to Pressbooks process

  • I did a quick scan of the HTML files and everything looks ok, however, it is tough to say without seeing it rendered in Pressbooks (especially Latex).
  • Note that some changes have been made to the material in OpenStax since the docx files were pulled. Images, resources and wording may differ. I have checked with Thomas, who advised to work with what we have. It would be impossible to keep our material up to date.
  • Ensure there are no direct internal links to the OS text. Thomas had mentioned that redirects through OS are ok. These are typically found in the “Link to Learning” sections.
  • Formatting to check:
    • Bolding.
    • Consistent note box colour coding.
    • Images need to be added manually.
      • Be sure to copy alt text from OS and add it to the image in PB.
      • Copy/paste figure captions from the body and add them to the image.
    • After pulling material from OS, footnotes were added within the material. I did my best to flag these via comments found in docx files located in the “CompiledDocs_ConvertedLatex” folder.
    • Ensure Latex has properly rendered.
      • Snippets of the equations have been included in the “Images” folder for reference.
  • Refer to Chapters 1-3 for examples of formatting and layout. Those styles are not concrete, so you may have better ideas.
  • Chapter 7 had issues during conversion. Be sure to pay attention to the images, formatting and heading levels.
  • If you need to convert a docx file to html via Pandoc, see the instructions below:
    • Convert .docx to .md
      • pandoc -f docx -t markdown Chapter1Word.docx -o Chapter1MD.markdown
    • Convert .markdown (.md) to .html
      • pandoc Chapter1MD.markdown --wrap=none -f markdown -t html -s -o Chapter1HTML.html
    • If TeX warnings pop up, identify which equations are flagging. Re-create in MathJax and convert them to LaTeX, including “$latex “ and “$” at the beginning and end of each Latex code.
    • Open HTML file in browser.
    • Copy <body> element in HTML.
    • Paste into Pressbook.

Below is a summary of the folders found in the main Pre-Production directory:

  • CompiledDocs_ConvertedLatex
    • docx files that have been compiled, formatted and have equations converted to Latex.
    • You probably won’t use these files too much, but I did flag footnotes.
  • CourseMaterial
    • Individual and compiled files of the course material taken from OS.
  • HTML_From_Pandoc
    • Converted html files you will work with.
    • Open in a browser, copy the <body> tag via console and paste the HTML into PB.
  • Images
    • A collection of all the images used in the course, divided by chapter.
    • I also included Latex snippets for reference.
  • Pandoc_conv
    • Files I used to convert from docx to markdown to html via Pandoc.

item.title: WeBWorK: Adjusting Number of Attempts for Homework Sets and Quizzes
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
We can set the number of attempts in both Homework Sets and Quizzes, but the process is different for each type of activity.

Homework Set Problems

  • In the WeBWorK course, select the Homework Set to update
  • In the left-hand menu, select the Homework Set title under the Hmwk Sets Editor option
  • Scroll down to the Problems section
  • For each Problem, update the Max Attempts field to the required number
  • Scroll to the bottom of the page and select the Save Changes button

Quizzes

  • In the WeBWorK course, select the Quiz to update
  • In the left-hand menu, select the Quiz title under the Hmwk Sets Editor option
  • Under Set Parameters>Test Parameters, update the Graded Submissions per Version to number of allowed attempts
  • Scroll to the bottom of the page and select the Save Changes button

item.title: Final Exams Online Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Online Formatting

Not all exams are suitable for online. Check instructions to students and answers. If diagrams are required or special formatting it may not be possible. Discussion with ID/OLFM may be required to resolve. (See Online Course With Paper Exam below). Unless specifically designed to be one form or have clearance from SME then DO NOT combine forms. They will be setup as individual forms.

  • Try to pull as much content up with Respondus by Creating a copy of the file then adjusting to proper format.

NOTE: There are Word Macros that will substantially speed up processing of multiple choice questions. If you are not familiar with tools please talk to someone has used.

  • Alternate method to get content up is to first copy and paste into text document and then add to Moodle (this will strip excess Word formatting)
  • Some question types will require a direct build in Moodle (anything that in not one of the basic question types: Multiple choice, T/F, Essay, Short Answer). Note: Respondus does allow you to build more complex questions.
  • If course is not ready then put questions in a formatting container then move over to actual Moodle container using Export Moodle XML once the container is stable (check with EST about container status)
  • To bulk fix known issues - upload via respondus, export xml from Moodle, use Oxygen to format (GRID or Text view), import xml back into moodle.

Pooled Forms

  1. Create a copy of original file to develop as online document. Keep original
  2. Prep document so like questions are together and questions of same value are together. Remove all headings and instructions.
  3. Once ready pull exam or as much as possible into Respondus and setup for uploading to Moodle and generating paper copies.
    • Using Respondus to setup Quizzes
  4. Upload content into Moodle and build exam - see instructions below
  5. Generate at least 2 word documents for paper copies (select different randomization routines on output - it will always randomize questions in same way each time letter is picked eg. an A randomization will be consistent.
    • Output documents will need standard print formatting.

Individual Forms

If it not possible to have pooled exam questions use individual categories for blocks of questions for use of random blocks.

Moodle Setup - Behind the scenes:

Create category name that indicates exam (Form A, Pooled etc)

  • Create sub-category names that reflect type of question and also value if possible (Where possible build categories to have equal value)
  • Long Essay - to be answered in Moodle as too many issues when Word used.
  • Create a descriptive question that lays out exam structure and describes any important information, repeats materials - see proctor U folder for starting template
  • Create descriptive question for any section that has instructions
  • Create a descriptive question called Final Steps question to ensure last question saved. - see proctor U folder for starting template

If a course has a final exam which can be setup up for Proctor U invigilation the following steps must be done:

  1. Setup of Final Exam Tab - set to hidden, until all material is setup fully (Done by EST)
  2. Adjust Final Exam information in the Course Guide - see below. (Done by EST)
  3. Add same text information to Final Exam tab (Done by EST)
  4. Create final exam (Done by ELO)

Moodle Container - Standard Wording

Examples of general text to be displayed on tab and initial and final question text can be found in the ProctorU_wording.xml file.

This can be found in: https://olsvnapp01olpd.tru.ca/svn/production/trunk/Courses/ProctorU

Screen Shots of a Sample Setup

Quiz Activity Setup

  • Naming of activity: Final Exam - exam password provided by ProctorU - if multiple exams need to indicate by number (don't put in form letter)
  • Description field, should be set visible to page and have Materials Permitted listed (paper and online must match) Formatting: Materials Permitted (small heading), Materials themselves - regular paragraph with bold, for no materials state None. (example below)
  • Submission - open attempts submitted automatically
  • Attempts - 1
  • Review options - none
  • Decimals in grade should be 2 (will allow for quarter marks)
  • Restrictions:
    • Password: Copied from previous course version when possible. If new exam, generate password from bitwarden.com, 16 characters, enable all additional options (e.g. upper/lowercase, numbers, etc.)
    • Browser security: If students are not required to open resources in a new tab (e.g case studies, formular sheets, etc.), enable the Full screen popup/JavaScript security option.
  • Completion tracking - none

Final Exam Description Example:

Final Exam Description Code - UPDATE MATERIALS INFO AS NEEDED:

<h5>Materials Permitted:</h5>
<ul>
  <li>UPDATE TO MATCH INFORMATION PROVIDED</li>
</ul>
<h5>Materials Provided:</h5>
<ul>
  <li>UPDATE TO MATCH INFORMATION PROVIDED</li>
</ul>
<h4><strong>If you encounter technical issues during your exam:</strong></h4>
<ol>
  <li>You must notify ProctorU immediately so that they can assist you in
    resolving the issue.</li>
  <li>If you are unable to resolve the issue with ProctorU, you must let <a
      href="mailto:exams@tru.ca">exams@tru.ca</a> know right away.</li>
</ol>
<div class="noteCaution"><strong>PLEASE DO NOT </strong>submit any exam
  questions or files via email to your Open Learning Faculty Member. Exam
  questions <strong>MUST</strong> be submitted inside the final exam in Moodle.
  Any emailed work <strong>WILL NOT</strong> be graded</div>

Quiz Activity Question Build

  • 1st question should be the descriptor question with general instructions - setup on its own page with its own heading
  • For each type of question use headings to help guide students
  • Use descriptive questions at start of sections to help guide students when necessary
  • Use random blocks or shuffle to make exams unique
  • last questions - Final Steps - reminds students to Save and Submit exam, also forces save in system
  • if exam contains essay questions, we need to provide clear instructions to students to move to different page to save.

Quiz Tool Notifications

For Graded Assessments (Quizzes/Midterms/Exams) the OLFM's will need to be notified when a student submits - especially in a continuous enrollment course.

Moodle does not have a simple front-facing setting to turn-on quiz submission notification, it must be done by modifying tool permission. Each tool needs to be individually changed.

Visual Step by Step to Adjust Quiz Tool Notification

Online Course With ONLY Paper Exam

If an online course has a final exam that can only completed in paper/written format, the Course Guide can still direct students to the Final Exam tab with some additional information. Remove any ProctorU details and replace with the following wording in the Final Exam tab:

The Exam for this course will be a paper exam that will need to be taken prior to your course completion date and at an approved testing location.  You will be responsible for any associated fees.

Please contact exams@tru.ca a minimum of one month prior to when you would like to take the exam.  They will help you determine options in your area and guide you on how to schedule your exam.

item.title: Final Exams Print Setup
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent Updates:
****UPDATES IN PROGRESS***
- Added section on Final Exam document naming
- Add note and information about using standing OL Word/Print formatting

Final Exam Print Formatting Overview

IMPORTANT: Final Exams will now use our standard OL Word/Print formatting and styles for Final Exam documents (e.g margins, headings, text size, etc.). Please review the Word/Print Formatting information and apply the OL Styles template when working on Final Exams.

Method 1: From Previous Exam/Answer Key

  1. It is usually (not always) easier and quicker to format the answer key first.
  2. Open a previous version of an answer key, modify it to the course that it pertains to (course acronym, course title, form letter) do a "save as" and rename it (i.e., ECON1221_A_ak_09SEPT14.doc).
  3. Copy and paste in the proper information. It is easier to format if it is pasted in as "unformatted" text.
  4. Once the answer key is formatted and complete, do a "save as" and this time save it out as the exam (i.e., ECON1221_A_ex_09SEPT14.doc).
  5. Next, go into an older final exam then copy and paste the cover page into the new final exam. At this time, change the course acronym, course title, and form letter of the cover page. Make sure the headers are changed, as well.
  6. Be sure to remove all answers from the exam. Remove bold and asterisk from multiple-choice question. Be sure to remove any written answers from short-answer or essay questions.

Method 2: From Scratch

  • In some cases the final exam documents provided need to be formatted from scratch. Use the Word/Print Formatting information and apply the OL Styles template when creating a new Final Exam document. More exam-specific information below.

Method 3: From Moodle

  • If we need to create a randomized paper exam from an LMS pooled exam, please reach out to the Production Supervisor for the best approach based on the exam setup.

Final Exam Document Naming

Final exam document names should match the following:

  • No spaces, use underscores
  • Course acronym and number: PSYC3451
  • Version(s):
    • SW5 OR
    • SW5_SW6 for multiple versions (see more details below)
  • Form Letter - H
  • Type:
    • FE - Final Exam
    • FEAK - Final Exam Answer Key
    • PE - Practice Exam
    • PEAK - Practice Exam Answer Key
  • Date signed off - DAYMONTHYEAR, 10JUN26

Document Naming Examples:

  • PSYC3451_SW5_H_FE_10JUN26
  • PSYC3451_SW5_H_FEAK_10JUN26
  • PSYC3451_SW5_PE_10JUN26
  • PSYC3451_SW5_PEAK_10JUN26

For final exam items that may cover one to three versions:

  • PSYC3451_SW4_SW5_H_FE_10JUN26
  • PSYC3451_SW4_SW5_H_FEAK_10JUN26

For final exam items that cover four or more versions, we can use a dash to indicate multiple versions:

  • PSYC3451_SW4-SW10_H_FE_10JUN26
  • PSYC3451_SW4-SW10_H_FEAK_10JUN26

Formatting Final Exam Paper Forms

  • Apply OL styles
  • Format margins, headings and text, etc. to match standard OL Word/Print Formatting
  • Title pages can be inserted/replaced after formatting complete
  • See additional notes below

Header/Footers

  • No header/footer on first page
  • Header: ABCD: ####: Final Exam - Form X → Page # of #
    • Example: HRMN 4841: Final Exam - Form E → Page 2 of 12
  • Footer (centred): TRU Open Learning

Headings

  • Body of exam should have headings properly styled (visible on left side Navigation bar)
  • Headings should be used for main section breaks such as Instructions, Part 1, Part 2, etc.
  • Main heading levels should start at H2 and continue with H3, H4, etc. at needed

Question Numbering

  • Use the built-in Numbering/Bullet list and/or headings where applicable for structuring exam questions (Select option that is most effecient)
  • You may need to adjust added spacing when students are required to add their answers directly to the exam

Final Exam Title Page

Insert/replace after document formatting is complete.

Table that will need the following updated:

  • Course Code
  • Course title
  • Form Letter updated
  • Time Allowed
  • Total pages
  • Total Marks
  • Materials Permitted
  • Materials Provided
  • Instructions below table need to be tweaked to reflect what is listed

Examples of Materials Permitted

  • None
  • Ruler, pens, pencils, and erasers
  • A scientific, non-programmable calculator

Examples of Materials Provided

  • None
  • Formula sheets
  • Two sheets of extra working paper (Update number to match requirements)
  • Two exam answer booklets (Update number to match requirements)

Example Instructions:

Answers directly in exam document

  • Write all your answers in the spaces provided on the exam paper.

Answers is exam booklet

  • Unless otherwise indicated, write all your answers in the exam answer booklets provided.
  • When you have finished, return all papers, including the exam and the exam answer booklets, in the envelope. Failure to do so may result in a FAIL grade.

Formatting Final Exam Paper Answer Keys

Please use standard OL Word/Print Formatting similar to the Final Exam with additional notes below.

Header/Footers

  • No header/footer on first page
  • Header: ABCD: ####: Answer Key - Form X → Page # of #
    • Example: HRMN 4841: Answer Key - Form E → Page 2 of 12
  • Footer (centred): TRU Open Learning

Answers

  • Use bold to indicate/highlight the correct answer

Final Exam Answer Key Title Page

Insert/replace after document formatting is complete.

  • Course code
  • Course title
  • Form letter

Final Exam Example Documents

Final Exam Example: Question Heading Numbering

Final Exam Example: Question List Numbering

Final Exam Anwer Key Example

Final Exam Templates

Final Exam Title Page

item.title: Final Exam Internal and External Reviews
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Similar to the course content, Final Exams go through an Internal Review and External Review process before sign-off.

Internal Review

Once the final exams and keys have been formatted, then it is time to send them to EST assigned with Internal Review of the course.

EST should be checking for formatting issues, question errors (especially online) and overall settings for online. Best Practice is to check both as student and higher level system user.

  • Online Assessments Internal Review Process
  • Paper Exam Forms Internal Review Process

Steps necessary before sending to Internal Review

  1. Fully Setup Assessment using Correct Settings/Layout - in correct Location
    1. Make sure information in description box is complete (what students see before test starts)
    2. Make sure timing/review options are correct
    3. Make sure layout is useful to students - the longer the assessment the more important the use of Headings and descriptor questions
      1. Quiz/Self-Test - may not have any headings
      2. Midterm - Instructions question at start with heading - outlining exam setup, Final Steps section at end, use headers in between to show different areas of exam
      3. Final Exam - Instructions question at start with heading - outlining exam setup, Final Steps section at end, use headers in between to show different areas of exam
  2. Setup a version of questions on "Do not Copy" tab
    1. Make sure built so any pools used are obvious - use headings and page breaks - don't make just one unstructured dump
    2. If many Self-test/short quizzes - can all go in one check quiz but use Headings to provide guidance to reviewer
    3. Make sure settings are: unlimited time/attempts plus all review items are checked for "Immediately" and "Later"
    4. For Final exams - password can be added
  3. Make sure review copy of questions are available
    1. Quizzes/Self-tests - in Temp folder in subversion
    2. Final Exam - in Examrepo folder for course \working\for IR

External Review (Final Sign-off)

After any changes recommended by Internal Review have been done, then exams are ready to be sent for External Review

  • New/Major revision courses should have exams (print/online) sent to ID for review, unless they want you to send directly to SME
  • Maintenance revision should have exams sent to OLFM who did work
  • Amendments will often go to Curriculum Services, depending on the changes or they may go directly to the OLFM

Example External Review Communication (Paper and Online)

Please log External Review communications on the course Final Exam task.

Note:
- Remove reference to paper exams if not required
- Adjust wording (remove DO NOT COPY details) for instances where changes were made to LIVE containers (e.g. Paced course amendments or new exam material in LIVE containers).

Subject: ABCD 1234 SW1 - Final Exam Ready for External Review [PROD-12345]

Hello,

Please find attached the paper-based final exam for ***COURSE NAME AND NUMBER*** and the online information in order to do a final review and sign off.

Online information:
***LINK TO FINAL EXAM TAB***
Password: ***FINAL EXAM PASSWORD***
Please do not give password out to students.

You will see two tabs, the Final Exam tab and the DO NOT COPY tab. The one named Final Exam contains the exam the students will be receiving, and the DO NOT COPY tab is for ease of question review only.

Let me know if you have any corrections, or if they can be signed-off. Thank you.

item.title: Final Exam Sign Off and Upload
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
D4P Sign-off Steps

For course exams (online and paper):

  • Adjust the Exam Status to Active
  • Set the Exam Progress to Waiting for upload

Moodle Sign-off Steps

  • If more than one exam, please ensure only first exam is visible, hide all other exams from students
  • Make sure DO NO COPY tab is set to be hidden
  • Confirm Exam quiz activities have OLFM notifications enabled

Papar Forms Sign-off Steps

Uploading Paper Forms

Important: Make sure any attachments have been added into the final PDF file (i.e., readings, periodic tables, formula sheets, etc.)

  1. Once final sign-off has been received and the exams and keys are okay to go, then they get put in a "waiting to upload" status. They do not get uploaded to the Printshop folder until a final email has been received from DSA Course Management letting us know the course has been launched.
  2. When we receive notification of the course being launched, the final exams are saved out as a PDF file into a folder called "Printshop Exams" located in O:\Open Learning Share\Printshop Exams.
  3. The answer keys are also saved as a PDF file, then saved into a folder called "Final_Exam_answerKeys_PDF" located in O:\Open Learning Share\Final_Exam_answerKeys_PDF

Exam Sign-off Communication

After course sign-off, we'll receive a notification from DSA Course Management that the new course session is opening and that containers have been copied. Tod/Exams will reply asking us to confirm the Exam details, such as:

  • Does the course still have a final exam
  • Were there any changes to the exam such as time, materials permitted/provided, password or paper exams

After we have confirmed the exam details, updated the D4P exams records and uploaded the paper forms (see above) we can reply to Exams request. There’s an example communication in the Final Exam Communications section.

item.title: Final Exams General Overview
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
UNDER DEVELOPMENT

JIRA Tracking/Email

Course Development

Tracked in Jira PROD project using the Exam subtask and Exams Communication subtask under the main course task. Use the olenvironmentdev@tru.ca shared inbox/email for course related exams communications. See more information and examplse in the Final Exam Communications section. All steps of exam formatting process should be tracked through JIRA with Workflow changes and comments

Exams Support

Tracked in the Jira OLCONTS project as Content Support - Exams tasks. Use the olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca shared inbox/email for exams content support realted communications. See more information and examplse in the Final Exam Communications sectiom.

Note: If communicaiton sent to personal email, forward request to the corresponding shared inbox in order for a JIRA task to be assigned.

Exam Material Storage

As of August 15, 2025 Exams material will start to be brought into Subverion for storage.

Subversion Storage:

Here is the typical Exam folder structure in Subversion

Exams

  • Content - The Content/Version folder holds the current "working" files for active exams, similar to standard course content.
    • SW#
    • SW#
  • Forms - Completed/signed-off documents are moved Forms folder
    • Active - Holds the current active exam documents
    • Obsolete - Holds exam documents that have been remove and are not longer valid

Network Storage:

Most of the current exam material is located on the O: drive network share: O:drive: O:\Open Learning Share\Final Exams and Keys\examrepo

Final signed off version of material should be at highest course direct level but MAY NOT be. Use D4P2 to ensure that any material grabbed in the correct version. Newest material may be under a directory called Working.
and

  • If exam is requested to be pulled by Exams Department, put Word, PDF's into "Pulled" subfolder within versioned folder. Make sure to remove copies in exams folders.

Exam Forms Naming & Documenting

Naming

Paper Based Forms Only

  • If Exam is designated as no change and only has minor typos then no form letter change is required.
  • Form letter will be next available letter up to Letter Y (Letter Z is reserved for challenge exams). The form letter that is given on received files is MOST OFTEN not the letter that is assigned.
  • Include the version number in the file name to help make it unique.
  • Dates should only be attached to paper exams on upload, while working on and waiting for signoff there should be NO Date in file name.

Online/Paper - Set forms

  • Form letter will be next available letter up to Letter Y (Letter Z is reserved for challenge exams). In Moodle the Exam should be numbered on the front end. For example, Form A and Form B are being used. Setup in Moodle should have (1) and (2) showing to students with Form letters only provided in categories in back end.
  • Paper and Online exam form should match so it is clear that content is the same.

Online/Paper - Pool based

  • Online
  • Creating a Paper from online exam: Choice 1 - build out from Respondus. This requires that exam is setup properly in respondus. (note Randmization as RND Form Letter in D4P and on form header) OR Choice 2 - export a randomized attempt. This produces a PDF that will need adjusting (leave as PDF). Note: Print formatting does not need to be exact if just creating a PDF version of online exam.

Exam Documentation

  1. JIRA:
    • For courses that are part of typical curriculum development cycle (New/Major/Maintenance/Amendment), exam task should have a record that is linked to production course task. **This includes courses with no exam or change in exam.
    • Stand alone exam material will not have a link to production task.
    • Classification of Exam task will reflect either D4P2 (curriculum development) OR whatever is appropriate for exam.
  2. D4P2: will maintain the accuracy of the D4P information & JIRA

Material Processing

Overall Process

Starting JAN 2020, exam material process and production material process has been integrated.

Course material and the relevant exam material are more integrated as the result of online assessments. The following image shows general workflow for curriculum development work.

Data Tracking and Formatting are being done separately.

  • The Exams Liaison Officer is tracking all exam related material and doing formatting of midterms/exams.
  • The E-Learning Support Technicians are tracking and formatting all other course documentation.
    At the internal review stage the two processes combine.
    The E-Learning Support Technician who is doing an internal review of course material should also be reviewing all exam material (paper and online) at the same time. Each Internal Review is tracked separately in JIRA so two tasks are generated. The ELO will need to assign the Internal Review sub-task to EST. ELO keeps the main task on their list. The Internal Review from Exams goes back to Exams Liaison Officer position.

Integration between the two workflows is being accomplished by a JIRA task coming from Production Project called Exam Status (sub-task).

  1. EST will assign this production sub-task to ELO when they start of formatting course material. This lets the ELO know that course formatting is beginning and allows ELO to inform EST about type of exam material to come - paper only; paper & practice PDF; paper, practice PDF & Online versions. The ELO should respond back (assign back to EST) as soon as possible to allow correct structures to be built.
  2. EST will assign same sub-task back to ELO when the course material is ready for internal review, the EST doing Internal Review should be listed on sub-task. ELO will send back with confirmation that exam material is ready for internal review. ELO will then assign their JIRA Exam project IR sub-task to designated person.
  3. EST will assign task back when course is about to go to External Review. ELO will provide any passwords required for online material back to EST using same task.
    1. The External review can either be separate or together depending on what type of development cycle work as follows:
      1. Maintenance: Course Material to Naomi, online exam to Naomi first, paper exam to OLFM, once online material looked at by Naomi then OLFM put into container to look over. EST will have to let ELO know when online material can be sent to OLFM (basically at signoff)
      2. Major: Course Material to ID, online and paper to ID.
      3. New: Course Material to ID, online and paper to ID.

Process for Non-regular Final Assessment material

With advent of COVID-19 there has been a push to get more final assessments online. Courses have either had a proctorU exam added or an alternate assessment added to allow students to complete a course. These updates to courses are completely independent to course updates. This material has a different workflow process.

  1. In JIRA, Special Online Assessments are classified as "Online Exam" - green cloud with up arrow symbol
    1. Components to add: "COVID-19", Faculty course belongs to and either "Alt Assessment" or "ProctorU"
    2. Summary should clearly state Course Code/master number - whether Alt Assessment or Final Exam in ProctorU -if there is a relevant Form letter it should be added
    3. JIRA workflow is Queue, In Progress, Internal Review, External Review/Sign off, Waiting for Upload/, Uploaded

Note: Unlike regular workflow the main JIRA tasks gets moved between team members AND Internal Review AND External Review both have changes done by person reviewing. Waiting for Upload to Uploaded needs to be coordinated with either gap in ProctorU exams or with Exams group.

Exam Status Requests

Production E-Learning Support Technicians will be assigning an Exam Status sub-task from production process

  • Response should be sent back as soon as possible as it indicates start of formatting process
  • If require a response back for inserting material - please indicate
  • Responses back will come when production material is ready for internal review and should be dealt with right away

Exam File Requests

Final exam requests will come from Instructional Designers and Curriculum Services.

  • All exam requests should be sent to csexams@tru.ca, where a JIRA task will be assigned.
  • Check D4P for most current version, cross check against master spread sheet provided by Tod until confirmed all data records up to date.

Special Need Exams

Special Need Exam requests will come from the Exams Supervisor. The request will specify the special accommodation needed for the final exam (i.e., extended time, split into two sittings, enlarged font, etc.)
When modifications are complete, a final review will need to be made. Sometimes there are "suggested times" listed throughout the exam that will no longer be applicable, so a final review is crucial.
Once satisfied with the modification, print out the exam(s) and deliver to the Exams Supervisor.

Challenge Exams

Challenge exam requests will come from the PLAR Department. They will go through the same process as a final exam, except they will always be given the form letter "Z". They are also uploaded as a pdf file to the Printshop Folder.

item.title: Final Exam Reset Requests
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
NOTE: We're in the process of changing this workflow and instructions will change in the future.

The Exams team sends requests to olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca and Jira sorts them in to the OL Content Support Project as an Exams Support Request.

Form-based/Non-pooled Exams

Here are the steps for completing a student final exam request in Moodle:

  1. Locate student in Moodle using their ID number: https://moodle.tru.ca/admin/user.php
  2. Find the required course link in Course Details section of their Moodle profile and go to Final Exam section
  3. Locate the Moodle exam activity where the student completed their original attempt
  4. Once confirmed, add restrictions to hide current exam in settings using Restrict access and student ID number (ensure activity is hidden if students don't match the criteria)
  5. Go to other exam activity and add restrictions to show current exam in settings using Restrict access and student ID number (ensure activity is hidden if students don't match the criteria)
  6. On the Final Exam tab, double check visibility based on restriction logic and ID numbers
  7. Remove student data from Jira task, update task fields as needed and log time
  8. Reply back to the Exams team, noting the student has been given access to a new exam version (see example below). Be sure to include task number in email subject to capture communication.

Example communication:
The student has been given access to a new exam version in FULLCONTAINERNAME. Thank you.

Pooled Exams

In some instances, the Exam team will ask us to confirm if an exam is pooled (randomized from question bank(s).

Here are the steps to confirm if exam is pooled.

  1. Locate student in Moodle using their ID number: https://moodle.tru.ca/admin/user.php
  2. Find the required course link in Course Details section of their Moodle profile and go to Final Exam section
  3. Locate the Moodle exam activity where the student completed their original attempt. Often for pooled exams there may only be one.
  4. Select the Final Exam quiz activity and go to the Questions section
  5. In the Questions section, you can see if the questions are selected from a pool or if you just see the questions. In some cases there is a mix of pooled/non-pooled questions that well note in the communication back to exams. (E.g. there are 25 pooled multiple choice questions and 3 non-pooled essay questions).

item.title: TinyMCE XML QA/Toggle Moodle Fix
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
The TinyMCE editor is removing the required JavaScript link information needed for our XML QA and Toggle tags to work when the content is saved. The current solution is to use the Atto Editor if you are working on Moodle content that uses the QA or Toggle tag, and Sean is looking at solutions to resolve the issue moving forward.

If you come across a broken QA or Toggle link, you can switch to the Atto editor and add the required JavaScript code directly to the content.

NOTE: You must update the JavaScript code to match the unique identifier included in the "a id=" tag information for it to work correctly.

Here are some examples:

QA

Missing code:
<p><a id="aLink_cg_d0e105_1"></a>Show Answer</p>

Correct code:
<p><a id="aLink_cg_d0e105_1" href="javascript:showhide('aLink_cg_d0e105_1','answer_cg_d0e105_1','Show Answer','Hide Answer');">Show Answer</a></p>

Example code fix:
<p><a id="aLink_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER" href="javascript:showhide('aLink_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER','answer_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER','Show Answer','Hide Answer');">Show Answer</a></p>

Toggle

Missing code:
<p><a id="togLink_400000000184"></a>Show</p>

Correct code:
<p><a id="togLink_400000000184" href="javascript:showhide('togLink_400000000184','toggle_400000000184','Show','Hide');">Show</a></p>

Example code fix:
<p><a id="togLink_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER" href="javascript:showhide('togLink_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER','toggle_UNIQUEINDENTIFIER','Show','Hide');">Show</a></p>

item.title: Final Exam Communications
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Recent updates:
- Added information about external links to the New Session\Exams Details Reply (after Course Sign-off) example communication
- New section under development to provide more information on Final Exam communications

Overview

E-Learning Support Technicians need to communicate with the other teams involved with Final Exams, including Curriculum Service, Exams and PLAR. Different task types may require responses from different emails as described below

Course Final Exam Development

This includes Maintenance/Major/New Revisions and Amendments going through the curriculum development process. Communications may include internal comments on Exam subtask (e.g. Internal Review) and external emails for items such as questions and the External Review process.

All course-related final exam emails should come from the olenvironmentdev@tru.ca email address, so if replies come back in, they get captured by JIRA. Best Practice is to copy & paste message into JIRA or BCC to olenvironmentdev@tru.ca with JIRA PROD number in subject line, so communication gets captured as part of main task.

Final Exam Content Support

This includes support tasks such as exam resets, corrections, accessibility request and PLAR challenges exams.

All exam support related emails should come from the olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca email address, so if replies come back in, they get captured by JIRA. Best Practice is to copy & paste message into JIRA or BCC to olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca with JIRA OLCONTS number in subject line, so communication gets captured as part of main task.

The following summarizes types of communication and who should receive.

Example Communications:

Course Final Exam Development

Final Exam communications regarding course development should be sent from olenvironmentdev@tru.ca.

Start of work

Now integrated with course start of work communication. See course communication examples.

Internal Review

Details added to Exams Jira task and assigned to EST for Internal Review

Quality Assurance

Final Exam notes/questions can be included on the QA task assigned to the Production Supervisor

External Review

Now integrated with course External Review communication. See course communication examples.

New Session\Exams Details Reply (after Course Sign-off)

Hello Tod,

XXXX XXXX SW# has both an online exam and a paper exam with the following details:

Online

  • Time limit:
  • Materials Permitted:
  • Materials Provided:
  • [IF APPLICABLE] External Resources: Students will need to open additional resources in a new browser tab
  • Password:

Paper

  • Written Form X
  • Written Form X

The new exams do not apply to the previous version. [EST NOTE: This is most often the case, but may apply to previous versions, especially for amendments] Please let me know if you need any additional information. Thank you.

Final Exam Content Support

Exams Content Questions

This communication can be dynamic depending on the task and various factors involved. Our main goal is to provide as much course information and details as possible to make it easier for them to provide the information we require. Our communication should contain much of the following information below as needed:

  • Course acronym, number and version (e.g. BIOL 2341 SW2)
  • Who initiated the request (e.g. OLFM(s), Instructional Designer, etc. - include names)
  • Other affected stakeholders (OLFMs, other OL teams, etc.)
  • Brief summary of request details (include original email that generated the task, if applicable)
  • Include screenshots, copy/pasted text, documents, etc., if that helps provided additional context for the request
  • If LIVE assessments are involved, provide the full name of affected containers and the number of students who have completed the assessment for each one
  • Provide any other relevant information

PLAR Challenge Exam Sign-off

(Logged on main Jira work item)

Sent from: olexamcontentsupport@tru.ca

Sent to: plar@tru.ca and tdenham@tru.ca

Subject: ABCD 1234 SW# - Challenge Exam Reviewed and Sign-off

Hello,

The ABCD 1234 SW# challenge exam setup and review is complete in the PLAR container.

There are no changes to Proctor U information and the password matches the current Moodle course (EST NOTE: If there is no matching course in Moodle, we can provide the new password.)

OR

The challenge exam has the following updated information: (e.g. Different time, materials permitted/provided, password, etc.)

Let us know if you need any additional information.

Thank you,
EST NAME

item.title: Final Exam, Practice Exam and Midterm Corrections
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
***IN PROGRESS, CHECK WITH PRODUCTION SUPERVISOR IF YOU HAVE ANY QUESTIONS***

Final Exam Corrections:

  • Confirm affected course version and exam versions (online paper forms) in D4P exam records
  • Determine if correction will impact exam setup (materials change, question/total exam mark change, structure change, etc.). If so, please check with Production Supervisor before proceeding. If not, continue.
  • Apply corrections across all current DEV, LIVE courses and paper forms/answer keys
  • Any updated Paper form and Answer Key documents need to be PDFed and uploaded to O: drive when applicable.
    • Updated Paper Form Exam PDF to: O:\Open Learning Share\Printshop Exams
    • Updated Paper From Exam Answer Key PDF to: O:\Open Learning Share\Final_Exam_answerKeys_PDF
  • Notify OLFM(s) after changes are complete.

Midterm Corrections:

  • In progress - affected by what review options students receive.

Practice Exams:

  • Since these activities are not graded, we can often update as needed, without additional follow-up
  • Ensure changes are made across all active courses and documents

item.title: Working with .emf Image Files
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
It's common to find .emf image files in CHEM courses that have images of chemical structures and formulas. They are created using ChemDraw and can not be saved using the right-click/save process used for standard images. Here are a couple workflows to manage these types of images.

Screenshot Images

If there are a minimal amount of images that can't be exported using the right-click/save method, we can use SnagIt to capture the images for the course content. Note, you may need to make the image larger in the Word document.

Use Inkscape to Convert .emf Files

Important: Adobe Illustrator is known to cause graphics to shift when .emf files are opened.

If the course has a lot of .emf type images we can use Inkscape, a free and open-source software vector graphics editor to open save images.

Basic Open/Save Processing with Inkscape

  • Download and install Inkscape
  • Change the Word document .docx extension to .zip
  • Extract the "word/media" folder that containers all the images in the document
  • Use Inkscape to open, resize and save images as .jpg or .png as required

Command Line Processing with Inkscape

Inkscape offers command line access for basic image conversion and resizing. The following command will covert an .emf file to .png and rescale 8x which works well for many smaller images.

inkscape INPUTFILENAME.emf --export-filename=OUTPUTFILENAME.png --export-dpi=768

Adding Inkscape to System PATH Environment Variable

This process allows you to run Inkscape from any directory in your command line.

Windows:

  • Search for "Environment Variables" in the Windows search bar and select "Edit the system environment variables."
  • In the System Properties window, click on "Environment Variables."
  • Under "System variables," find and select the "Path" variable, then click "Edit."
  • Click "New" and add the full path to your Inkscape installation directory. This is typically something like `C:\Program Files\Inkscape\` or `C:\Program Files\Inkscape\bin\` (depending on your installation and version).
  • Click "OK" on all open windows to save the changes.

Important: Close and reopen your command prompt or PowerShell window for the changes to take effect.

Batch Processing with Inkscape

***IN PROGRESS***

In the folder with .emf files:

  • Hold down the 'Shift' key, right-click in the folder, and select "Open PowerShell window here".
  • Paste the following script to convert .emf to .png into PowerShell and hit enter
# Get all .emf files in the current directory
Get-ChildItem -Filter "*.emf" | ForEach-Object {
    $inputFile = $_.FullName
    $outputFile = $_.FullName -replace '\.emf$', '.png'
    
    # Run Inkscape conversion
    inkscape $inputFile --export-filename=$outputFile --export-dpi=768
    
    Write-Host "Converted: $($_.Name)"
}
  • If you want to convert to .jpg instead of .png, just change .png to .jpg in the script.

item.title: Text/Media Bootstrap Element Toggle Fix to close
item.dc:creator: cteare
item.content:encoded:
When editing a Text/Media Box with collapsible Bootstrap Elements the code may change to permanent "Show" causing the section to be open when you get to that page.

Two spots need to be adjusted to change this back to proper behavior of a default Collapse state these are bolded in text below (note code shown is the correct code):

<h4 class="panel-title"><a class="accordion-toggle collapsed"
        href="#t-assessments" data-toggle="collapse" aria-expanded="false"><i
          class="fa "></i>Assessments</a></h4>
  </div>
  <div id="t-assessments" class="panel-collapse collapse">

For the first instance, aria-expanded, it will be changed to "show" but need changed to "false"

For the second instance, div tag, an extra word "show" gets included after the "collapse" and must be removed.

item.title: Moodle Tracking Project Overview
item.dc:creator: cteare
item.content:encoded:
The Moodle Shell Tracking (MST) is our inventory of Moodle shells. It is designed to track both existence of Moodle shells as well as status of any work done on them.

All shells should have an entry: DEV and LIVE

The Project has very simple structure with DEV shells being a main task and LIVE shells being sub-tasks of the LIVE shell.

Data entries should occur at two points:

  1. On build out of DEV shell. Once a shell has been created in Moodle a record can be created in the project.
  2. On creation of Live shells. Sub-task entries can be added under the appropriate DEV shell.

Main JIRA Dashboard for the Project is: Moodle Shell Tracking

As of December 2025, the project is setup to track a number of major container adjustments. Once all adjustments are done the workflow will be simplified.

DEV Shell Record Creation

The field definitions required on record creation are:

DEV Shell Full Record

Beyond the above fields, once created the DEV record has the following field which may/may not be used.

Live Shell Record Creation (Active Moodle Shell Subtask)

Find Master shell and create subtask by:

Create New Active Moodle Shell Subtask

Summary: Create new subtask, fill in fields

  • Go to the Moodle Shells Sorted: Dev-Live Filter and search for course.
  • Select the primary DEV Moodle Shell work item
  • Create a subtask
  • Add/update LIVE Shell Records as noted in the table below
  • Update the following fields/info for new shell task
    • Enrollment Status - Active for new copy
    • Course ID Number - From Jira task/LIVE course shell

Clone/Copy Active Moodle Shell Subtask

Summary: Clone existing subtask and edit

  • Go to the Moodle Shells Sorted: Dev-Live Filter and search for course.
  • Select the most recent LIVE version copy subtask and clone task
  • Update the following fields/info for new shell task
    • Enrollment Status - Active for new copy
    • Course ID Number - From Jira task/LIVE course shell
  • Remove clone link

Once the task/record(s) have been added to the Moodle Tracking Project in Jira, add the MST component to the LIVE container check task and close the work item.

LIVE Shell Records

Live Shell Full Record (Active Moodle Shell Subtask)

Workflow

The basic workflow is:

Task Creation -> To Do -> Active Course -> On Archived List -> Archived Off Server

Until all maintenance projects are done the task will go through the following workflow:

Task Creation -> To Do-> Academic Integrity Queue -> Help Available Link Block Queue then either
a. Exam Working Queue ->Exam Setup Adjustment Queue -> Library Links-> Active Course
OR
b. Library Links Queue -> Active Course

Each status has a tick box in the container updates field. A course should not go to active until that field in filled in.

item.title: Video/Audio Submission Quiz Questions
item.dc:creator: cteare
item.content:encoded:
Students can record Audio/Video submissions as part of a quiz question response.

Key Points:

  • The response is limited to 2 minutes.
  • Material will show up in My Media area after submission.

Question type to use: Essay Question

Settings:

Response Format: HTML editor with file picker

Require Text: Text input is optional

Input box size: can be smaller for audio but for video leave 10 lines so it looks like it displays correctly

Allow Attachments (IMPORTANT!): must be at least 1

Require Attachments: Attachments are optional

IMPORTANT NOTES THAT MUST BE INCLUDED FOR STUDENTS:

  • Audio/Video tool will allow you to record and then give you prompt to Attach Recording. Recording will not be included unless that step is done.
  • Recordings must be completed and attached before quiz end time or else they will not be included.

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

item.title: Test
item.dc:creator: nsingular
item.content:encoded:
Sensors indicate no shuttle or other ships in this sector. According to coordinates, we have travelled 7,000 light years and are located near the system J-25. Tractor beam released, sir. Force field maintaining our hull integrity. Damage report? Sections 27, 28 and 29 on decks four, five and six destroyed. Without our shields, at this range it is probable a photon detonation could destroy the Enterprise.

Communication is not possible. The shuttle has no power. Using the gravitational pull of a star to slingshot back in time? We are going to Starbase Montgomery for Engineering consultations prompted by minor read-out anomalies. Probes have recorded unusual levels of geological activity in all five planetary systems. Assemble a team. Look at records of the Drema quadrant. Would these scans detect artificial transmissions as well as natural signals?

We're acquainted with the wormhole phenomenon, but this… Is a remarkable piece of bio-electronic engineering by which I see much of the EM spectrum ranging from heat and infrared through radio waves, et cetera, and forgive me if I've said and listened to this a thousand times. This planet's interior heat provides an abundance of geothermal energy. We need to neutralize the homing signal.

item.title: Moodle Quiz Settings
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Quiz Settings Overview

OL Production requires the following quiz setting information to correctly set up quizzes in the Moodle environment.

  • Name - This is what the student sees as a link to the quiz in their Moodle course
  • Description/Instructions - Brief quiz overview/instructions for students
  • Time limit - How long the student has to complete the quiz
  • Number of attempts - How many times a student can attempt the quiz
  • Review options - Controls what the students can see after completing the quiz

Quiz Review Options

These quiz review settings control what information students will be shown when they review their past attempts at the quiz and are set on a per-quiz basis.

We can control what students see Immediately after the attempt (means within 2 minutes of the student clicking "submit all and finish") and Later, while the quiz is still open (means after 2 minutes).

We do have an additional After the quiz is closed option that can be used for online-paced courses. Since the After the quiz is closed option is data/time-specific it needs to be set by the Open Learning Faculty Member.

  • The attempt - Will show how the student responded to each question.
  • Whether correct - Displays whether the student's response to each question is correct or incorrect.
  • Marks - Reveals the marks awarded to the student and the grade for the quiz.
  • Specific feedback - Will show the feedback for the response to the answer as set when adding the question to the quiz. Each response to a question can have feedback for both correct and incorrect answers. Also allows Open Learning Faculty Member to provide feedback after quiz attempt.
  • General feedback - Displays the general feedback for the whole question as set when adding the question to the quiz. You can use the general feedback to give students some background to what knowledge the question was testing.
  • Right answer - Reveals the correct answer to each question, whether the student answered correctly or not
  • Overall feedback - Displays feedback for the entire quiz as set in the quiz settings

Example Standard Assessed Quiz Settings

Standard Assessed Quiz

Name: Quiz 1 (20%)

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of Modules A, B, and C, complete Quiz 1. It is worth 20% of your grade. You will have 50 minutes and one attempt to complete this quiz. Be sure to be prepared and give yourself enough uninterrupted time to answer the questions all at one time.

Time limit: 50 minutes

Number of attempts: 1

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if included in quiz material or if the OLFM wants to provide additional feedback)

Health-Science Assessed Quiz

There are stricter settings for Health-Science sector quizzes. This would include MDLB, RESP, NURS, HLTH courses. The students are NOT allowed to see the correct answer, however, for these courses it is typical that feedback is provided.

Name: Quiz 1 (20%)

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of Modules A, B, and C, complete Quiz 1. It is worth 20% of your grade. You will have 50 minutes and one attempt to complete this quiz. Be sure to be prepared and give yourself enough uninterrupted time to answer the questions all at one time.

Note: The mark you received for each question and general feedback for incorrect answers will be available immediately after you have submitted the quiz for 2 minutes only (feedback will have tan/yellow highlight). We recommend you review and look up the correct answers after the quiz and in preparation for the final exam. After 2 minutes, only the grade will be available.

Time limit: 50 minutes

Number of attempts: 1

Review options:

Immediately after the attempt (available for 2 minutes):

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if included in quiz material or if the OLFM wants to provide additional feedback)

Later, while the quiz is still open (after 2 minutes)

  • Marks

Self-test Quiz

Name: Module A Self-test

Description/Instructions: Complete this self-test to check your understanding of key concepts. The self-tests are not graded, and they do not count towards your final grade.

Time limit: unlimited

Number of attempts: unlimited

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if provided)
  • General feedback (if provided)
  • Right answer
  • Overall feedback (if provided)

Practice Exam

Name: Practice Exam

Description/Instructions: After a thorough review of all course materials, complete the practice exam under exam conditions; i.e., give yourself three hours and do not refer to your textbook or notes for help. Once complete, check your practice exam answers provided and consult your Open Learning Faculty Member if you need assistance or have any questions.

Time limit: Should match Final Exam time limit

Number of attempts: unlimited

Review options: Immediately after the attempt AND Later, while the quiz is still open

  • The attempt
  • Whether correct
  • Marks
  • Specific feedback (if provided)
  • General feedback (if provided)
  • Right answer
  • Overall feedback (if provided)

item.title: Instructional Designer FAQs
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
What should I include in the course files?

  • Quiz settings included in course material
  • YouTube video embed flagged
  • Flag external resources that require/have Copyright clearance
  • Over commenting (flagging every single item) not required - we would need to discuss what those items are

What shouldn't be included in the course files?

Can we maybe have the sidebar comments that have been resolved removed from the course documents? While it's expected that everything has been resolved when it's gotten to Production I have sometimes followed up on a tracked comment that wasn't resolved, but then it makes me paranoid that every time I see comments they aren't resolved, and I'm following up on things that are unnecessary.

Who creates the OLFM Guide if there isn't on included in the Course Files?

  • IDs/Editors create the OLFM documents. Production will compile the assignment only if we’re not provided any additional material. - https://editors.trubox.ca/standardized-open-learning-faculty-member-guide/
  • If Production doesn't receive and OLFM Guide with the course files we'll follow up with the Editor and cc the ID.

What is D4P and who updates the course status?

  • IDs update the D4P course status so that the information shows up on our Production reports

How do I make images more accessible?

Image ALT tags can be used to provide accessible text desciptions to images.
