item.title: CIS Update Instructions
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
CIS Update Workflow

  1. Using the instructions and details below, update the CIS material in directly in D4P.
  2. On the specific date the update is required, export a CIS document from D4P and send to olcisupdates@tru.ca to be uploaded. NOTE: CIS updates can be entered at anytime prior to the upload date, but please do not send the upload request until the document needs to be changed online.
  3. The Learning Environment Development (LED) team will upload the document to the TRU server and send an email confirmation once complete.
  4. If there is an urgent request, you can message the LED Supervisor in Teams or Mattermost so they are aware.
  5. If you have any questions about the CIS process, formatting, exporting, etc., please contact the LED Supervisor.

Viewing/Accessing the CIS content in D4P

  • Locate the course record in D4P by using the Course Search field or the Course List link located at the top of the page.
  • On the right-hand side in the Course Information Sheets (CIS) box, you can:
    • Click the View Posted CIS link to view the active document on tru.ca.
    • Click the Edit Offline Master CIS button to view/edit the current CIS content and generate a file to be uploaded.

CIS Editing Screen Overview

  1. Update Comment Field: Enter your standard CIS update comments.
  2. Requested Upload Date: Select the upload date and D4P will finalize the CIS revisions to the database after this date has passed. You can edit the current CIS version until the end of the selected upload date.
  3. Action Buttons: Use the provided buttons to Save your current CIS revisions, Export an XML file to be uploaded, or Preview CIS in a pop-up window. 
  4. Last Updated By: This section provides information regarding who made the last CIS updates and when.
  5. Versions: This section will display the status of the CIS, allow you to download and preview previously finalized versions of the CIS. See the Versions section below for more information.
  6. CIS Content and Editor: This is the main text editing section for making CIS revisions. The top bar provides the formatting options (bold, italics, lists, links, etc.) similar to Word. See the CIS Editing/Formatting Notes below for more information.

CIS Editing/Formatting Notes

▶ IMPORTANT: When copy/pasting text into the CIS Content Section, it's recommended that you paste "Plain Text" using the Ctrl + Shift + V keyboard shortcut, as additional "hidden" Word formatting may be included and cause formatting issues. If your web browser does not support the Plain Text keyboard shortcut, you can right-click in the area you want to add your content and select the "Paste as plain text" or "Paste without formatting option".

▶ Add/reapply any formatting (bullets, bold, italics, subscript, etc.) using the buttons at the top of the editor section.

▶ If a section of the CIS is not required, leave the heading in place and the section below blank. (NOTE: Do not change/remove default headings)

▶ The CIS version content can be edited, saved and exported until the end of requested upload date before a final version will be captured in the D4P database. Once it is finalized in the database, you can only export the XML and view using the links in the Versions section.

CIS Update Steps:

  1. Add the document History note to the Update Comment field.
  2. Select the Requested Upload Date. This date can be the current date or future date depending on the requirements.
  3. In the CIS CONTENT editor, add text updates using the editor options to apply various formatting including bold, italics, links, etc. (Important: See the notes about copy/pasting above)
  4. Once the changes are complete, click the Save CIS button. As noted above, you can make edits to the CIS until the end of the Requested Upload Date before it is finalized in the D4P database.
  5. Click on the Preview CIS button to review the changes and confirm the document is correct before exporting the file
  6. Click the Export XML button to generate an XML file to be uploaded by the LED team.
  7. Send the exported XML files to olcisupdates@tru.ca, the LED team will upload as soon as possible and reply with a confirmation once the upload is complete.

Versions

As noted above, you can make edits to the CIS until the end of the Requested Upload Date before it is finalized in the D4P database.

  1. Upload Date: When you click the Save CIS button, a new table row will be generated with the Requested Upload Date information
  2. Status: The Status column will show "In Progress" to indicate that the CIS information is saved and able to be edited up until the end of the Requested Upload Date. After the Requested Upload Date has passed, the CIS document will be logged to the D4P database and Status will be updated to "Finalized"
  3. XML: Use the Download link to export the CIS into an XML file that will be sent to the LED team to be uploaded.
  4. Preview: Select the View link to preview a draft version of the current CIS information.

item.title: Quiz Formatting Guide
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Required Quiz Details

  • Description/Instructions
  • Time limit
  • Number of attempts
  • Review options
  • Questions bank/pool information

Question Formatting Guidelines and Examples

  • Questions should be numbered
  • Answers in bold
  • Additional feedback can be identified with @ symbol

Multiple Choice Questions

1. Who determined the exact speed of light?

@ No. The correct answer is Albert Michelson, who won the 1907 Nobel Prize for Physics for determining the exact speed of light.

    a. Albert Einstein

    *b. Albert Michelson

    c. Thomas Edison

    d. Guglielmo Marconi

item.title: Respondus
item.dc:creator: hasslethishoff
item.content:encoded:
Word‑to‑Respondus Converter (DOCX): Knowledge / Other Settings

Last updated: January 27, 2026 This page defines the canonical rules and behaviors the agent must follow to convert .docx (and optionally .rtf/.txt) exam files into a Respondus‑compliant .docx. The rules reflect Respondus’ Standard Format and our local policy choices: keep existing “Title:” lines if valid; convert end‑of‑file answer keys to inline asterisks and remove the key; otherwise validate and flag—do not auto‑fix.

3.1 Canonical Respondus rules (must enforce)

  1. Question opener: Each question begins with a number followed by a period . or closing parenthesis ), and a space (e.g., 3) or 3.). The stem follows on the same line. Questions should be in numeric sequence. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)[4](https://dls.cna.nl.ca/teach/pdf/Standard_Format_for_Importing_Questions_to_Respondus.pdf)
  2. Options (MC/MA/T‑F): Each option begins with a letter A–T followed by . or ) and a space, one option per line. [5](https://www.tamucc.edu/dlai/assets/guides/respondus-4-standard-question-formats.pdf)
  3. Correct answer (inline): Mark the correct choice by placing an asterisk * immediately before the option label with no space (e.g., *b) or *b.). [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  4. True/False recognition: List True (or T) before False (or F), otherwise Respondus imports the item as multiple choice. [6](https://uwaterloo.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CELISKB/pages/29177547829/How%20to%20Format%20and%20Import%20a%20Word%20Document%20to%20RespondUs)[2](https://kb.uconn.edu/space/TL/26024247323/Formatting%20Word%20Documents%20for%20Respondus)
  5. Question types in scope: MC, T/F, Essay, Fill‑in (F), Fill‑in Multiple Blanks (FMB), Multiple Answer (MA), Matching (MT). Use a Type: line when required, e.g. Type: E | F | FMB | MA | MT. [2](https://kb.uconn.edu/space/TL/26024247323/Formatting%20Word%20Documents%20for%20Respondus)
  6. Matching format: Each pair uses exactly one equals sign: a) Prompt = Match. [4](https://dls.cna.nl.ca/teach/pdf/Standard_Format_for_Importing_Questions_to_Respondus.pdf)
  7. General feedback: Place between the stem and the first option using ~ for correct feedback and @ for incorrect feedback; per‑option @ lines are permitted immediately under an option. [7](https://ecampus.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2442/2020/03/Respondus-Standard-Format-for-Importing-MC-and-TF-Questions.pdf)
  8. Titles: A Title: line above the question is optional. If absent, Respondus uses the first 20 characters of the stem as the title at import. (Our policy: keep existing titles if correct; do not add new ones.) [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  9. Embedded content: Keep images, tables, and equations embedded in the Word file—Respondus imports them when using the Word (DOCX) importer. [3](https://web.respondus.com/tech-tip-importing-word-files-with-respondus-4-0/)

3.2 Validation checks (flag unless noted)

  • Non‑standard openers (missing number, delimiter, or required space). [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  • Skipped or duplicate numbering (e.g., 1, 2, 4…), which can cause import errors. [4](https://dls.cna.nl.ca/teach/pdf/Standard_Format_for_Importing_Questions_to_Respondus.pdf)
  • Auto‑numbering/bulleted lists detected (Word lists can prevent inline * from working); flag for manual correction. [8](https://und.edu/academics/ttada/_files/_docs/respondus/formatting_guide_respondus-remediated.pdf)
  • Option label problems (labels not A–T, missing delimiter or space). [5](https://www.tamucc.edu/dlai/assets/guides/respondus-4-standard-question-formats.pdf)
  • Missing correct answer (no inline * and no end‑key provided). Respondus would otherwise default to A and warn. [5](https://www.tamucc.edu/dlai/assets/guides/respondus-4-standard-question-formats.pdf)
  • T/F out of order (False listed before True). [6](https://uwaterloo.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CELISKB/pages/29177547829/How%20to%20Format%20and%20Import%20a%20Word%20Document%20to%20RespondUs)[2](https://kb.uconn.edu/space/TL/26024247323/Formatting%20Word%20Documents%20for%20Respondus)
  • Matching pairs malformed (no = or multiple =). [4](https://dls.cna.nl.ca/teach/pdf/Standard_Format_for_Importing_Questions_to_Respondus.pdf)
  • Feedback in the wrong location (general ~/@ not between stem and first option). [7](https://ecampus.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2442/2020/03/Respondus-Standard-Format-for-Importing-MC-and-TF-Questions.pdf)
  • Titles/Points policy: Keep if present; flag for review (we don’t add or remove by default; Points: #.# is supported by Respondus but we leave scoring to Respondus). [9](https://support.cci.drexel.edu/bb-learn/bb-learn-basics/tests/respondus/respondus-40-campus-wide-test-import-microsoft-word-tool/respondus-40-campus-wide-microsoft-word-file-format-and-example-file/)

3.3 Output conventions (house style)

  • Correctness source of truth: Inline * before the option label. Final output must use inline only. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  • Titles: Keep Title: if correctly provided; otherwise omit and let Respondus generate from the stem. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  • No points added: If Points: exists in the source, preserve and flag; otherwise leave scoring to Respondus after import. [9](https://support.cci.drexel.edu/bb-learn/bb-learn-basics/tests/respondus/respondus-40-campus-wide-test-import-microsoft-word-tool/respondus-40-campus-wide-microsoft-word-file-format-and-example-file/)
  • Preserve embedded Word objects (images/tables/equations). [3](https://web.respondus.com/tech-tip-importing-word-files-with-respondus-4-0/)

3.4 Authorized conversion: end‑of‑file Answers: key → inline *

  1. Detect a terminal Answers: block and parse subsequent lines (e.g., A, 1. B, or multi‑answer A, C, D) until EOF. Any text after the answer list is ignored by Respondus. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  2. For each question, apply inline * markers to the corresponding option(s). If inline marks already exist and conflict with the key, trust the key, update inline marks accordingly, and record the change in the validation report. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  3. Remove the Answers: block from the output to avoid duplication/ambiguity. [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)

3.5 Regex helpers (for agent parsing)

QUESTION_OPEN:   ^\s*(\d+)[\.\)]\s+(.+)$
OPTION_LINE:     ^\s*([A-Ta-t])[\.\)]\s+(.+)$
INLINE_CORRECT:  ^\s*\*([A-Ta-t][\.\)])\s+(.+)$
TYPE_LINE:       ^\s*Type:\s*(E|F|FMB|MA|MT)\s*$
TITLE_LINE:      ^\s*Title:\s+(.+)$
TF_TRUE:         ^\s*[Aa][\.\)]\s*(True|T)\s*$
TF_FALSE:        ^\s*[Bb][\.\)]\s*(False|F)\s*$
MATCHING_PAIR:   ^\s*[A-Ta-t][\.\)]\s+[^=]+=[^=]+$
FEEDBACK_OK:     ^\s*~\s+.+$
FEEDBACK_BAD:    ^\s*@\s+.+$
ANSWERS_BLOCK:   ^\s*Answers:\s*$
ANSWERS_LINE:    ^\s*(\d+\.\s*)?([A-Ta-t](\s*,\s*[A-Ta-t])*)\s*$

3.6 Validation report (CSV schema & example)

Columns: QuestionNumber, TypeDetected, Issues, Severity, Suggestion, LocationHint, ActionTaken 
QuestionNumber,TypeDetected,Issues,Severity,Suggestion,LocationHint,ActionTaken
2,TF,"True/False listed as 'False' first",Error,"List 'True' before 'False' so Respondus recognizes T/F","line 45",None
7,MC,"Missing inline * on any option",Warning,"Add *b) (for example) to mark the correct answer","line 128",None
10,MT,"Matching pair missing '='",Error,"Use 'a) Term = Match' with a single '='","line 201",None
14,MC,"End-of-file Answers: key detected",Info,"Inline asterisks preferred; key removed after conversion","EOF lines 350-370","Converted key to inline *; removed key"
15,MC,"Inline * conflicted with key",Warning,"Verify intended correct answer","line 402","Replaced inline * to match key"

3.7 Import into Respondus (for reference)

In Respondus 4.0: Start → Import Questions → Type: “Microsoft Word 2007 [DOCX]” → Browse → Preview → Finish → Publish to Moodle. [3](https://web.respondus.com/tech-tip-importing-word-files-with-respondus-4-0/)

References

  • Respondus: “Tech Tip: Importing Word Files with Respondus 4.0” – images/tables/equations and import steps. https://web.respondus.com/tech-tip-importing-word-files-with-respondus-4-0/ [3](https://web.respondus.com/tech-tip-importing-word-files-with-respondus-4-0/)
  • Standard Format (Multiple Choice, True/False, titles, inline *, Answers: keys). University of Wyoming PDF mirror: https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf [1](https://www.uwyo.edu/lms/wyocourses/improved/respondustabsfolder/exam_formatting.pdf)
  • Question type codes & formatting (E, F, FMB, MA, MT; T/F order). UConn Knowledge Base: https://kb.uconn.edu/space/TL/26024247323/Formatting%20Word%20Documents%20for%20Respondus [2](https://kb.uconn.edu/space/TL/26024247323/Formatting%20Word%20Documents%20for%20Respondus)
  • Additional Standard Format guide (feedback markers, answers list details). UConn eCampus PDF: https://ecampus.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2442/2020/03/Respondus-Standard-Format-for-Importing-MC-and-TF-Questions.pdf [7](https://ecampus.uconn.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2442/2020/03/Respondus-Standard-Format-for-Importing-MC-and-TF-Questions.pdf)
